    Does the disclosed backlog support the Street's FY27 margin step, or only the plan's?

    GEV: does the disclosed backlog support the FY26→FY27 margin step the Street needs? Research note, 2026-09-30

    What we asked

    Read F01_final_synthesis.md and R01_redteam_final.md first (list_overnight_outputs / read_overnight_output; file names end in .md), then whatever else you need. Everything you produce is research input: facts, numbers, formulae and sources only, never memo prose. Apply the two-citation rule to every number. Where a figure is your own calculation, show the formula and mark it [computed]. "Not disclosed" and "could not find" are valid answers. Do not repeat work that an earlier output already did well: cite it and go further.

    THE QUESTION THIS TASK SETTLES: does GEV's own disclosed backlog support the FY26 -> FY27 margin step that consensus needs, or only the smaller step on management's straight-line path to the 2028 framework?

    Known so far (verify, do not assume): - Consensus FY27 adj EBITDA is $9,574M (MarketScreener) or $9,339M (FactSet, as displayed by Boursorama, dated 2026-09-28/30) on about $52.7-52.9B revenue. Consensus FY26 is $6,359M / $6,394M. - The research base is $8,744M from a FY26 base of $6,185M (D01_fy27_build_A.md section 4: Power 20.5%, Electrification 20.5%, Wind 0, corporate -475). So the FY26 -> FY27 EBITDA bridge is +$2,559M in the research base against +$2,945M to +$3,215M on the Street. The whole thesis lives in that $386-656M. - Management discloses the change in equipment "margin in backlog": company +5 pts in 2024 and +6 pts / about $8B in 2025; Power +11 pts in 2025 and +17 pts since YE22 from an "approximately breakeven" start; the 2026 change "at least $8B" and larger than 2025. - The RPO note gives the conversion schedule: equipment RPO $64,245M at 12/31/25 (37 / 69 / 97% within 1 / 2 / 5 years) and $87,821M at 6/30/26 (36 / 65 / 97%). Segment equipment RPO is in the MD&A. - The vintage model (research files; src/vintage_model.py) gives the order-vintage shares of 2027 equipment revenue: pre-2025 8-20%, 2025 vintage 47-62%, 2026-or-later 29-35%; Power-only pre-2025 6-16%.

    Build the mechanism: FY27 equipment margin = sum over order vintages of (share of FY27 equipment revenue x that vintage's margin), for the company and for Power separately, and compare the implied FY26 -> FY27 change with what the research base and the Street each need. State every assumption, give low / base / high, and show formulae a person can redo on paper.

    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    Everything here is research input. Any range is a research estimate, and the team picks its own numbers. I have written no memo prose and chosen no forecasts.

    Short answer. On GEV's own backlog numbers and management's own statements about timing, the order book supports roughly a straight-line step to the 2028 plan. That is slightly below the research base. It does not support the Street's step. To reach the Street, 2026 orders that ship in 2027 must already carry close to all of that year's price premium. The CEO says the 2026 premium lands mainly in 2029–30, which contradicts that. This conclusion rests on one uncertain link: how much of the backlog margin actually reaches the income statement. That ratio has ranged from about 0.2x to 1.6x a year (Q10 test 2).

    Bottom line

    The backlog measure is a contribution margin, and no SEC filing defines it. GEV defines "margin expansion" as the "increase or decrease in the average estimated contribution margin in backlog compared to prior year." It is a cost-as-known estimate and excludes future productivity. - Company increments: +7 / +5 / +6 pts (FY23/24/25). Power: +3 / +3 / +11. Power's YE22 starting point was "approximately breakeven." Dollars added: ">$6B" over 2023–24, "$8B" in 2025, and "at least $8B" in 2026. - [S1: D4Q25 slide 5 fn b; T4Q25 chunk 246127] [S2: R4Q25 "grew equipment margin in backlog by $8B, with 6 pts"; BOFA "in '24… 5 points. In '25… 6 points"] - Order-vintage margins backed out from these disclosures (points above each YE22 base) [computed]: - Company: 2023 orders ≈ +9.6; 2024 ≈ +13.7 to +15.5; 2025 ≈ +20.3 to +21.6; 2026 ≈ +26 to +35 (depends on assumptions). - Power: 2023 ≈ +5.2 to +5.9; 2024 ≈ +5.5 to +7.5; 2025 ≈ +19.3 to +20.4; 2026 ≈ +34 to +40. - Inputs: [K24 and K25 RPO tables; D4Q24 slide 25 EDF adjustment; LAG p.5 "larger than… low double digits"] - Change in equipment contribution margin, FY26→FY27, weighting each vintage by the RPO conversion schedule [computed]: - Under management's timing (2026 orders shipping in 2027 carry roughly 2025-vintage margins): company +1.4 to +2.6 pts, $0.37–0.69B; Power +2.6 to +3.3 pts, $0.33–0.42B. - If the full 2026 premium also lands in FY27: company +5.0 to +5.8 pts ($1.34–1.55B); Power +8.5 pts ($1.07B). - What each case needs: - The research base's margin-rate gain (Power +688, Electrification +262 = $950M) needs 2026-vintage revenue in FY27 at about +25 to +26 pts. That is about one-third of the 2026 premium. - The Street (margin-rate gain of $1,336–1,606M) needs +31 to +36 pts (company) or +34 to +40 pts (Power). That is the entire estimated 2026 premium, on every 2026 dollar shipped in FY27. [computed §4] - Management's timing contradicts that requirement: - 2025 margin reaches the income statement "starting 2 to 3 years from now, so call it '27, '28 and some… '29 and '30" [S1: BOFA #4] [S2: BOFA-MS listing, title only → effectively SINGLE-SOURCE on text]. - The 2026 change "tells you the equipment margins for '29 and '30, largely" [S1: LAG p.10] [S2: EL PP-06 verification of the same PDF → SINGLE primary document]. - Heavy-duty lead time is about 3 years [S1: TP1] [S2: X-SM / TP2, "2026 and 2027 largely sold out" as of July 2025]. - The pass-through from backlog to the income statement is unstable, and the conclusion depends on it: - Reported equipment gross-margin change divided by the change in vintage-weighted contribution points: FY24 ≈ 1.1–1.6x; FY25 ≈ 0.95–1.06x; H1'26 vs FY25 ≈ 0.2–0.35x. - For Power, the derived equipment EBITDA margin rose about +9 to +13 pts a year in FY24–25, several times the backlog arithmetic. - So non-backlog levers (execution, absorption, legacy losses running off) have at times been larger than the backlog effect. [S1: 10Q income statement; K25 via facts PMX-22] [S2: EL E01/D06 split, a derived and circular series per R01 #3]

    Q2

    What the measure is, and how its level compares with reported margins

    AskedWhat is the measure? Gross margin or contribution margin; before or after which costs; equipment only or with services? Is it defined in any filing? How does the level implied for the YE25 backlog compare with reported equipment gross margin (company FY24, FY25, H1'26: equipment revenue minus cost of equipment sold) and with Power?

    Definition. - It is the "average estimated contribution margin in backlog," change versus the prior year, for equipment only [S1: D4Q25 fn b] [S2: T4Q25 "equipment backlog margin dollars"]. - Services backlog margin is discussed separately and only qualitatively [T4Q25 chunk 246150, Parks]. - It is a cost-as-known estimate. The CEO refers to "variable cost productivity not embedded in our backlog margins today" [S1: T4Q25 chunk 246128] [S2: EL PMX-28, GEV PDF]. - No SEC filing defines it. The term is absent from both 10-Ks (vintage_verification #15). This session's corpus hits were releases, calls and the proxy only. - GEV does not say which costs count as variable, so fixed manufacturing overhead, D&A, SG&A, R&D and warranty treatment are not disclosed.

    Implied levels. Two readings of the dollar statements fit the data: - (a) Stock reading. "$ added" = change in (equipment RPO × average margin). With m24 = m25 − 6: - 8,000 = 64,245·m25 − 43,047·(m25 − 6%) → m24 ≈ 19.6%, m25 ≈ 25.6%. - Back-cast: m22 ≈ 7.6% on the EDF-adjusted $28,131M. That gives 2023–24 dollars added of $6.29B, consistent with ">$6B". - Rounding sensitivity (±$0.5B, ±0.5 pt): m25 ≈ 21.7–28.9%. - (b) Flow reading. "$ added" = margin on the year's orders: - 2025: $8B / $42.1B of orders = 19.0%. 2023–24: >$6B / $52.1B = >11.5%. - Against the vintage points above, this implies a company base of about −1 to −2%, i.e. near breakeven like Power. That puts YE25 at about 16.5%. - Both readings fit. The data do not identify which one GEV uses.

    Against reported company equipment gross margin (GAAP; after D&A and fixed factory cost): - FY23 −2.4%, FY24 5.1%, FY25 10.4% (13.4% before the $637M Offshore Wind charge). - H1'25 10.0%, H1'26 11.8% (11,713 − 10,328), Q2'26 13.1% (6,459 − 5,613). - [S1: 10Q income statement] [S2: facts PMX-22 / K25 p.38; offshore charge from K25 revenue-recognition note] - The gap: backlog contribution level 16–29% vs gross margin 11–13%, i.e. about 4–17 pts. GEV never reconciles the two. [computed]

    Power. - Backlog level YE25 ≈ +17 pts from a "breakeven" base [T4Q25 chunk 246150; D4Q25]. - Reported Power segment EBITDA margin (equipment and services combined): 14.68% FY25, 17.63% H1'26 [S1: 10Q Note 24] [S2: Q2 release]. - Derived Power equipment EBITDA margin: FY25 −8.5% to −4.8%; H1'26 0% to +3.6% [EL E01/D06; circular per R01 #3]. - So Power equipment EBITDA runs about 13–25 pts below the backlog contribution level. That is consistent with a large fixed-cost layer; the size of that layer is not disclosed.

    Q3

    Each order vintage's own margin

    AskedBack out each order vintage's own margin from the change in the backlog average. Given backlog dollars and the average-margin change at YE23, YE24, YE25 (and 6/30/26 if disclosed) and the conversion of old backlog in between, what margin, in points above the YE22 base, do the 2024 orders, the 2025 orders and the 2026 orders carry? Show the algebra and give a range for the unknowns.

    Method (pro-rata). The old book runs off at its average margin:

    v_t = [RPO_t·(L_{t−1}+Δ_t) − (RPO_{t−1} − Rev_t)·L_{t−1}] / [RPO_t − (RPO_{t−1} − Rev_t)]

    where L is the average level in points above the base. - FIFO variant: shipments draw from the oldest vintages first. - Curve variant: the old book converts only its disclosed one-year percentage.

    Company. The EDF-adjusted base is confirmed by Strazik's "grown over 50% to $43 billion": 43,047 / 28,131 = +53%, whereas the unadjusted +35% would not be "over 50%".

    Vintage Pro-rata FIFO Curve variant Inputs
    2023 9.57 9.57 — RPO22 adj 28,131; RPO23 adj 36,770; Rev23 18,258; Δ +7
    2024 15.53 13.72 — RPO24 43,047; Rev24 18,952; Δ +5
    2025 21.15 20.25 21.60 (old book converts 44%) RPO25 64,245; Rev25 20,934; Δ +6
    2026 26.4 / 28.1 / 31.4 / 34.8 for Δ26 = +5 / +6 / +8 / +10 similar — RPO26 assumed $100B (team's choice); 2026 draw 23,771

    Power. 2023–25 are from EL PMX-29 (corrected); 2026 is new.

    Vintage Central Range Inputs
    2023 5.2 5.2–5.9 adj RPO22 9,808, RPO23 9,928; Rev23 5,598; Δ +3
    2024 7.5 5.5 (FIFO) – 7.6 RPO24 12,461; Rev24 5,708; Δ +3
    2025 20.4 19.3 (FIFO) – 20.4 RPO25 24,707; Rev25 6,686; Δ +11
    2026 ~35–37 34–40 Old book 15,565 (= 24,707 − 37% conversion) at 17; YE26 Power RPO 40–50B (6/30/26 already $39,261M); Δ26 = +12 to +15 (">11", LAG)

    Independent price check on the 2026 Power vintage. A price increase of p on unchanged cost moves margin to 1 − (1−m)/(1+p). Starting from about 20–25% (the 2025 vintage, and Q4'25 orders) with p = 20% (">20% above 4Q'25", T2Q26 chunk 251590), the result is 33.7–37.5%. That agrees with 34–40 [computed].

    Unknowns that drive the ranges: - Rounding of the disclosed increments (±0.5 pt). - Conversion order (pro-rata vs FIFO). - The Power runoff curve, which borrows the blended curve (VM hole 1). - YE26 RPO, including Prolec's acquired backlog, which enters RPO without being an order. - FX and cancellations.

    Q4

    FY26 and FY27 equipment margin by vintage (points above base)

    AskedApply the vintage shares to get FY26 and FY27 equipment margin (points above the base) for the company and for Power. What is the FY26 -> FY27 change in points and in $M on FY27 equipment revenue (state the revenue you use)?

    Q9

    Over-time vs point-in-time recognition

    AskedPercentage-of-completion: for which products is revenue recognised over time and for which at delivery, and how does that shift when a vintage's margin reaches the income statement?

    • Over time (percentage of completion, cost-to-cost): "customized goods including power generation equipment and long-term construction contracts" [S1: K25 revenue-recognition policy, p.44–45].
    • Point in time: "non-customized equipment and other goods we manufacture on a standardized basis… generally no earlier than when the customer has physical possession" [S1: K25 p.45] [S2: VM hole 6, quoting the 10-K]. The same policy wording was not found verbatim in K24 → treat as [SINGLE document].
    • Split: not disclosed.
    • Mechanism:
    • On over-time contracts, a vintage's margin reaches the income statement as costs are incurred, i.e. during manufacturing. That is ahead of shipment, so HA units shipping in 2029 start booking revenue and margin in 2027–28.
    • Estimate changes are recognised immediately as cumulative catch-up; Offshore Wind losses show the downside: $379M / $1,005M / $637M in FY23–25 [K25 p.44].
    • This is the main reason the RPO dollar curve, which is built on revenue recognition, and "ship year" (GLJ, and the CEO's "'29-'30") can disagree. The RPO curve already reflects over-time recognition. The CEO's year language may refer to deliveries.
    Q10

    Three hand-checkable tests for the model

    AskedThree hand-checkable tests the team can run in its model to decide whether the Street's bridge is supported by the backlog. For each: inputs, formula, and what each result would mean.

    1. Required-X test (Power and company). - Formula: X_req = [Rev27 × (L26 + ΔL_needed) − pre × v_pre − s25 × v25] / s26. - Inputs: Q4 table plus the team's FY27 revenue; ΔL_needed = (bridge margin-rate $) / Rev27. - Readings: X_req ≤ ~21 means the 2025 vintage alone covers it. X_req about 25–28 needs part of the 2026 premium (research base). X_req ≥ 34 needs the whole 2026 premium in 2027, against the CEO's "'29–'30" (Street).
    2. Pass-through calibration. - Formula: k = Δ(reported GAAP equipment GM) / Δ(vintage-weighted points). - History: FY24 +7.5 / (4.6–7.0) = 1.07–1.63; FY25 +5.3 / (5.0–5.6) = 0.95–1.06; H1'26 vs FY25 +1.4 / (5.3–7.1) = 0.20–0.26. - Update with the Q3'26 10-Q (10-28) and the FY26 10-K. - Readings: FY26 k back near 1 favours the Street's pace; k < 0.5 favours the research base or below.
    3. RPO-share test on the January disclosure. - YE26 10-K Note 9: FY27 book slice = RPO26 × 1-yr%, split into pre-2026 (= 64,245 × 32% = 20,558) and 2026 orders. - If the 2026-order share of FY27 equipment revenue is ≤ ~25%, the Street's X_req rises above 35 (harder). If it is ≥ 40%, the required X falls toward 28. - Also compare the Power change in backlog margin against ">11" (LAG). A large number bears on 2029–30, not FY27 (CEO).

    G2: The Street's FY27 needs 2026-vintage pricing in 2027. That is a partial counter to "'29–'30". - G13 / G22: YE26 RPO conversion percentages and the backlog-margin page arrive in late January alongside the FY27 guide. The Q3 10-Q equipment GM (10-28) gives an early k reading. - G20: Traps are contribution vs gross vs EBITDA margin; the stock vs flow reading of "$ added"; EDF-adjusted vs reported RPO; segment-note vs MD&A Power equipment revenue (3,834 vs 3,851). - G21: If this research is wrong, FY26 k should rebound toward 1: Q3'26 equipment GM ≥ ~14.5% with Wind excluded, or Q4 on a similar basis.

    Arithmetic

    A. Company levels (stock reading). - m24 = (8,000 − 64,245 × 0.06) / (64,245 − 43,047) = 4,145 / 21,198 = 19.56%. So m25 = 25.56%, m23 = 14.56%, m22 = 7.56%. - Check: 43,047 × 0.1956 − 28,131 × 0.0756 = 8,420 − 2,127 = 6,293 (> $6B ✓).

    B. Vintages. Company pro-rata: - v23 = 36,770 × 7 / 26,897 = 9.57 - v24 = (516,564 − 17,818 × 7) / 25,229 = 15.53 - v25 = (1,156,410 − 22,113 × 12) / 42,132 = 21.15 - FIFO: v24 = (516,564 − 17,818 × 9.57) / 25,229 = 13.72; v25 = (1,156,410 − 22,113 × 13.72) / 42,132 = 20.25. - Company 2026 (RPO26 = 100,000; old book 40,474 @18): v26 = (100,000 × (18 + Δ) − 728,532) / 59,526. - Power 2026: v26 = (RPO26 × (17 + Δ) − 15,565 × 17) / (RPO26 − 15,565). For example 45,000 at Δ12 gives 35.3.

    C. FY26 / FY27 weights. As in the Q4 tables. For example, Power under management timing: (1,200 × 6.5 + 6,706 × 20.4 + 4,774 × 20.4) / 12,680 = 241,992 / 12,680 = 19.08.

    D. Street margin-rate requirement. - 3,215 − 694 − 517 − 400 = 1,604. FactSet: 2,945 − 1,611 = 1,334. - Power X_req = (12,680 × (15.81 + 5.43 + 3.04 to 5.17) − 144,602) / 4,774 = 34.2–39.9. - Company X_req = (26,900 × (17.3 + 4.97 to 5.97) − 399,873) / 6,342 = 31.4–35.6.

    E. Straight line to 2028. - FY26 guide mid 13% → 20% in FY28 gives a FY27 margin of 16.5%. - On (46.0 + 56.0) / 2 = $51.0B of revenue that is $8.42B; on $52.74B it is $8.70B. - Increment from 5,980 (13% × 46.0): +$2.44B, against research +2.56 and Street +2.95 to +3.22.

    F. Pass-through ratio k. As in Q10 test 2. - Predicted company points: FY24 4.58–7; FY25 10.19–12; FY26 17.3. - FY24 FIFO = 9,079 × 9.57 / 18,952 = 4.58. FY25 FIFO = (17,818 × 9.57 + 3,116 × 13.72) / 20,934 = 10.19.

    What would change this

    FY26 k ≥ ~0.9 in the Q3 10-Q or the FY26 10-K. That would mean non-backlog levers are working, and it would favour the Street. - A statement at Q3 (10-28) or in January that 2026 orders are shipping in 2027 at new pricing. It would contradict LAG p.10 and lower the weight on the timing constraint. - A YE26 two-year conversion percentage well above 69%, i.e. the book shortening. A larger 2026 share in FY27 lowers X_req. - GEV clarifying that "$ added" is margin on orders (flow). Levels would fall to about 16.5%; the point changes would not move. - FY27 guide with a low end ≥ 18%. That would directly contradict the finding.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The "closes $0.6–1.3B of GLJ's gap" figure in this task's text is superseded. The consistent figure is $0.55–0.62B [EL; brief §5].
    2. The brief treats GEV's timing statements as a single "'27 and beyond" message. The Jan-25 wording for the 2024 vintage ("2026 and beyond") slid to "'27 and beyond" in Jan-26 [T4Q24; T4Q25].
    3. The brief says the Dec-2024 and Dec-2025 investor updates quantified backlog margin. I found no quantified backlog-margin statement at either event. The quantified disclosures come from January calls and decks, BofA, the Q1'26 call and Laguna.

    Bottom line

    The FY27 consensus for adjusted EBITDA is a band of $9.34–9.65B across vendors, not a single $9,574M. - FactSet (Boursorama, 09-26): $9,339M. MarketScreener: $9,574M (09-29) and $9,570M (09-04). ChartMill: $9,652M (08-20). GLJ's quoted "Street": $9.45B (09-14). - [S1: BOURSO table "Prévisions de résultats… au 26/09/2026"] [S2: MS-0904/MS-0929 "EBITDA" row] [S3: CM yearly table] [S4: GF] - Only MarketScreener and FactSet show GEV's adjusted-EBITDA FY25 actual of $3,196M. ChartMill's FY25 "EBITDA" is 2,525, so ChartMill is on a different basis. - The vendors' EBIT line is mixed-basis. So the $8,150M EBIT that MarketScreener and FactSet share tells you nothing about which EBITDA figure is right. - The FY25 EBIT actual in both vendors (1,388 / 1,389) is GAAP operating income [10K MD&A "Operating income (loss) $1,388"]. - The FY27 EBITDA–EBIT gap the vendors imply is only $1,189–1,424M. Filings put FY27 D&A alone at about $1.67B: Q2'26 D&A of $418M × 4, lifted by roughly $715M a year of Prolec intangible amortization [computed; 10Q Note 24 reconciliation and Prolec PPA table; Q2REL p.8]. - At least some contributors must be submitting EBIT before acquisition amortization. - FY27 EPS of $24.69–24.85 is internally consistent with MarketScreener's own line items. It does not tie to either EBITDA figure on a full-GAAP basis. - Using filings-based D&A and add-backs, a GAAP EPS of $24.85 needs about $9.9–10.2B of adjusted EBITDA. - If brokers exclude Prolec amortization, it needs about $9.2–9.4B, which sits nearer FactSet's $9,339M. - The P/E of 38.7x therefore rests on an EPS of mixed definition [computed §4-C]. - No published segment consensus exists for FY26–FY28 in any free source searched. - The only published FY27 segment figures are GLJ's own Power 18.5% and its quoted "consensus" of 20.7% [S1: GF] [S2: corpus 235411, MarketBeat 09-18]. - New since the brief: Mizuho (Neutral, $949, 09-30) cut FY27 EBITDA from $9.4B to $9.3B "due to lower Electrification margin growth" and raised FY28 from $12.8B to $13.0B. [SINGLE-SOURCE for the estimates] [S1: INV-MZ]. SI-MZ confirms the note, rating and analyst, but the estimates sit behind its paywall. - Quarterly consensus is not internally consistent, and the two vendors miss in opposite directions. - MarketScreener's FY27 quarters sum to EBITDA of $9,886M against an annual $9,570M (+3.3%). - ChartMill's quarters sum to $9,093M against an annual $9,652M (−5.8%). - The H2'26 margin consensus needs is the same at both: 16.33% (MarketScreener) and 16.29% (ChartMill), against 15.0% at the guide midpoint and 16.75% at the top of guide [computed §4-B]. - Consensus FY26→FY27 incremental EBITDA margin is 44.7% (FactSet) to 49.8% (MarketScreener). - Delivered: 37.1% for FY24→FY25, and 27.9% for H1'26 year on year [computed §4-D; 10K; Q2REL; MS quarters]. - This bridge of company totals is the only Street FY26→FY27 bridge that can be built from published inputs.

    Definition check. Two vendors are on GEV's adjusted-EBITDA definition: - MarketScreener: FY24 2,035 and FY25 3,196 [CT-03]. - FactSet/Boursorama: FY25 3,196. - Both match the 10-K reconciliation "Adjusted EBITDA (Non-GAAP) $3,196 $2,035" [10K MD&A chunk 29797]. - ChartMill's actuals (FY25 2,525; FY24 2,064) are not on that basis. Its FY27 figure of $9,652M should not be used as a like-for-like consensus.

    Why EBIT can match while EBITDA differs. 1. The line is mixed-basis. The FY25 EBIT actual is GAAP operating income ($1,388M) [S1: 10K MD&A "Operating income (loss) $1,388 $471"] [S2: MS-0904 EBIT row 471 / 1,388; BOURSO 1,389]. But the FY27 EBITDA–EBIT gaps (1,424 MarketScreener; 1,189 FactSet) are below the filings-implied FY27 D&A of about $1.67B (§4-C). The EBIT estimates are therefore mostly not GAAP operating income. 2. Each line is averaged over whichever brokers submit it. EBITDA and EBIT contributor sets differ, and neither vendor publishes per-line counts. 3. The two vendors may be the same feed at different settings. EBIT matches to the dollar on 09-26 and 09-29, but FY26 EBIT differs by $320M (4,662 vs 4,342), so they are not identical feeds. - Boursorama notes that FactSet recommends the median. Whether Boursorama displays median or mean is not stated. - MarketScreener's upstream provider is not verified. - The $235M FY27 EBITDA gap is the same order of size as FY25 restructuring plus separation add-backs (277 + 180 = 457 [10K]). That fits a mix of "GAAP EBITDA" and "adjusted EBITDA" contributors. This is a hypothesis, not verified.

    • A GAAP EPS of $24.85 needs adjusted EBITDA of $9.93–10.16B.

    General questions answered along the way

    G2: FY27 consensus needs 45–50% incremental margins, against 37% delivered in FY25 (§4-D). The full-year FY27 margin roughly equals the Q4'26 exit rate. - G20: Definition traps: - EBIT is mixed-basis. - EPS is mixed ex-amortization/GAAP. - ChartMill is off-basis. - Quarterly sums don't tie. - The FactSet MarketWatch FY25 EPS of "7.28" is not GAAP. - The 20.7% Power figure has a single origin. - G22: The only dated revelation of segment assumptions is GEV's own January FY27 outlook. The Street publishes no segment numbers the team could track before then. - G24: FY27 FCF of about $7.4B is now two-sourced (MarketScreener; TIKR/CIQ).

    Arithmetic

    A. EV multiples and lookup values - EV/EBITDA = 247,200 / 9,339 = 26.5x; 247,200 / 9,574 = 25.8x. EV is from the brief. - Lookup value at 25x on FactSet: (25 × 9,339 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $910.8. On MarketScreener: $932.9. Difference: −$22/share.

    B. H2'26 margins - Guide midpoint: FY26 revenue 46,000 × 13% = 5,980. Less H1 EBITDA 2,146 = 3,834. H2 revenue = 46,000 − 20,442 = 25,558. H2 margin = 3,834 / 25,558 = 15.00%. - Top of guide: 46,500 × 14% − 2,146 = 4,364; 4,364 / 26,058 = 16.75%. - Bottom of guide: 45,500 × 12% − 2,146 = 3,314; 3,314 / 25,058 = 13.23%. - MarketScreener consensus: (1,702 + 2,523) / (12,004 + 13,876) = 4,225 / 25,880 = 16.33%. - ChartMill consensus: 4,248 / 26,072 = 16.29%. - H1 inputs: Q2REL; 10Q.

    C. EPS↔EBITDA - Prolec amortization: 2,860/12 + 533/6 + 8/3 + 771/2 = 238.3 + 88.8 + 2.7 + 385.5 = 715 per year (straight-line assumption). - Adjusted EBITDA required for EBT of 8,864, full GAAP: 8,864 + 1,672 + (100 to 326 of restructuring and separation) − 506 − 200 = 9,930–10,156. - Excluding Prolec amortization: subtract 715 → 9,215–9,441. - GAAP EPS at 9,574: (9,574 − 1,672 − 326 + 706) × 0.7508 / 267.8 = $23.22; with 100 of adjustments, $23.85.

    D.     Arithmetic

    A. Ex-Wind seasonality - Inputs: - FY24: H1 714/15,463; Wind H1 −289/3,701 (R2Q24/R2Q25); H2 1,322/19,472; Wind H2 −298/6,000. - FY25: H1 1,227/17,143; Wind −312/~4,105 (derived from −7.6%); H2 1,969/20,925; Wind −286/~5,005. - Ex-Wind margins: - FY24: H1 1,003/11,762 = 8.53%; H2 1,620/13,472 = 12.02%. - FY25: H1 1,539/13,038 = 11.80%; H2 2,255/15,920 = 14.16%. - H1'26: 2,803/16,983 = 16.50%. - H2'26 ex-Wind revenue ≈ 25,558 − 4,600 = 20,958. At 18.9–20.0%, that is 3,961–4,192. - FY = 2,146 + ex-Wind H2 + Wind H2: - Wind +257: 6,364–6,595 - Wind 0: 6,107–6,338 - Wind −286: 5,821–6,052

    B. H2 share test - FY25 H2 share = 1,969/3,196 = 61.6%. - FY26 floor = 2,146/(1 − 0.616) = 5,589. - Guide low end: 3,314/5,460 = 60.7%. Midpoint: 3,834/5,980 = 64.1%. Consensus: 4,213/6,359 = 66.3%.

    C. Segment-midpoint FY26 - Power 19,873 × 1.19 × 18% = 4,257 - Elec 14,750 × 19% = 2,803 - Wind −400; corporate −475 - Total = 6,185 - Top: 19,873 × 1.20 × 19% = 4,531; 15,000 × 20% = 3,000; −400; −450. Total 6,681.

    D. Q4 at midpoints = FY segment − H1 − Q3: - Power 4,257 − 1,842 − 1,004 = 1,411 - Elec 2,803 − 1,200 − 741 = 862 - Wind +257; corporate −118 - Total 2,412

    E. Q4 consensus requirement: (2,535 − 257 + 118)/(7,462 + 4,253) = 2,396/11,715 = 20.45%.

    F. Gap decomposition: 9,574 − 8,744 = 830 = (6,359 − 6,185) + (3,215 − 2,559) = 174 + 656.

    What would change this

    Q3 Wind below about −$100M, or the FY Wind guide widened. The base then likely lands at or below the guide midpoint, and the base share of the gap rises toward 37%+. - Q3 Power ≥ 18.5% or Electrification ≥ 20%. This supports the segment-top FY26 (~$6.5–6.7B). The research growth path would then sit only −3.5% to −5% below consensus FY27. - A disclosed Vineyard settlement gain or loss could move Wind H2 by an amount that has not been quantified. - Prolec seasonality differing from legacy Electrification would weaken the Electrification seasonal inference.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The brief's framing suggests FY26 consensus is stretched. The evidence says the stretch is almost entirely Wind. Power and Electrification seasonality support consensus; the issue is not company-wide margin.
    2. "Never beaten first margin guide": against the final guide, FY24 finished 5bp above the midpoint and FY25 10bp below it. The company margin lands near the midpoint; it is neither a beat nor a miss pattern.
    3. Quarterly EBITDA versus consensus is not a one-way record. There were two misses (Q4'25 −10.9%, Q2'26 ~−2%) and two beats (Q3'25, Q1'26).

    Q8

    Scorecard and break-even table

    AskedBottom line: the three best-evidenced reasons the multiple compresses to 25-26x or lower by late January, and the three best-evidenced reasons it does not, each with two sources; which side has the better evidence. Then the break-even table: for FY27 EBITDA of $8.6B, $8.9B, $9.3B and $9.6B, the January price at 23x, 25x, 26x and 28x (state the bridge you use).

    Reasons the multiple compresses to ≤25–26x 1. Peer gap. 28.2x vs US peers at ~21x and all peers at 17.7x [MS; TIKR]. 2. Mechanical. At consensus, a flat price already means 25.1x by late January; the roll itself does it. 3. In-sample triggers. A margin-held report day (−8.69% / −12.55% over 5 days), plus AI risk-off days that took the multiple to 24.9x (12-17-25) and 25.4x (09-14-26) [NQ; EnergyWatch; BX-13]. - Also: the 06-30→09-14 fall was ~all de-rating while estimates rose [CL; R08].

    Reasons it does not 1. The floor has risen. 12-month closing floor ≈ 23.4x; month-ends ≥25.0x; 2026 troughs 25.4–28.5x [CL; NQ reconstruction]. 2. January and event record. Both January days were positive, and framework or margin raises delivered +13.75% to +15.62% [BX-13; D04B/Barron's]. 3. Street and capital return. No FY27 cuts; brokers raising targets; $3.0B authorization left, with a December pattern of re-ups [R08; 10Q2].

    Which side has the better evidence (research judgement): - The "does not compress" side has more direct, GEV-specific evidence: its own troughs and event days. - The "compress" side rests on relative value, which has not bound since the spin, plus event risk that is real but undated. - The short's arithmetic needs ≤~26x at the research FY27 number, which is near the observed 12-month floor band (25–26x).

    Break-even table: January-2027 price - Bridge: Price = (m × NTM + $9,113M) / 266.33M. NTM = 11/12·FY27 + 1/12·FY28, with FY28 = FY27 × 1.3645 (the consensus FY28/FY27 ratio), so NTM = FY27 × 1.03038. - Net cash is held at the 6/30/26 level; each +$1B adds +$3.75/share.

    Arithmetic

    A. Late-January bridge - NTM(cons) = 11/12 × 9,574 + 1/12 × 13,064 = 9,865. - Flat-price multiple = (962.49 × 266.33 − 9,113) / NTM = 247,227 / 9,865 = 25.06x. - Table cells: (m × FY27 × 1.03038 + 9,113) / 266.33. Example: 8.9B at 26x = (26 × 9,170 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $929.5.

    B. Reconstructed month-end multiples - CL-implied NTM EBITDA at each anchor: E = (P × 266.33 − 9,113) / m_CL.

    Anchor Price CL multiple Implied E ($M)

    12-17-25 614.19 24.87x 6,211
    04-23-26 1,149.53 40.39x 7,354

    07-29-26 900.28 27.54x 8,375

    • E is interpolated linearly between anchors, and held at 5,852 before 11-04. Because E was probably lower before 11-04, the Oct-25 multiples are lower bounds.
    • Month-end multiple = (P × 266.33 − 9,113) / E. Example: 08-31, E = 8,375 + 33 × 9.04 = 8,673, giving (898.53 × 266.33 − 9,113) / 8,673 = 26.54x.
    • Caveats: today's share count and net cash are applied to all dates, and CL's EV definition is unknown. Error ≈ ±1x.
    • Threshold price for 26x at 11-04 = (26 × 5,852 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $605.5.

    C. 09-14 cross-check - NTM = 0.296 × 6,359 + 0.704 × 9,450 = 8,535. - EV = 874.76 × 266.33 − 9,113 = 223,862, so the multiple is 26.2x (CL: 25.44x).

    D. 52-week-high decomposition - E at 06-30 = 7,772 + 20 × 12.3 = 8,018; multiple = 303,788 / 8,018 = 37.9x. - ln(8,800 / 8,018) = +0.093; ln(25.44 / 37.9) = −0.399; sum −0.306 vs ln(223,862 / 303,788) = −0.305. Ties.

    E. Other - Buyback remaining: 10.0 − 7.0 = $3.0B; 3.0 / 256.3 = 1.17%. - FY27 FCF yield: 7,417 / 256,340 = 2.9%. - Siemens Energy multiple ratio: 28.2 / 12.6 = 2.24; growth ratio: 43.3 / 36 = 1.20. - Event returns, e.g. Jan-26 20-day: 876.01 / 692.70 − 1 = +26.46%.

    What would change this

    Floor and percentiles: a point-in-time EV/EBITDA history (FactSet or Bloomberg) showing late-2025 troughs well below 23x would lower the floor. If it showed the Jan-26 dip above 26x, the "≤26x episodes" list shrinks. - Reference class: verified 1- and 3-month paths for VRT-25, ETN-26 and PWR-25. If all recovered within a month, the "guide below consensus = de-rating" reading weakens. - Break-even table: a December-2026 authorization re-up, or a larger H2 cash build, raises every cell by about $3.75 per $1B.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The brief's premise that "the short loses ~3% if the multiple holds" is right only at 28x. The relevant break-even at FY27 $8.6–8.9B is 27.0–27.9x, and at consensus it is 25.1x (§4-A).
    2. "52-week range $530.16–$1,195.94" is intraday. On closes it is $547.96 (2025-11-04) to $1,174.86 (2026-06-30), as already flagged in prior work.
    3. The earnings date may be in conflict (TrendSpider shows 10-21 vs the brief's 10-28). Verify on the GEV IR site.

    What we asked

    Read F01_final_synthesis.md and R01_redteam_final.md first (list_overnight_outputs / read_overnight_output; file names end in .md), then whatever else you need. Everything you produce is research input: facts, numbers, formulae and sources only, never memo prose. Apply the two-citation rule to every number. Where a figure is your own calculation, show the formula and mark it [computed]. "Not disclosed" and "could not find" are valid answers. Do not repeat work that an earlier output already did well: cite it and go further.

    THE QUESTION (outside view): in this gas-turbine and grid-equipment upcycle, how fast have better order prices turned into reported margins at GEV's direct competitors, and what is the largest one-year segment margin step anyone has delivered? The Street needs GEV's company adj EBITDA margin to rise about 4.4 points in FY27 (13.7% to 18.15%) after about 5.3 points in FY26; the research base has about 3.3 points. Use the competitors' own filings and results presentations wherever you can.

    • Q1. Siemens Energy Gas Services: orders, backlog, revenue and profit margin before special items for FY22-FY25 and each reported FY26 quarter; FY26 guidance and how it changed; mid-term targets (FY28) and when they were raised; management statements on order pricing, backlog margin and the time it takes to reach the income statement; the date of the FY26 results and FY27 guidance (November 2026).
    • Q2. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Energy Systems / GTCC: the same series and statements; order intake in GW; FY2026 guidance; medium-term plan targets.
    • Q3. Grid equipment: Siemens Energy Grid Technologies, Hitachi Energy, Eaton Electrical Americas, Hubbell Utility, Schneider. Segment margin by year 2022-2026 and the largest one-year step each delivered. This is the base rate for GEV Electrification going from 18-20% (FY26) to 22% (2028).
    • Q4. The lag: for each competitor, how many quarters pass between a price increase in orders and its arrival in segment margin, in management's own words?
    • Q5. Base rate: across all these segments and years, the distribution of one-year margin changes (median, 75th percentile, maximum). Where do +3.3 points (research base, GEV company FY27) and +4.4 points (consensus) sit? Do the same for GEV Power (+2.5 points in the research base).
    • Q6. What is different about GEV that could justify a faster step (services mix, Prolec, the Wind loss going away, slot-reservation economics, the size of its price increases)? Evidence for each.
    • Q7. Capacity and pricing behaviour: announced heavy-duty gas-turbine capacity additions (GEV to 24 GW in 2028 and actions toward 30 GW in 2030; Siemens Energy; MHI; others) and any sign that pricing is flattening or lead times are shortening.
    • Q8. Read-through dates before late January 2027 and what each could tell the team.
    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    Scope and method. This is research input only: facts, arithmetic and ranges. Every "range" below is a research estimate; the team chooses its own numbers.

    I read F01, V07 and P6 first. None of them had a peer margin base rate, so everything in this file is new work, built from: - the competitor filings and decks in the corpus; - Exa and web search for years the corpus lacks.

    On the two-citation rule. Many peer numbers appear in two documents from the same publisher, for example the Siemens Energy earnings release and its analyst deck. They are independent documents but not independent publishers, and the tables flag this as "same-publisher".

    Bottom line

    Distribution of realised one-year margin steps. Across 17 realised steps at direct and adjacent peer segments (FY22–FY25), the median step is +3.1 pts, the 75th percentile +3.9 pts and the maximum +6.7 pts (Hubbell Utility Solutions, 2023, adjusted operating margin). - The only other step above +4.4 pts is Siemens Energy (SE) Grid Technologies FY25, at about +4.8 pts. - The largest step in heavy-duty gas is +3.5 pts (SE Gas Services FY25). MHI Energy Systems managed +2.6 and +1.7. - [computed §4; inputs SE-AR25 + SE-CMR24; MHI-FY24 + MHI-FY25; ETN23 + ETN25; HUBB23 + HUBB24 + HUBB25; HIT25 + HIT25b] - Where GEV's company steps sit. The Street's +4.4 pts for FY27 sits at about the 88th percentile: 2 of 17 peer segment-years reached it. The research base's +3.3 pts sits at about the 53rd percentile. - Caveat: GEV's figure is a company margin, and it gets a mechanical lift from the Wind loss shrinking (about 0.76 pts, per F01/E05). - The closest company-level analog, SE group FY24→FY25 at +5.0 pts, was also driven by a wind loss narrowing [SE-AR25 §2.4.2; SE-Q4FY24 / SE-PR24]. - The gas peers show the lag directly. SE Gas Services backlog margin rose about 12 pts on new units and about 3 pts on service between FY22 and FY25. Reported GS margin rose only +6.4 pts (6.6% → 13.0%) over the same three years. - Weighting the backlog-margin gains 40/60 new unit/service gives about +6.6 pts. That is roughly equal to the reported gain. - This is consistent with the whole backlog-margin gain reaching the P&L within about three years at SE's 3+-year lead times. - [SE-CFO26 chunk 251878; SE-IR26 chunk 251823; SE-AR25; lead times per the Power Engineering / trade-press report in corpus src:1699 — SINGLE-SOURCE on lead times] - The gas peers are accelerating now, but the fiscal-year steps are still around 2.5–3.6 pts. - SE Gas Services: Q3 FY26 17.3% vs 13.0% (+4.2 pts year on year); 9M FY26 16.6% vs 14.6%. The FY26 guide of 14–16% was never raised, even though 9M already sits above its top [SE-Q3R; SE-Q3P]. - MHI Energy Systems: Q1 FY26 18.9% vs 13.3%. The full-year forecast is 15.5% vs 13.0% (+2.5 pts), unchanged at Q1 [MHI-Q1; MHI-FY25]. - GEV's own Electrification already beats the peer base rate. Its margin went +5.3 pts (FY24) and +5.9 pts (FY25), 3.7% → 9.0% → 14.9%, which would rank 2nd and 3rd in the peer set. - Going from the FY26 guide of 18–20% to 22% in 2028 needs only about +1–2 pts a year. That is below the peer median. - GEV Power's organic step in FY25 was only +1.0 pt (13.2% → 14.2%) against +2.2 pts reported. - [GEV10K segment MD&A and organic non-GAAP table; S2: master brief §3 / FACTS for the reported Power series] - No sign of heavy-duty pricing flattening was found. - MHI is explicitly restraining bookings as it doubles capacity: "does not mean that we are immediately seeking to book twice as many orders" [TP-MHI, two corpus copies of the same trade article — same-origin]. - MHI's FY26 order forecast (¥3,550bn, raised from ¥3,450bn) is still below FY25's ¥3,936.7bn, which is the first year-on-year decline guided by a heavy-duty OEM [MHI-Q1; MHI-FY25].

SINGLE-SOURCE, deck only. - Q1 FY26 release attributes the gain partly to "higher profitability of the processed order backlog" [SE-Q1R chunk 251841]. - CFO, Q3 FY26: new orders "are still coming in at higher margins than older backlog" [facts TP-30, Investing.com transcript 2026-08-05]. I could not open a second transcript copy. - Time to the P&L: SE did not state it in quarters. The nearest data points are lead times of "three years or longer" [corpus src:1699 — SINGLE-SOURCE] and the FY22→FY25 conversion arithmetic in §4.

    Q6

    What could justify a faster GEV step

    AskedWhat is different about GEV that could justify a faster step (services mix, Prolec, the Wind loss going away, slot-reservation economics, the size of its price increases)? Evidence for each.

    Factor Evidence Direction
    Wind loss going away −$400M → ~0 is about 0.76 pts of company margin (F01 / E05). The FY26 Wind guide needs +$257M in H2 (brief §4) Supports about 0.5–0.8 pts of the +4.4 without any segment step
    Services mix Power services share fell 67.9% → 63.1% (brief §3). Company services gross margin fell 35.1% → 31.6% (F01, 10-K / 10-Q) Against: mix has been a headwind, and margin gains came from equipment
    Slot-reservation economics SRAs are 54% of GEV's GW vs 27% at SE (facts RQ-16). SRA pricing "10 to 20 points" and ">20%" above backlog (brief §6). But the CEO dates the margin to '29–'30 Supports price; the timing evidence argues against FY27
    Size of price increases LG&E/KU all-in cost +53–57% (brief §6). Wood Mackenzie sees about $600/kW by end-2027, +195% vs 2019 (corpus src:3846; SINGLE-SOURCE, secondary) Industry-wide, so it also flows to SE and MHI, whose steps are still ≤3.5
    Prolec +$3.1B revenue in the Electrification guide (brief §4). Prolec's margin was not verified this session Unknown
    GEV's own record Electrification +5.3 / +5.9 (GEV10K) beat peers; Power +2.6 / +2.2 reported, only +1.0 organic in FY25 (GEV10K non-GAAP table) Electrification: GEV can beat base rates. Power: it has not so far
    Operating leverage Power incremental margin 44.4% from H1'25 to H1'26 (V07 R6, citing the 10-Q) Supports acceleration; the peer analog is MHI's Q1 FY26 +5.6 pts
    Q7

    Capacity and pricing behaviour

    AskedCapacity and pricing behaviour: announced heavy-duty gas-turbine capacity additions (GEV to 24 GW in 2028 and actions toward 30 GW in 2030; Siemens Energy; MHI; others) and any sign that pricing is flattening or lead times are shortening.

    Capacity plans - GEV: 20 GW/yr run-rate from Q3'26, 24 GW in 2028, toward 30 GW by 2030 (brief §3; facts PP-22). - SE: about 35 large-GT manufacturing units, +15 in 2027; medium units 80 → about 100 by 2028; 15–16 GW of deliveries in FY26; 6 GW shipped in Q3 [corpus src:1699 — SINGLE-SOURCE trade article of the Q3 call]. SE sold 194 gas turbines in FY25, about 2x FY24 [SE-CFO26 chunk 251877; corpus src:3189 "~200 GTs"]. - MHI: double large-frame capacity vs 2024 (trade press corpus src:244; TP-MHI). The CFO said the doubling "does not mean that we are immediately seeking to book twice as many orders as before" (2026-08-06 briefing) [TP-MHI].

    Signs of flattening - Pricing: none found. SE says new orders still carry higher margins than the backlog (TP-30), and MHI says margins at booking are improving (MHI-QA). - Softer signals: 1. MHI's FY26 order forecast is ¥3,550bn vs ¥3,936.7bn actual in FY25 (−10%) [MHI-Q1; MHI-FY25]. 2. SE GT book-to-bill is flat at 1.5 [SE-Q3P]. - Lead times: no evidence of shortening. SE is at 3+ years (src:1699); GEV is selling 2031–32 slots (V07; corpus src:3846). - Capacity vs orders: Wood Mackenzie puts manufacturing capacity at 60–70 GW against about 110 GW of orders at end-2025 (corpus src:3846 and src:137 — two web pages citing the same Wood Mackenzie figure, same-origin).

    General questions answered along the way

    G2 (has GEV delivered the consensus pace before?). At company level, yes: FY26 is about +5.3 pts. In Power, no single year has exceeded +2.6 reported or +1.0 organic (FY25). Among gas peers, no year has exceeded +3.5 (§Q5). - G11 (physical constraints). SE lead times are 3+ years and MHI is restraining bookings. Capacity additions arrive in 2027–30 (§Q7), so price-to-margin conversion is lead-time-bound. - G12 (when accounting shows results). SE's reported margin tracked backlog margin with about a 3-year lag (A4). That is consistent with the GEV CEO's '29–'30 statement, not with a front-loaded FY27. - G19 (analogies). Grid peers plateaued after their big step (Eaton 2025 −0.3; Hubbell 2024 −0.4). The step-then-plateau pattern is the base rate for short-cycle price realisation. - G21 (what we'd see if the short view were wrong). SE's FY27 GS guide stepping more than +3.5 pts, or MHI's ES reaching about 18% for the full year. Q1 FY26 was 18.9%.

    Arithmetic

    A1. Peer one-year steps (pts) - SE GS FY25: 12.95 − 9.46 = +3.5 - SE GT FY25: 15.8 − 11.0 = +4.8 (±0.5 from rounding the FY24 figure) - SE TI (SE-CFO26 chunk 251893: −2.0 / 1.1 / 5.1 / 7.4 / 11.3): +3.1, +4.0, +2.3, +3.9 [SINGLE-SOURCE; the AR shows FY24 7% and FY25 11%, consistent] - MHI ES: +2.6, +1.7 - Hitachi Energy segment: 12.92 − 9.63 = +3.3 - Eaton EA: +1.9, +4.0, +3.7, −0.3 - Hubbell adj.: +6.7, −0.4, +0.5 - Schneider (organic): +0.5; I used the reported +0.1 in the sort.

    A2. Distribution - Sorted (n = 17): −0.4, −0.3, 0.1, 0.5, 1.7, 1.9, 2.3, 2.6, 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 4.0, 4.0, 4.8, 6.7. - Median = 9th value = 3.1. P75 = 13th value = 3.9. P90 ≈ 4.3. Max = 6.7. - Direct-only (n = 12): median (2.6 + 3.3) / 2 = 2.95; P75 ≈ 3.78.

    A3. GEV positions - Consensus company step: 18.15% − (6,359 / 46,282 = 13.74%) = +4.41 pts (MS consensus per the brief). - Percentiles are counts from A2.

    A4. SE GS conversion check - Blended backlog-margin gain = 0.40 × 12 + 0.60 × 3 = 6.6 pp. - Reported margin gain FY22→FY25 = 13.0 − 6.6 = +6.4 pts. - Weights are FY25 backlog weights (SE-IR26), which is an approximation.

    A5. GEV Electrification to 2028 - (22 − 19) / 2 = +1.5 pts a year (range +1.0 to +2.0 across the 18–20% guide).

    A6. MHI Q1 margins - 101.3 / 536.3 = 18.9%; 56.4 / 423.2 = 13.3%.

    What would change this

    The "+4.4 is ~88th percentile" finding changes if SE guides FY27 GS at ≥ +4.4 pts above its FY26 actual (Nov-2026), or if MHI H1 ES stays above 18%. Either would show gas peers now converting faster than their history. - The "lag of ~8–12 quarters" finding changes if SE or MHI management state explicitly that FY27 absorbs most of the 2025 pricing. - The "no pricing flattening" finding changes on any OEM comment on flat or declining pricing, SRA cancellations, or lead times below 3 years. MHI's lower FY26 order forecast is the watch item.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The brief implies a steady climb in Power margin. Organically, the FY25 Power step was only +1.0 pt (13.2% → 14.2%) against +2.2 reported; the difference comes from FX and dispositions [GEV10K non-GAAP organic table; single document]. The team should use organic figures when citing the pace.
    2. The SE Q4 FY26 date of 2026-11-11 conflicts with 2026-11-12 in SE's own Nov-2025 calendar. Re-verify.
    3. Not a contradiction but worth flagging: GEV Electrification's past steps (+5.3, +5.9) are above every grid peer except Hubbell 2023. Peer base rates do not argue against the 22% 2028 Electrification target.

    SE GS FY23 profit and margin; SE GT FY22–FY23. The SE Q3 FY26 call transcript on the SE IR site would serve.

    Q2

    Five PM objections

    AskedThe five strongest objections a Citadel portfolio manager would raise to THIS thesis. For each: the best evidence for the objection, the best evidence against it, and which wins on the evidence.

    1. "A consensus above guidance is the signature of a serial raiser (sandbagging), not a Street that is too high." - For the objection:
      • FY26 went from the Jan guide midpoint of $5,340M to the current $5,980M (+12%), with consensus at $6,359M (+19%) [R07 §1].
      • In Dec-24, the targets "slightly lagged consensus", and a year later the new framework surpassed the market (JPM via TipRanks and Yahoo; Morningstar).
      • FCF beats of 65–89% (brief).
      • Against:
      • The margin has never finished above its first numeric guide: FY25 came in at 8.40% vs an 8.5% midpoint [R01 #8].
      • The margin guide was held in July, when Q2 missed.
      • Wind was cut and then missed: −$598M against "~$400M" [Q3'25 release; 10-K p.72].
      • Winner: the objection, for the Q3 and FY26 rungs (consensus is inside the ranges). Undetermined for FY27–28.
    2. "Your management anchors are stale or constructed, so the ladder widens by construction." - For:
      • The FY27 comparison point is interpolated.
      • The FY28 framework dates from January 2026, and the FY26 revenue guide has risen $1.5B since.
      • The pack's own T4: management's plan implies a 52.2% incremental margin from FY26 to 2028, above the Street's FY27 45–50%.
      • T3: the Street's FY27 step (+3.9 to +4.4 pts) is smaller than the guided FY26 step (+4.6).
      • Against: the Street's FY28 margin (21.6%) is 1.6 pts above the plan, and revenue staleness does not explain that.
      • Winner: the objection, largely. The widening is partly an artefact of timing.
    3. "The multiple has a floor you need to break." - For: no month-end close below ~25x in the last 12 months, and troughs have stepped up from 15.6x to 23–25x to 25–28.5x [S04; D05]. - Against: the 2025 troughs were 15.6–16.5x; the peer median is 17.7x; GE's P/E halved between 2000 and 2002 while EPS rose 19% [D05]. - Winner: the objection, over the January horizon. 25–26x is at the floor, not inside the range.
    4. "January will not settle it, and it comes bundled with positives." - For:
      • R07 zones: ~35% thesis-wrong, ~45% ambiguous, ~20% thesis-right.
      • Both prior first guides were at or below consensus, and the stock still rose (+5.01% and +15.62% next day) because frameworks were raised alongside.
      • The CEO has pre-flagged a backlog-margin change "larger" than low double digits, $200B backlog and ≥125 GW [S04; D07; LAG].
      • Against: no framework event is scheduled for January (the CMD is in spring). Q2'26, a hold with no margin raise, fell 8.69%.
      • Winner: the objection.
    5. "There is no information edge: GLJ published it, the backlog margin is disclosed, and the premium is growth-justified." - For:
      • PEG 0.65 vs VRT 0.64.
      • Two-year EBITDA CAGR of 43.3% is the highest in the set.
      • GLJ's note made the same point on 09-14.
      • Revisions since then are flat.
      • Sources: [S04; D05; R08]
      • Against: the gap to Siemens Energy is not explained by growth (2.2x its multiple for 1.2x its growth), and the Street's +4.4-pt step sits at the 88th percentile of peer segment steps [S05].
      • Winner: roughly even.

    Facts in S01–S05 that contradict the thesis

    AskedIs there any fact in S01-S05 that contradicts the thesis outright? Quote it with its source.

    • S03: "Seasonality in Power and Electrification supports consensus FY26… Consensus ($6,359M) sits exactly on 'Wind delivers.'" This directly undercuts the FY26 rung, which S03 read as consensus = management's segment guides delivered [S03 §1, from releases Q2'24–Q2'26].

    • S02, both ways: Mizuho "raised FY28 from $12.8B to $13.0B". One broker is moving FY28 away from the plan even as it cuts FY27.

    Nothing is an outright falsification. The S03 and S04 lines are the closest.

    Q5

    Base rate for another raise, and signs of slowing

    AskedGEV has raised or held every guide since the spin. What is the base rate for "a company that has raised N times in a row raises again", and what evidence (if any) says this raise cycle is slowing: the July 2026 margin-guide hold, the Q2'26 EBITDA shortfall, revision momentum, anything else?

    • Base rate. No clean academic base rate for "raise after N raises" was found.
    • Myers, Myers & Skinner (2007) find 746 firms with EPS-increase strings of 20+ quarters, "much larger than would be expected by chance". Strings persist more than chance would predict, which the authors read as partly managed [S1: SSRN 741244] [S2: Exa library record of the same paper; one study → effectively SINGLE-SOURCE].
    • Guidance practice is sticky: past guidance predicts current guidance [NYU Stern working paper on guidance consistency, abstract only].
    • A naive Laplace estimate on 11 post-spin report/event days with no company revenue or FCF cut gives (11+1)/(11+2) ≈ 92% "no cut" next time [computed; the count is from R01 #5]. But the thesis does not need a cut.
    • The relevant base rate is first guides versus consensus. It is 2 of 2 at or below consensus (FY25: JPM "slightly below"; FY26: at or below on revenue). In both cases the stock rose, because frameworks were raised at the same event [TipRanks 2024-12-11; S04 §1 item 5].
    • Evidence of slowing:
    • The margin guide was held in July after the April raise [Q2REL; T2Q26 chunk 251606].
    • Q2 adj EBITDA was ~$1,255M (11.3% × $11,104M), below LSEG and StockStory estimates (−2.1%) [Q2REL; Reuters/StockStory via R08].
    • FY27 EPS revisions decelerated: +11.0%, then +6.5%, then +0.3% [R08: cnyes/FactSet → MS].
    • Q3 EPS revisions: −1.5% over 1 month and −2.1% over 3 months (ChartMill); −2.9% over 30 days (Zacks) [D07].
    • Mizuho cut FY27 [Investing.com; SINGLE].
    • Evidence against slowing:
    • The FY26 revenue-guide increments accelerated: +$0.5B, then +$1.0B [R08: TipRanks/TheFly; Reuters].
    • Yahoo counts 18 up / 3 down FY27 revisions over 30 days.
    • Jefferies (→$1,185) and Bernstein (→$1,298) raised targets after GLJ [R08].
    Q6

GEV's multiple history has not been regressed against its forward growth: a point-in-time growth series is not available.

    (c) Growth once the window rolls. - Consensus FY26→27 is +50.6% and FY27→28 is +36.5%; the plan path FY27→28 is +30.4%. - FY28→29 has no published consensus (Q6). My research range for FY28→29 EBITDA growth is about +15% to +35% (team's choice). On the §4-F base, the Sep-27 NTM roll is +21% on the consensus path and +36% on the plan path.

    Q2

    Power equipment vs services split: E01 vs D06

    Verdict: confirmed on direction and change; not confirmed on level. GEV does not disclose it, and every level depends on three undisclosed parameters: - D&A inside cost of services (d); - Wind and Electrification services gross margins; - how Power overhead is allocated between equipment and services.

    Implied Power equipment EBITDA margin FY23 FY24 FY25 H1'26
    D06 central −27% −13.5% −4.8% +3.6%
    E01 central −31% −18% −8.5% 0.0%
    Joint band (E01 §1) −41 to −19 −29 to −5 −18 to +3.5 −9 to +11
    Power services EBITDA margin (E01 central) 29.7% 26.7% 26.6% 27.9%
    • Why they differ: about 2.7 of the 3–5 points comes from overhead share (D06 66% by revenue; E01 58%, citing the 10-K R&D description p.7). The rest comes from d and the non-Power services margins.
    • What survives every scenario:
    • The change from FY23 to H1'26 is +29.9 to +32.3 points [E01 Q3].
    • Company services gross margin fell from 35.1% to 31.6% while Power's gross margin before D&A rose from 23.0% to 28.2%. The improvement came from equipment [S1: 10K p.39] [S2: 10Q p.6].
    • Management statements match on a contribution-margin basis only:
    • YE2022 backlog margin "approximately breakeven" [S1: Q4'25 call chunk 246150] [S2: GEV webcast transcript 01-28-2026].
    • "Stabilizing Gas new unit contribution margins LSD-MSD" [S1: GE 2019 outlook deck] [S2: 2020 UBS transcript via D06].
    • Definition trap (E03): Power equipment/services revenue differs between the segment note (H1'26 3,834 / 6,593 / 22 intersegment) and the MD&A (3,851 / 6,598). Use the segment-note figures for the split, because the cost lines sit there.

    How the team re-derives it by hand (H1'26; each step verified this session): 1. Company services gross profit (after D&A) = 8,729 − 5,974 = 2,755 [10Q p.6; Q2REL income statement]. 2. Add back services D&A. d = 1.75% × 8,729 = 153 (assumption, team's choice of 1.0–2.5%). 3. Take off non-Power services gross profit. Wind: 10% × 1,174 = 117. Electrification: 32.5% × 948 = 308 (assumptions). Revenues are from 10Q p.23. 4. Power services gross profit before D&A = 2,755 + 153 − 117 − 308 = 2,483 (37.7% of 6,593). 5. Power overhead = SG&A 918 + R&D 286 + other (100) = 1,104 [10Q p.23]. Services share 58% = 640. 6. Power services EBITDA = 2,483 − 640 = 1,843 (27.95%). 7. Equipment EBITDA = 1,842 − 1,843 = −1, on equipment plus intersegment revenue of 3,856 = 0.0%. 8. Check: (1,843 − 1) / 10,449 = 17.63%, which equals the reported Power margin.

    FY25, same method: services 26.55%, equipment −8.5%. That matches E01.

    Kill rule (research proposal; the team sets its own) - Short: FY27 guide low end ≥ 18%; or EBITDA guide midpoint ≥ ~$9.4B (−2% vs consensus); or 2028 raised to ≥ $12.5B. - The price stop is $1,079: consensus rolled at a constant 28.2x [E02 Q4]. - I added a dollar leg because of E04/E05: a revenue-led guide can land below 18% on margin and still be close to consensus in dollars. - Long: midpoint ≤ 17% with no 2028 raise, or NTM EV/EBITDA ≤ 20x.

    Q6

    What incentives (E04) and pricing evidence (E08) add

    E04, incentives - Bonus EBITDA targets were set at about the guide midpoint (FY24 $2,000M; FY25 $2,900M). FCF targets were set at the top of the guide. - Actual EBITDA beat the target by +1.75% and +10.2%; FCF by +70% and +48% [S1: DEF 14A -25-000049 p.54; -26-000049 p.50] [S2: 4Q24 / 4Q25 releases]. - The "beats are cash, not margin" pattern is now in the pay record. - No 2026 targets are disclosed. The 2024–26 PSU targets appear only in the spring-2027 proxy. - What it adds: the pay record supports conservative guiding. That weakens any inference from "guide < consensus" to "consensus too high".

    E08, pricing - There is no turbine-only price by vintage. The GE-linked all-in plant cost steps are: - 2024 → 2025: +53% to +66% (LG&E/KU $1,398 → $2,144/kW; JEA $2,326) [S1: KY PSC 2025-00045 Tummonds p.4–5] [S2: GridLab T2]. - A new same-owner pair (Oglethorpe 7HA.03): $2,316 → $3,226–3,787/kW, +39% to +64% nominal, about +19% to +45% after escalation (the 2033 figure is single-source) [S1: 0000788816-25-000023 slide 4] [S2: 0000788816-26-000050 slides 5/8]. - CEO-endorsed GE slice: ~$750/kW (30% × $2,500) [S1: Q3'25 transcript src:3796] [S2: Motley Fool]. - What it adds: support for a big vintage price step, which is long-leaning beyond 2027. It gives no FY27 timing information. There is no escalation clause evidence, and older fixed-price backlog cannot be repriced [10K Item 1A; E06 Q6].

    General questions answered along the way

    G1. At a flat price the stock needs 25.1x in January and 20.3x in Sep-27. Physically: 5 → 6 GW a quarter, 24 GW in 2028, Power at 22% by 2028 [A1; LAG-SA]. - G2. Consensus FY27 needs +5.15 points of company margin; the largest step so far is +4.6 points (V11 R1). It also needs above-trend equipment margin (A3). - G7. The gap is interpretation and timing, not information. The backlog-margin slide is published every January (V10). - G12. Fixed-price equipment with no escalation found, and deposits at 3.0x cash. Old backlog cannot be repriced [E06 Q6/Q7]. - G15. Five drawdowns of 15% or more since the spin, median −24.6%; the GLJ-day drop was 106% recovered in 11 sessions [BX; Nasdaq]. - G16. Rates: a Fed hike on 09-16 and 49–64% odds of an October hike [E07 rows 22–23]. - G17. Buybacks: $3,037M left, and a new authorisation plausibly comes in January (inference). The guiding cushion is visible in the pay record (E04). - G19. GE 2000–02: the multiple de-rated 1.5–2 years before earnings fell, and earnings broke only after orders turned. No order turn is visible yet; H2'26 signings are set to roughly halve [E06 Q2/Q4]. - G24. H1 OCF excluding deposits was −$3.0B while ~$3.67B was bought back [10Q p.7]. - New from LAG-SA (read this session): "every gigawatt of HAs will generate $500,000,000 of high-margin services revenue over the first 20 years" [SINGLE-SOURCE until checked against LAG-PDF].

(25 × 9,365 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $913.3. - A3, required equipment margin. e = (P − w·s) / (1 − w), with s = 28%: - Consensus P 21.7–23.5%: w = 0.60 gives 12.3–16.8%; w = 0.55 gives 14.0–18.0%. - Builds P 20.0–20.5%: w = 0.60 gives 8.0–9.3%. - Trend: an H1'26 base of 0–3.6% plus 1.25 years × 6–10 points a year gives 7.5–16%. - A4, split re-derivation.     Bottom line

    The primary-source numbers in F01 hold up. Its framing often does not. All 20 rows of the hand-verify table that I re-opened match the filings. I could not re-open rows 4, 10 and 18 myself (see the survivor list). The serious problems are claims presented as disclosed or confirmed when they are derived, circular or selective. - [S1: 10-Q 0001996810-26-000148, statements and Notes 9/14/24] [S2: Q2'26 release -26-000147; FY25 10-K -26-000015] - The CFO claim is wrong as F01 states it. The two sources conflict; they do not agree "exactly". - The 8-K says McDonough becomes CFO effective 1 Jan 2027, and Parks becomes strategic advisor from that date. - GEV's press release says Parks "will continue as GE Vernova's CFO through 2026 inclusive of the third and fourth quarter earnings calls." - So Parks is slated to present the late-January call, but McDonough holds the CFO title on that date. - [S1: 8-K -26-000153 Item 5.02, 2026-08-27] [S2: gevernova.com CFO-transition press release, 2026-08-27] [S3: CNBC 2026-08-28, "staying on… through its next two earnings calls"] - "Consensus implies FY27 Power 21.7–23.5%" is a back-solve, not a consensus figure. No free segment consensus exists. - D01A derives 21.5–23.5% (F01 silently changed this to 21.7%) by assuming Electrification at 21–22%. - The only published figure is GLJ's 20.7%. That sits below F01's range and only 0.2–0.7 points above the builds' 20.0–20.5%. - [S1: D01A §1] [S2: evidence_brief.md "20.7%… GLJ's figure only"] - The equipment-margin "hand re-derivation ties exactly" is circular. Equipment EBITDA is calculated as Power EBITDA minus the estimated services EBITDA, so the 17.63% check is guaranteed to tie. The 0.0% level comes entirely from four assumptions. - [S1: F01 Q2 steps 1–8] [S2: 10-Q Note 24 footnote (b): segment costs exclude D&A; no cost split is disclosed] - "Consensus is above trend" depends on which trend you pick. - The recent pace (+6 to +10 points a year) gives the F01 result. - The FY23→H1'26 average of the same E01 series (~+11 points a year) gives 13.75% (from E01's 0% base) to 17.35% (from D06's 3.6% base) by FY27. Most of consensus's 12–18% requirement then sits on trend. - [computed §4-B; inputs E01 §1, D06] - "Never cut" is weaker than F01 says. Wind was cut at Q3'25 to "~$400M" of losses, and then missed that figure: FY25 Wind EBITDA was −$598M. - [S1: Q3'25 release -25-000159 guidance section] [S2: Q4'25 release -26-000012 Wind table; FY25 10-K p.72]

    G2. On FY26 consensus, the FY27 margin step (+4.41 points) is smaller than the FY26 step already assumed (+5.34). The largest delivered step is +2.57 points [§4-B; MS; 10-K]. - G7. The Q4'25 call confirms analysts already track backlog margin ("17 points of improvement since year-end '22"). The variant is not information-based [chunk 246150; Q4'25 release "equipment margin in backlog expanding six points"]. - G11. H2'26 commitments are "directionally 20 GW… likely conservative" after 40 GW in H1. Slots are being sold for 2032; 12 GW of 2030–31 supply was added "at premium pricing" [earningscalls.dev Laguna copy 09-16; Q2 release]. - G17. On the CFO handover, the Q4 call is a Parks call under a McDonough title. The guiding style on the FY27 outlook therefore likely stays Parks'. This weakens "new-CFO reset" framing in either direction [8-K; PR]. - G20. Equipment margin = equipment EBITDA ÷ (segment-note equipment revenue + intersegment revenue)

    Caveats, which the team must state on the chart: 1. RPO includes nuclear, hydro and steam equipment, but GW counts gas turbines only. This biases backlog $/kW up. 2. RPO excludes revenue already recognised on over-time contracts, while GW counts full units until shipped. This biases backlog $/kW down. 3. Revenue per kW shipped includes non-gas equipment revenue and over-time revenue not tied to shipments. That makes it a scaling ratio, not a price. 4. Aeroderivative mix: Q2'26 shipped 16 aero of 29 units, and the Q2'26 order mix was aero- and combined-cycle-heavy [S1: 10Q-2Q26 p.29 units] [S2: CALL-2Q26 src:3161, "higher dollar per kW price in orders, given a higher mix of aeroderivatives"]. 5. Firm GW are rounded integers: ±0.5 GW moves Q2'26 backlog $/kW by about ±$7.

    Arithmetic

    A1. Cushion equivalents (research estimates; the team chooses its own number) - FY26 Street vs current guide midpoint: - 46.0B × 13% = 5,980. Street 6,359 / 5,980 = 1.0634. - FY27 equivalent: 9,574 / 1.0634 = 9,003, i.e. 17.07% on 52,740. - FY26 Street vs first guide midpoint (ex-Prolec): - First guide midpoint: 41.5B × 12% = 4,980. - Prolec estimate: 3,100 × 22% = 682 (both are assumptions: ~$3.1B from Q2REL; 22% from D10). - Street ex-Prolec: 6,359 − 682 = 5,677. Ratio 5,677 / 4,980 = 1.140. - FY27 equivalent: 9,574 / 1.14 = 8,398, i.e. 15.92%. - FY24 bonus cushion: 9,574 / 1.0175 = 9,409 (17.84%). - FY25 bonus cushion: 9,574 / 1.102 = 8,688 (16.47%). - FY28 premium: 13,064 / 11,200 = 1.166. Applied to FY27: 9,574 / 1.166 = 8,211 (15.6%).

    A2. Margin guide in dollars (on revenue of 52,740) - 17% → 8,966; 18% → 9,493 (−0.8% vs consensus); 19% → 10,021.

    A3. Horizon noise - Realised: 3.34% × √81 = 30.1%. - Implied: σ = 0.108 / (0.798 × √(30/365)) = 0.108 / 0.2288 = 47.2%. The 37-DTE expiry gives 0.124 / (0.798 × 0.3184) = 48.8%. (Assumes expected move ≈ ATM straddle ≈ 0.798σ√t; THETA does not state its method.) - Implied over 81 sessions: 47.2% × √(81/252) = 26.8%. - P(profit) ≈ Φ(4.3 / 26.8) = Φ(0.160) = 56.4%; Φ(4.3 / 30.1) = Φ(0.143) = 55.7%.

    A4. Probability of touching the stop (driftless, reflection principle) - ln(1,078.8 / 962.49) = 0.1141. - P = 2 × [1 − Φ(0.1141 / σ_T)]: - σ_T 0.268 → 2 × (1 − Φ(0.426)) = 2 × 0.335 = 0.670. - σ_T 0.301 → 2 × (1 − Φ(0.379)) = 0.705. - A −4.3% drift in the short's favour lowers this modestly. Not computed exactly.

    Kill-rule and pass-mark design for Q3 (10-28) and January

    GEV kill rules, pass marks and price stops for the two candidate pitches (research input; the team sets every threshold)

    What we asked

    Read F01_final_synthesis first (list_overnight_outputs / read_overnight_output), then whatever earlier outputs you need. Everything you produce is research input; elements and facts only, never memo prose.

    Design precise, measurable kill rules and pass marks for both candidate pitches, taking into account the guidance cushion (E04: a 16.5-17.8% FY27 margin guide can still be consistent with consensus), the bundled positives (E05), the volatility, and the Q3 print on 2026-10-28. For each: the reported line, the threshold, the date, and the evidence for why that threshold (not another) separates "thesis right" from "thesis wrong". Include a price-based stop and explain how to choose its level from GEV's realised volatility. Research options with trade-offs; the team chooses.

    Bottom line

    A kill rule based on the FY27 margin guide alone cannot tell "thesis right" from "thesis wrong". Management has historically beaten its own guides, so a guide below consensus can still be consistent with consensus being met. That cushion is wider than E04 found. - E04's two completed years: actual adj EBITDA beat the bonus target (set at about the guide midpoint) by +1.75% (FY24) and +10.2% (FY25) [S1: DEF 14A 0001996810-25-000049 p.54; DEF 14A 0001996810-26-000049 p.50] [S2: 4Q24 release 0001996810-25-000004; 4Q25 release 0001996810-26-000012]. - FY26 adds a third, larger data point. The January 2026 guide midpoint was $5,340M ($44.5B × 12%). The current guide midpoint is $5,980M, which is +12.0%. Consensus is $6,359M, which is +19.1% [S1: 0001996810-26-000012 EX-99 "expects revenue of $44-$45 billion… 11%-13%"] [S2: news corpus src:27, 2026-01-23; current guide from Q2REL 0001996810-26-000147; consensus from MS and ChartMill $6.4B]. - Dividing consensus FY27 ($9,574M) by these cushions gives the guide midpoint that would still be consistent with consensus: $9,409M, $8,688M, $8,548M and $8,039M. On consensus revenue that is 17.84%, 16.47%, 16.21% and 15.24%. - The research proposal is a three-zone January test, measured in dollars, not margin points. Dollars = revenue-guide midpoint × margin-guide midpoint. - Thesis-wrong zone (short killed): midpoint ≥ ~$9.4B. - Ambiguous zone: ~$8.55–9.4B. - Thesis-right zone: ≤ ~$8.55B, i.e. below every observed cushion except the FY26 consensus-implied one. - Mapped onto D04B's margin distribution, this gives roughly 35% / 45% / 20% (research judgement; see A3). About half the time the January call will not settle the thesis. A second dated test is needed: the 2028 framework at the January call or the spring CMD. - The Q3 print on 2026-10-28 is a gate, not a verdict. The line that has moved the stock is the company margin guide. - The three margin or framework raise days closed +13.75%, +14.58% and +15.62%. Q2'26, a revenue and FCF raise with the margin guide held, closed −8.69% [S1: BX-13, Yahoo/Nasdaq closes] [S2: D07 citing Reuters/MoneyTimes 2026-07-22; Barron's 2025-12-12]. - Pass marks should sit on the FY26 margin guide, Q3 EBITDA against the guide-implied $1,535–1,716M, and Q3 Power margin against the 17–18% Q3 guide. - Volatility check. Since-spin daily σ is 3.34% (53% annualised) [S1: BX series] [S2: verifier 3.35%]. The 30-day close-to-close figure is 47.1% on 09-25 [S1: alphaquery] and the 20-day figure 50.3% on 09-16 [S2: thetaOwl]. Implied vol is about 45% (alphaquery 30-day mean IV 45.2%); the thetaOwl expected-move curve implies about 45–49%. - Over the 81 sessions to late January, that is 26.6–30.1% of 1σ noise. - F01's $1,079 short stop (+12.1%) gets hit before January about 62–70% of the time under zero-drift noise alone [computed A5]. A stop that pure noise hits only ~1/3 of the time sits at about +30–34% ($1,250–1,290). That is above the 52-week high of $1,195.94 and about 7x the central expected gain of +4.3% (E02). A pure price stop does not fit a thin edge, so the realistic choices are thesis-event exits plus sizing or defined-risk structures (options below). - For a 12-month long, any stop between −15% and −30% gets hit 45–76% of the time under noise alone [computed A6]. Two of the five post-spin drawdowns (−24.6% and −25.5%) would have triggered a −25% stop [S1: BX-07/08, Yahoo chart] [S2: Nasdaq historical, 626 sessions agree].

    Answers 3

    Kill rules and pass marks: SHORT into the late-January 2027 FY27 outlook

    Checkpoint 0: 10-23 finals. Nothing is reported before the finals. Every rule has to be pre-committed without seeing Q3.

    Checkpoint 1: Q3'26 on 10-28, 7:30 ET. FOMC is the same day and megacap reports fall around it, so noise stacks up [S1: GEV events page] [S2: earningscountdown, via F01].

A short can lose ~10–15% in one session on a margin-guide raise [BX-13]. - G17 (what management controls): guidance cushion (A1–A2); buyback authorisation timing; bundling of positives on the January call. - G18 (kill rule): §2. - G21 (what we would see if wrong): Q3 EBITDA ≥ ~$1,800M or Power ≥ 19.5% (above guide); a FY26 margin raise.

    Arithmetic

    A1, cushion ladder. 9,574 / 1.0175 = 9,409 (17.84%); / 1.102 = 8,688 (16.47%); / 1.120 = 8,548 (16.21%); / 1.191 = 8,039 (15.24%). Margins are on $52,740M. - A2, FY26 cushion. Jan-26 guide midpoint: 44.5 × 12% = 5,340. Current: 46.0 × 13% = 5,980, and 5,980 / 5,340 = 1.120. Consensus: 6,359 / 5,340 = 1.191. - Caveat: the Jan-26 guide includes Prolec for 11 months. I could not verify how much of the later raise was organic versus inorganic. - A3, zone probabilities from D04B (uniform within each bucket; research judgement): - Kill (≥17.84%): 30% + 22% + 8% plus 0.16 × 30% ≈ 35%. - Pass (≤16.21%): 5% + 10% + 0.21 × 25% ≈ 20%. - Ambiguous: ≈ 45%. - A4, FY26 raise to 13–14%. (13.5% × 46,000 − 2,146) / 25,558 = 4,064 / 25,558 = 15.9% H2 margin, vs consensus H2 16.3% [H1 figures: 10-Q / Q2REL]. - A5, barrier probability. P = 2[1 − Φ(ln(1+b) / (σ√T))]. - σ√T = 3.34% × √81 = 30.1%, or 47% / √252 × 9 = 26.6%. - Example, $1,079: ln 1.121 = 0.1142; 0.1142 / 0.301 = 0.379; Φ = 0.648; P = 70%. - Close-monitoring correction: shift the barrier by +0.5826 × σ_daily ≈ +1.9 points, giving 66%. - The ~1/3 tolerance needs z = 0.974, i.e. a barrier of 0.974 × 26.6–30.1% = 25.9–29.3% in log terms, or +29.6% to +34.0%. - A6, long. σ√T = 53% or 47%. Example, −25%: ln 0.75 = −0.2877; 0.2877 / 0.53 = 0.543; Φ = 0.706; P = 59%. - A7, implied Q3 event move (thetaOwl, 09-15; the straddle ≈ 0.8σ√t convention is an approximation): - Oct-16 base σ = (10.44 / 0.8) / √(31/365) = 44.8%. - Oct-30 variance = (13.9 / 0.8)² = 301.9. - Base variance over 44 days = 44.8² × 44/365 = 241.9. - Event sd = √60.0 = 7.7%. - A8, stop prices. (30 × 9,865 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $1,145. (28.2 × 9,865 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $1,079. (20 × 9,865 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $775. - A9, session counts. Oct 22 + Nov 20 + Dec 22 + Jan 1–27 17 = 81. Window 1 (09-30 to 10-27) = 20.

    What would change this

    FY27 guided in dollars with no margin figure: the zones apply directly. If only a margin range is given, convert using the revenue-guide midpoint, not consensus revenue. - A disclosed 2026 bonus target (proxy): would recalibrate the cushion. It is not available until spring 2027 (E04). - A live options chain showing IV well below 45%: narrows every stop grid. A spike toward 70% widens it. - Paid segment consensus putting FY27 Power ≤ 21%: move the Power kill line down to about 20.5%.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. "FY27 guide margin at or above ~18%" as the short's kill rule. It should be a dollar line at ≥ ~$9.4B (17.84% only at consensus revenue). A pass needs ≤ ~$8.55B, not just "below 18%".
    2. E04's 16.5–17.8% cushion band understates the ambiguity. FY26 extends it down to 15.2–16.2% (A1).
    3. F01's $1,079 stop. On volatility alone it has a ~62–70% chance of being hit before the thesis date.
    4. Consensus FY27 Power margin. GLJ's 20.7% conflicts with the builds' 21.7–23.5%. The Power line thresholds should sit below both.

    Consensus drift: is the Street already cutting FY27?

    GEV consensus revisions tracker, FY26–FY28 (research input, as of 2026-09-30)

    What we asked

    Read F01_final_synthesis first (list_overnight_outputs / read_overnight_output), then whatever earlier outputs you need. Everything you produce is research input; elements and facts only, never memo prose.

    Track how consensus FY27 (and FY26, FY28) revenue, adjusted EBITDA and EPS have moved over the last 6-9 months: MarketScreener snapshots, Zacks/Yahoo revision data, FactSet or LSEG figures quoted in press, analyst target changes (e.g. Jefferies cut to $1,185 on 2026-09-22). Two sources per datapoint. Answer: is the Street already moving FY27 down toward the research range ($8.6-8.9B)? If so, by the January call the surprise may be small — estimate how much of the gap could close before the guide, and what that does to the short's expected value.

    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    Bottom line

    The Street is not moving FY27 down toward $8.6–8.9B. - Over nine months, FY27 EPS rose +18.6% and revenue +7.1% [CN 01-29 → MS 09-29; cross-check YF, ZK]. - Since Q2 (07-23), FY27 EPS is flat: +0.3% (24.78 → 24.85) [CN 07-23; MS]. It is −0.3% on FactSet's own 09-02 figure (24.70) [MW, unverifiable]. - Since GLJ (09-14), the only visible drift is −0.7% in seven days on Yahoo (24.87 → 24.69) [YF], plus one trim (Erste 24.64 → 24.55) [tickerreport 09-23; ad-hoc-news 09-21]. - No free FY27 adjusted-EBITDA time series exists. EBITDA is observed at only two points, from two vendors: - GLJ's "Street $9.45B" (09-14) [GLJ; corpus 223189]; - MarketScreener's $9,574M (09-29) [MS]. - The 1.3% difference is best read as vendor dispersion, not a revision. The change in EBITDA below is inferred from EPS and revenue. - Revisions cluster in the one or two days after each print. Between prints they are flat. - FY27 EPS moved +11.0% from Jan to Apr, +6.5% from Apr to Jul, and +0.3% from Jul to Sep [CN; MS]. - A Q2'26 adjusted-EBITDA miss (−2.1% vs estimates [StockStory 07-22; Reuters 07-22 "below LSEG estimates"]) produced no FY27 cut. Yahoo's FY27 figure went 24.25 (90 days ago) → 24.36 (60 days ago) [YF], and the FactSet median target held at $1,254.50 [CN 07-23; MW 09-02]. - Correction to the brief: Jefferies raised, it did not cut. The target went $1,155 → $1,185 on 2026-09-11 (Buy) [StreetInsider 09-11; MarketScreener 09-11], and was reiterated on 09-17 [Investing.com 09-17]. The Bernstein target went $1,206 → $1,298 on 09-15 [evidence_lanes POS-23; Bitget/Zhitong 09-16/17]. No cuts to targets or FY27 estimates by major brokers were found for 09-14 to 09-29. - How much of the gap could close before the January guide: research estimate. - Gap from consensus to the midpoint of the research range is −$824M (−8.6%) [computed]. - Most likely pre-guide closure is 0–25% of that gap, mainly at the Q3 print on 10-28. P(≥50% closes) ≈ 15–20%. - This is research judgement from the clustering pattern. The team sets its own probabilities. - Effect on the short's expected value. Drift before the guide does not change the post-guide EBITDA, so the estimate part of the P&L measured from today's entry survives; it just arrives sooner. - What drift removes is the surprise-driven de-rating. With E02's frames, that takes the short's EV from +4.3% at f=0 to about +1.9% at f=0.5 and −0.6% at f=1 (f = fraction of the gap closed before the guide) [computed from E02 §Q1]. - Drift that happens before the team's entry date lowers the pitch's edge directly. Drift after entry mostly moves the timing.

    Is the Street moving FY27 down toward $8.6–8.9B?

    No. The evidence: 1. The last visible direction is flat. FY27 EPS is flat since 07-23, and −0.7% over seven days after GLJ [YF].     Q4

    What drift does to the short's expected value (E02 frames)

    • The post-guide EBITDA outcome is fixed by the guide itself. Pre-guide drift therefore shifts when the estimate part is paid, not whether.
    • What drift erodes is the de-rating on the day of the surprise. Taking "sticky" as the no-surprise frame, EV(f) ≈ 4.3% − f × 4.9pt:
    f Short EV
    0 +4.3%
    0.25 +3.1%
    0.5 +1.9%
    0.75 +0.6%
    1 −0.6%
    • Upper bound: if drift itself triggers revision-momentum de-rating (E02's "harsh" frame), the EV can rise toward +12%.
    • Probability-weighting f over the Q3 grid gives a research EV of about +3.5% to +4.0%. Negative-f (upward) outcomes feed into E02's own +0.8% Q3-beat case.
    • Timing trap: drift before the team's entry date is lost edge; drift after entry is P&L banked early.

    Bottom line

    The segment note does not split Power's costs between equipment and services. For Power it gives equipment revenue, services revenue, intersegment revenue, one combined cost-of-revenues line (excluding D&A), SG&A, R&D and "other segment items". Any equipment or services margin is therefore an inference. It rests on three numbers GEV does not disclose: 1. D&A inside cost of services (d); 2. Wind and Electrification services gross margins; 3. how Power's overhead (SG&A, R&D, other) is shared between equipment and services. [S1: FY25 10-K 0001996810-26-000015, "SEGMENT EBITDA" tables p.72–73] [S2: Q2'26 10-Q 0001996810-26-000148 p.23; FY24 10-K 0001996810-25-000011, same table] - Power services EBITDA margin comes out at about 19–35% across periods; my central case is 24–30%.
