    −31% −18% −8.5% −7% 0% 0%

    D06 had −27 / −13.5 / −4.8 / −2.5 / +3.6 / +4. My central is 3–5 points lower in every period. About 2.7 of those points come from one choice: D06 splits overhead by revenue share (services carry ~66%). I give services 58%, because the 10-K says only about half of R&D supports existing products and the installed base [S1: FY25 10-K p.7 "Research and Development"] [S2: FY25 10-K Note 24 R&D line 549 vs SG&A 1,836]. The rest comes from d and the non-Power services margins. - The finding that survives every assumption is the change, not the level. Implied equipment margin rose about 30–32 points from FY23 to H1'26 in all my scenarios (low, central and high). It also rose about 6–8 points year on year from H1'25 to H1'26 on the same recast basis. Over the same time, company-wide services gross margin fell, from 35.1% (FY23) to 31.3% (FY25) and 31.6% (H1'26), while Power's gross margin before D&A rose from 23.0% to 28.2%.     Q2

    What bounds Power's services margin

    AskedWhat constraints bound Power's services margin? Show the arithmetic.

    The identity is:

    Power services gross profit before D&A = company services gross profit (after D&A) + d − Wind services gross profit − Electrification services gross profit.

    Then:

    Power services EBITDA = Power services gross profit − the services share of Power overhead (SG&A + R&D + other).

    Parameter ranges I used: - d = 1.0% / 1.75% / 2.5% of company services revenue. FY25 that is $171M / $300M / $428M, against total D&A of $853M. - Wind services gross margin 20% / 10% / 0%. - Electrification services gross margin 40% / 32.5% / 25%. - Services share of overhead 66% / 58% / 50%.

    FY25 bounds: - Hard ceiling (not realistic): all D&A in cost of services and zero Wind/Electrification services profit gives (5,360 + 853) / 13,072 = 47.5% gross. - Realistic floor: Wind services 30%, Electrification services 45%, d = 0 gives 29.3% gross. Less 66% of overhead (11.3% of revenue) leaves ~18% EBITDA. - Realistic ceiling: d = 500, Wind services 0%, Electrification services 20% gives 41.5% gross. Less 50% of overhead (8.6% of revenue) leaves ~33%.

    Scenario results:

    Q2'26 24.3 / 29.5 / 34.7 +9.0 / −0.2 / −9.4

    A higher services margin means a lower equipment margin. Equipment margins are on equipment plus intersegment revenue.

    Sensitivities (FY25): - d ±$100M moves s by ∓0.8 points and e by ±1.5 points. - Overhead share ±1 point moves e by ∓0.33 points. - Wind services margin ±1 point moves e by ±0.28 points. - One point of s is worth about 2.0 points of e in FY25 and 1.7 points in H1'26 (the services/equipment revenue ratio).

    AskedDo management statements (YE2022 equipment backlog margin "approximately breakeven"; 2020 "low to mid single digit" equipment margins) agree with your derivation?

    Yes on direction. The size cannot be tested, because the metrics are defined differently.

    AskedWhat does the trend imply for FY27 equipment margin under the CEO's '27-and-beyond / '29-'30 timing, versus what FY27 consensus implicitly needs?

    Required equipment margin: e = (Power margin − w × s) / (1 − w), where w is the services share of Power revenue. H1'26 w was 63%. As equipment grows faster, a plausible FY27 w is 0.55–0.60 (research estimate).

    Arithmetic

    Power gross profit before D&A = segment revenue − cost of revenues: FY23 4,011; FY24 4,519; FY25 5,140; H1'25r 2,416; H1'26 2,945; Q2'26 1,611.

    Overhead = SG&A + R&D + other: 2,290 / 2,251 / 2,238 / 1,113 / 1,104 / 581. Each ties to reported EBITDA within $1M (for example, 5,140 − 2,238 = 2,902).

    Company services gross profit: 5,265 / 5,122 / 5,360 / 2,405 / 2,755 / 1,515.

    FY25 central case: 1. d = 0.0175 × 17,134 = 300; Wind services profit 0.10 × 1,858 = 186; Electrification services profit 0.325 × 2,168 = 705. 2. Power services gross profit = 5,360 + 300 − 186 − 705 = 4,770 (36.5%). 3. Services overhead = 0.58 × 2,238 = 1,298, so services EBITDA = 3,472 (26.6%). 4. Equipment EBITDA = 2,902 − 3,472 = −570, which is −8.5% of 6,696 (6,420 + 276). On external equipment revenue only it is −8.9%.

    H1'26 central case: 1. d = 153; Wind 117; Electrification 308. Power services gross profit = 2,482 (37.7%). 2. Services overhead = 640, so services EBITDA = 1,842 (27.9%). 3. Equipment EBITDA = 1,842 − 1,842 ≈ 0, which is 0.0% of 3,856.

    Low and high corners use the parameter sets in Q2. I recomputed each and they tie to segment EBITDA by construction.

    Reproducing D06's FY25 central case (d = 350, 25% blended non-Power services margin, overhead by revenue share): 5,360 + 350 − 1,006.5 = 4,703.5, which gives e = −4.79%. That confirms D06's arithmetic. Changing only the overhead share to 58% gives e = −7.5%.

    Q5 formula: e = (M − w × s) / (1 − w). Example: (20.7 − 0.6 × 28) / 0.4 = 9.75%.

    What would change this

    A disclosure of Wind or Electrification services margins, or of D&A inside cost of services. Early adoption of DISE (ASU 2024-03) would give an expense disaggregation. - A GEV statement of equipment EBITDA or contribution margin, for example on the January 2027 call or at the spring-2027 CMD. - Q3'26 10-Q, 2026-10-28, after the finals. If company services gross margin rises 2 points or more while Power margin is flat, the implied equipment margin falls. Power at 18% or more on equipment-led growth supports the steeper trend.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The assignment's premise that the segment note gives a cost split is wrong. It gives only a combined Power cost of revenues. The equipment/services split rests on three undisclosed parameters.
    2. D06's central equipment levels look 3–5 points too high, mainly because it splits overhead by revenue share. The 10-K R&D language supports a higher equipment share of overhead.
    3. The "breakeven" and "LSD-MSD" figures are contribution margins, which GE's 2019 deck states explicitly. They must not be compared directly with equipment EBITDA.
    4. The research files contradict each other. D06 quotes a deck footnote defining backlog margin as "contribution margin"; evidence_lanes says GEV "has never defined" it. I could not find the footnote in the corpus.
    5. The corpus labels the Q4'25 transcript 2026-01-23. The call and release were 2026-01-28.

    Q3

    Reward/risk ranking and how sensitive it is

    AskedWhich pitch has the best reward/risk, and how sensitive is that ranking to the probabilities?

    Ranking by central expected return: 1. (a) +4.3% 2. (b) +1.8% 3. (c) −1.8% 4. (d) −4.3%

    Sensitivity of (a): - Moving 12.9 points of probability from J4 to J1 (P(J1) ≈ 27%, P(J4) ≈ 19%) brings the expected return to zero. - So does moving 17 points from J4 to J2. - Switching from the central to the sticky-multiple frame (+1–2 turns per scenario) gives −0.6%. One turn on a ~9.4B NTM is about $35/share (3.7%). - Conclusion: (a) survives moderate probability error but not a market that keeps paying 28x NTM through January.

    Sensitivity of (b)/(c): - ±1 turn on the probability-weighted NTM of $11,451M is about ±$43 (±4.5%). That is larger than the +1.8% expected return. - Moving 5 points from T1 to T4 gives −0.7%. - The 12-month sign is not robust. This matches D10 ("no edge at 12 months") and V10 (median p_long 0.46; horizon sorts direction).

    Robust across frames: - (a) weakly dominates (d) in every frame except the sticky one. - (b) vs (c) is undetermined. - (a) vs (b) depends on whether the team believes the multiple compresses before January.

    Q4

    Short into January: target, stop/kill, and a Q3 beat

    AskedFor the short-into-January pitch: what target, what stop/kill level, and what happens if Q3 (10-28) beats before the January guide?

    Target (research range, team's choice). - Probability-weighted value given a miss: (0.34 × $913 + 0.32 × $785) / 0.66 ≈ $851 (−11.6%). - Range $785–913. At the harsh multiples: $687–843.

    Kill (event-based). Any one of: - FY27 guide low end ≥18%. - 2028 framework raised to ≥~$12.5B. - 2026 Power backlog-margin change well above +11 points together with a guide at or above 18%.

    Sources: [S1: D10 Q6 kill table; S2: V10 R9/R13, where 9 of 9 variants agree on ≥18%].

    Stop (price-based, research options). - $1,079 (+12.1%): consensus rolled at a constant 28.2x. If the stock trades there before January, the market is paying the roll with no de-rating, which is the short's mechanism failing. - Wider: $1,175 (record close) or $1,181 (J1 at 30x). - Unweighted payoff at the $851 target and $1,079 stop: +11.6% vs −12.1%, i.e. about 1:1. Taking the edge from probabilities (P(J3+J4) = 66%) is legitimate only if the team defends the 25.1x flat-price multiple.

    If Q3 beats on 10-28. - Definition used here: EBITDA well above $1,728M, Power ≥19%, Wind ≥ breakeven. - Mechanism: a higher FY26 exit shrinks the step to 18.15%. D04A §6 flags that FY26 ≥14% with Q4 ≥17% makes +4 points "consistent with history". - Research shift: 10 points from J4 to J2 and 5 from J3 to J1, giving 19 / 30 / 29 / 22. - Result: E[January price] ≈ $955, i.e. about +0.8% to a short from $962.49, with the edge almost gone. - If the stock also jumps (Q1'26 analogue: +13.75% when the margin guide was raised), the mark-to-market loss is realised before the guide. - A Q3 print that only reaffirms (the past two Q3s: +1.25%, −1.59%) leaves the table roughly intact. - The Q3 call may also "frame" 2027 early (as in Oct-2025, D04A G14). That shrinks the January surprise either way. A cautious framing on 10-28 would move part of the short's payoff into October.

    Q5

    Fit to the 3–12-month horizon and "model and thesis alignment"

    AskedWhich pitch best fits the competition's 3-12 month horizon and "model and thesis alignment" criterion?

    (a) Fits at about 4 months, the low end of the window. - Alignment is the strongest of the four: the model's one number (FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin, research base $8.6–8.9B, −8% to −10% vs $9,574M) is tested by a dated company event with a pass mark and a kill rule [S1: D10 §1; S2: V10 Q4]. - The model must value on a January NTM (11/12 FY27 + 1/12 FY28) and state the multiple assumption. The playbook says to "Match the valuation date to the judging horizon" [S1: winners_playbook Step 10; S2: LSPD case, "the variance does not fit the horizon"].

    (b) Fits at 12 months. - The research's own FY27 is below consensus, so a long must rest on the roll-forward and the multiple. That is a multiple bet on consensus numbers, the Valvoline pattern [S1: brief §9; S2: V06 "no view that differs from the Street"].

    (c) Fits at 12 months, but alignment is weakest. - An about −8% estimate gap cannot beat a +39% roll unless the multiple falls to about 20x. - The Deere winner lost exactly this way: earnings fell further than forecast, yet the stock rose on a higher multiple [S1: pitch corpus michigan-uic-2023-de; S2: winners playbook].

    (d) Contradicts the research's own guide distribution. Not aligned.

    General questions answered along the way

    G1 / G5: The price holds only if NTM EV/EBITDA falls to 25.1x by January or 20.3x by Sep-2027 on unchanged consensus (A0). If the stock goes nowhere for 12 months, either estimates held and the multiple fell about 28%, or estimates were cut about 12.5% and the multiple fell to about 23x [S1: D05 §1; S2: D03 §1]. - G8 / G23: An estimate gap of about −8% is worth about $60–90/share. The roll-forward is worth about +$218/share over Jan→Sep at 25x. The short's upside beyond the gap is a multiple assumption [S1: D10 §1; S2: V10 A4]. - G13 / G18: The late-January guide is the test. The short passes at a midpoint ≤17.0–17.5% and is killed by a low end ≥18% or a 2028 raise to ≥~$12.5B [S1: D10 Q6; S2: V10 R9]. - G14: Q3 framing on 10-28, a surprise December event, or the January date slipping into February could each move or shrink the reveal [S1: D04A G14; S2: IR, no December event]. - G15: Worst plausible outcomes: −23% (Jan short) to −39% (12-month short); −29% (Jan long) to −33% (12-month long). History: median drawdown −24.6%, maximum −38.3% [S1: BX; S2: Nasdaq].

Sep-2027 scenarios. - T1: NTM 2,425 + 9,975 = 12,400 → 25x $1,198.2; 28x $1,337.9. - T2: 2,325 + 9,600 = 11,925 → 22x $1,019.3. - T3: 2,200 + 8,625 = 10,825 → 21x $887.8; at 23x $969.1 (≈ today). - T4: 2,075 + 8,100 = 10,175 → 18x $721.9; 16x $645.5. - Consensus at 28.2x: (28.2 × 12,191 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $1,325.

    B2. 12-month expected value. - 0.25 × 1,198.2 + 0.30 × 1,019.3 + 0.30 × 887.8 + 0.15 × 721.9 = 299.6 + 305.8 + 266.3 + 108.3 = $980.0 (+1.82%). - Long gain/loss: 75.97 / 58.50 = 1.30. - One turn = 11,451 / 266.33 = $43.0. - Moving 5 points from T1 to T4: −0.05 × 476.3 = −$23.8 → $956.2.

    What would change this

    (a) ranked first: - The stock trading above ~$1,079 before January (the market paying the roll). - A Q3 beat accompanied by an FY26 margin-guide raise. - A December 2026 event being announced. - D04-type guide probabilities proving too bearish (for example, sell-side previews pointing to 18–19%). - 12-month coin-flip: - Evidence the multiple is sticky, for example a peer re-rating toward GEV's level. Current peers are about 21x US / 17.7x all-eight [D05]. - The CMD date and content becoming known. - Q3-beat math: my 15-point shift is research judgement. A larger shift (for example to 25 / 30 / 27 / 18) makes (a)'s expected value negative.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. "First FY27 guide under the new CFO." Parks presents the call [CFO-PR; CFOD]. Drop that leg.
    2. "Modest short, 55–60%." This holds only for a horizon ending shortly after January, where it is about 55%, and the expected edge exists only if the multiple compresses below 25.1x. At 12 months there is no edge.
    3. Brief §7 "value today" formula. It uses FY27 EBITDA. For a January target, the NTM should be 11/12 FY27 + 1/12 FY28. The difference is about +$30/share on consensus, since 9,865 vs 9,574 is worth 291 × m / 266.33.
    4. "Never cut." Qualify it: Wind was cut, and the FY24 margin midpoint was narrowed down 25bp [D04A §7].
    5. $530.16 is an intraday low. The closing low was $547.96 [evidence_brief].

    Executive incentives and guidance behaviour (proxy deep dive)

    GE Vernova (GEV): how bonus and PSU targets compare with public guidance, from the 2025 and 2026 proxies (research input only, not memo text)

    What we asked

    Read GEV's 2025 and 2026 proxy statements (DEF 14A: 0001996810-25-000049 and 0001996810-26-000049) in full on compensation. Tabulate for 2024 and 2025: every annual-incentive (AIP) metric, its threshold/target/ maximum, the actual result and the payout; every long-term (PSU) metric and its targets and measurement periods; and any 2026 targets disclosed. Then compare each year's AIP targets with the company guidance issued around the same time (e.g. the FY25 AIP EBITDA target vs the FY25 adjusted EBITDA guide). Answer: are bonus targets set at, below or above public guidance, and by how much? What does the pay design imply for how conservatively the FY27 guide (late January 2027) is likely to be set? Evidence only.

    Bottom line

    The annual bonus targets were set at public guidance, not below it. The adjusted EBITDA bonus target was about the guide midpoint in both years: FY24 target $2,000M against "mid-single digits toward the higher end" on $34–35B revenue; FY25 target $2,900M, 0.7% under the $2,920M mid-case of "high-single digits" on $36–37B. The free cash flow (FCF) target sat at the top of the guide both years, 11.1% above the midpoint ($1,000M vs $0.7–1.1B; $2,500M vs $2.0–2.5B). The organic-growth target (5.0%, 5.2%) sat in the upper half of the growth the revenue guide implied. [S1: DEF 14A 0001996810-25-000049, p.54 table] [S1: DEF 14A 0001996810-26-000049, p.50 table] [guides S2: GE 8-K 0000040545-24-000024 (2024-01-23); GEV 1Q24 8-K 0001996810-24-000004; Dec-2024 investor update PDF; Reuters 2024-12-11] - Payouts beat target both years, and the size of each leg's beat mirrors the guidance pattern. - FCF paid 170% in 2024 and 200% (above maximum) in 2025. Actuals were +70% and +48% over target. - Adjusted EBITDA paid only 104% and 130%, on actuals +1.75% and +10.2% over target. - Organic growth paid 131% and 178%. - This is the brief's "beats are cash and revenue, not margin" pattern, now in the pay record. [S1: proxy tables above] [S2: 4Q24 release 0001996810-25-000004; 4Q25 release 0001996810-26-000012] - Payouts to the executives: the business-performance factor was 136% (2024) and 157% after a −10pt safety modifier (2025). The CEO was paid 164% of target in 2024 and was capped at 200% in 2025. [S1: 2025 proxy p.55; 2026 proxy p.53] [S2: AFL-CIO Paywatch, 2024 incentive $3,206,385; Creately/SEC extract, 2025 incentive $4.50M] - The bonus targets were not easy against the prior year. - FY24 targets were 2.5x FY23 adjusted EBITDA ($807M) and 2.3x FY23 FCF ($442M). - FY25 thresholds were about 18% above FY24 actuals. - So the slack comes from the guidance itself, not from targets set below guidance. [computed §4] - No 2026 targets are disclosed. - The 2026 bonus and 2026–28 PSU values are not in the 2026 proxy (searched "2026 AIP", "2026 PSU", "2026-2028", "for 2026"; only 2026 peer-group changes appear). - PSU targets for 2024–26 and 2025–27 are withheld until each period ends. The 2024–26 targets should appear in the spring-2027 proxy, after the January 2027 guide. [S1: 2025 proxy p.55; 2026 proxy p.53] [SINGLE-SOURCE per document; checked both proxies and the 10-K Note 17, which gives no targets] - What this means for reading the FY27 guide (arithmetic, not a forecast): - If the FY27 guide carries the same cushion as FY24–25 (actual EBITDA 1.8–10.2% above the bonus target), a guide midpoint of $8.69–9.41B, or 16.5–17.8% margin on consensus revenue, is consistent with consensus $9,574M still being hit. - A sub-18% FY27 margin guide therefore does not by itself show consensus is too high. This bears directly on the brief's proposed kill rule (FY27 guide margin at or above ~18%). [computed §4]

    Answers 6

    Q1

    2024 annual incentive (AEIP; renamed "AIP" in the 2026 proxy)

    Design: - The GE compensation committee approved the goals before the spin, and GEV's own compensation committee (CHCC) ratified them in early 2024. - Payout is 50% at threshold, 100% at target and 200% at maximum, linearly interpolated. - A safety and sustainability modifier adds or subtracts up to 10pts; it is applied additively. An individual performance factor (IPF) ranges 0–150%. Total payout is capped at 200%. [S1: 2025 proxy pp.49–50] [S2: 2025 proxy p.3 program summary, a separate section of the same document; also 424B3 0001996810-25-000052]

    Q3

    PSUs

    • 2024 PSUs (2024–26):
    • Metrics: 50% cumulative adjusted EBITDA, 50% cumulative FCF, with a relative-TSR modifier of ±20% against the S&P 500 Industrials. The modifier cuts below the 20th percentile and adds above the 80th; TSR is measured from the spin.
    • Payout 50/100/200%. Targets are not disclosed until the period ends. [S1: 2025 proxy pp.51, 55] [S2: 2025 proxy p.3 summary]
    • 2025 PSUs (2025–27):
    • Same metrics, but the relative-TSR bands moved to at/below the 25th and at/above the 75th percentile. Both bands are now easier to trigger.
    • Targets are not disclosed. [S1: 2026 proxy pp.46, 53] [S2: 2026 proxy p.39 summary]

    Arithmetic

    Payout interpolation - Payout = 100 + (actual − target)/(max − target) × 100 above target. - FY24 FCF: 100 + 701/1,000 × 100 = 170.1%. - FY24 EBITDA: 100 + 35/1,000 × 100 = 103.5%. - FY24 organic growth: 34,771/32,630 − 1 = 6.561%, so 100 + 1.561/5 × 100 = 131.2%. - FY25 FCF: $3,710M is above the $3,500M maximum, so 200%. - FY25 EBITDA: 100 + 296/1,000 × 100 = 129.6%. - FY25 organic growth: 37,818/34,608 − 1 = 9.275%, so 100 + 4.075/5.2 × 100 = 178.4%.

    Targets vs guide - FCF: 1,000/900 = 1.111; 2,500/2,250 = 1.111. - FY24 EBITDA grid (5–6% × $34–35B): $1,700–2,100M. Target margin 2,000/34,500 = 5.80%. - FY25 EBITDA grid (7–9% × $36–37B): $2,520–3,330M. Mid-case 8% × 36.5 = $2,920M; target/mid = 0.993. - Implied revenue growth: FY24 34/33.239 = +2.29% to 35/33.239 = +5.30%. FY25 36/34.935 = +3.05% to 37/34.935 = +5.91%.

    Targets vs prior-year actuals - FY24 targets: 2,000/807 = 2.48x; 1,000/442 = 2.26x. - FY25 thresholds: 2,400/2,035 = +17.9%; 2,000/1,701 = +17.6%. - FY25 targets: +42.5% (EBITDA), +47.0% (FCF).

    Actual vs target - EBITDA: 2,035/2,000 = +1.75%; 3,196/2,900 = +10.2%. - FCF: +70.1%; +48.4%.

    FY27 cushion grid - Implied guide midpoint = consensus $9,574M / (1 + cushion). - 1.75% cushion → $9,409M = 17.84% of $52,740M consensus revenue. - 10.2% cushion → $8,688M = 16.47%.

    PSU context (inference; targets undisclosed) - 2025–27 cumulative FCF before FY27 = 3,710 + 11,500–12,500 = $15.2–16.2B. That already exceeds the Dec-2024 framework of at least $14B for all four years 2025–28, the plan in force when the 2025 PSU targets were set. - 2024–26 cumulative FCF = 1,701 + 3,710 + 11,500–12,500 = $16.9–17.9B. - 2024–26 cumulative adj EBITDA = 2,035 + 3,196 + (12% × 45.5 = 5,460 to 14% × 46.5 = 6,510) = $10.7–11.7B.

Parks' 2027 bonus is fixed at target, so he has no stake in FY27 results. - Kill rule "FY27 guide margin ≥ ~18%": the pay record implies the guide is normally set 2–10% below the eventual actual. That lowers the jump-off base [D07 Q2/Q6]. 3. Q3 10-Q equipment-RPO 1-year conversion flat or falling (history 41→37→38→36%) [D07 Q6]. 4. A management statement on 10-28 framing FY27 as "on the path to the 2028 framework", i.e. linear. 5. No December event and no 2027 preview on the Q3 call. 6. Buy-side positioning or survey evidence that the "whisper" is at or above consensus (not found). If the whisper is already ~17%, a 17% guide is priced in and the short fails. 7. Option-implied vol through January (not found). If well below 53%, the signal-to-noise problem shrinks. 8. Idiosyncratic σ vs a peer basket (not computed). The GLJ-day excess vs peers was only −3% [brief §5]. A peer-hedged framing would strip the sector and AI beta that dominates the noise in (a).

    Red-team: why the 12-month LONG thesis fails

    GEV: red-team of the 12-month long ($962.49, 2026-09-29 close)

    What we asked

    You are a hostile PM. The alternative thesis: long GEV from $962.49 for 12 months on the +39% NTM EBITDA roll-forward, the raise record, sold-out competitors, Electrification strength and a spring-2027 Capital Markets Day. Destroy it with evidence: de-rating to peer multiples (US grid ~21x, all-peer median ~17.7x), the GE 2000-2002 precedent (42.6x to 21.1x while EPS rose 19%), AI-capex sentiment, gas-turbine cycle history, SRA conversion (54% of GW is reservations), deposit-funded cash, fixed-price contracts with no escalation found, services profit revisions, Wind, tariffs. Assign probabilities; name the most likely failure; list what evidence would make the long robust.

    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    This is research input only. Every probability is a research judgement, and every forecast is a research estimate. The team chooses its own numbers and writes its own prose.

    Source key - 10Q = 10-Q 0001996810-26-000148 (2026-07-22) - PR2Q / PR1Q / PR4Q / PR3Q25 = GEV earnings releases (8-K exhibits) -26-000147, -26-000063, -26-000012, -25-000159 - 10K = 10-K 0001996810-26-000015 - T2Q = Q2'26 call transcript (corpus src:3161) - D02 / D05 / V07 / V08 = earlier outputs tonight, which carry their own primary citations - FACTS = facts.csv

    Bottom line

    The multiple drives the result, and peer multiples take away most of the gain from rolling forward to Sep-2027 estimates. - At the US grid-peer median of ~21x NTM EV/EBITDA on consensus NTM EBITDA of $12,191M, the stock is worth about $995 (+3%). At the all-peer median of ~17.7x it is worth about $844 (−12%). - On management's own plan path (NTM $10,794M), the same two multiples give about $885 (−8%) and about $752 (−22%) [computed, §4-A]. - Sources: peer multiples [S1: MarketScreener valuation pages 2026-09-29, via D05] [S2: TIKR cross-checks on Vertiv and Schneider, 2026-08-25, via D05]. Most peer EV/EBITDA figures are [SINGLE-SOURCE: MarketScreener]. - The +39% roll-forward rests on the least reliable number in the model. That number is consensus FY28 EBITDA of $13,064M, which is 16.6% above management's own 2028 plan of $11.2B. - Consensus [S1: MarketScreener, FACTS CT-02] [S2: stockanalysis, per V07]. Plan [S1: PR4Q] [S2: news source N27, per V08]. - On the plan path the roll-forward is +23%, not +39% [computed]. - The GE precedent shows the pattern the long cannot rule out: gas-turbine earnings kept rising while the multiple halved. - GE's P/E went from 42.6x to 21.1x while EPS rose 19% [S1: GE 2000 and 2002 ex-99b on SEC] [S2: NY Post 2002-04-16; Blackwell case, via D05]. - Power Systems earnings rose 29% in 2002 and fell only in 2003: "The subsequent 2003 decline in shipments was reflected in the $0.14 per share drop" [S1: GE 2003 10-K ex13, sec.gov/…/000004054504000013/ex13.htm] [S2: GE dex99b, sec.gov/…/000119312504053388]. - Research probabilities for the long over 12 months:

    Outcome Probability
    Return > +10% ~22%
    Return < −10% ~25%
    Return > 0 ~55–64%
    Probability-weighted return about +1% before net-cash build, about +4% after
    • Computed from a 3×3 estimate × multiple grid (§4-B). The result is near market-like with a fatter left tail. On the evidence the long is a poor risk/reward rather than a broken thesis. The team should not claim it has been "destroyed".
    • Most likely failure (single largest grid cell, ~18%): the business delivers and the stock goes nowhere.
    • The FY27 outlook lands below Street's 18.15% margin (a mild cut), and the multiple settles at 21–23x. Result: roughly −4% to +3% after 12 months.
    • This matches how the stock has reacted to raises that came without a margin raise: −8.69% on Q2'26 and −4.45% on Q2'24 [S1: Yahoo/Nasdaq closes, FACTS BX-13] [S2: D05 event table].
    • Several of the listed attack lines are weak as FY27 EBITDA arguments.
    • Tariffs are small: $100–200M in 2026 [S1: 10Q MD&A] [S2: Reuters 2026-07-22].
    • SRAs mostly deliver in 2029 and later, so SRA conversion is a multiple/narrative risk, not a FY27 EBITDA risk.
    • The strong attack lines are the multiple, the plan-vs-Street gap, AI-capex sentiment, and FCF normalisation.

    Answers 12

    Q1

    De-rating to peer multiples

    Formula: price = (multiple × NTM EBITDA + $9,113M net cash) / 266.33M shares. Net cash is held at the Q2'26 level; see Q7 for the build.

    Sep-27 NTM EBITDA 25x 22x 21x (US grid) 17.7x (all-peer) 15.6x (GEV Apr-25 trough) 12.6x (Siemens Energy)
    $12,191M consensus $1,179 (+22%) $1,041 (+8%) $995 (+3%) $844 (−12%) $748 (−22%) $611 (−37%)
    $11,277M (−7.5%) $1,093 (+14%) $966 (0%) $923 (−4%) $784 (−19%) — —
    $10,794M plan path $1,047 (+9%) $926 (−4%) $885 (−8%) $752 (−22%) — —
    • Today's multiple is 28.2x NTM (MarketScreener-based) or 27.7x (Chartloom) [D05].
    • Peer medians: US grid ≈21x (PWR 22.0x, ETN 21.3x, VRT 20.6x, HUBB 15.1x); all eight peers ≈17.7x [S1: MarketScreener] [S2: TIKR for VRT (~24x) and Schneider (~17x) only]. [SINGLE-SOURCE] for the others.
    • Counter-point: GEV has the highest 2-year EBITDA CAGR in the set (43.3%, MarketScreener). On EV/EBITDA-to-growth it is 0.65, about the same as Vertiv at 0.64 [D05]. So a de-rating to peer median needs a story change, not just mean reversion.
    • Evidence that a story change can happen fast: the NTM EV/EBITDA went from 33x to 15.6x between Jan and Apr 2025 [S1: Chartloom, SINGLE-SOURCE for the series] [S2: price closes via Yahoo/Nasdaq, FACTS BX-04].
    Q2

    The GE 2000–02 precedent

    • GE peaked at $60 in Aug-2000, which was 42.6x FY01 EPS of $1.41. It traded at $31.85 on 2002-04-15, which was 21.1x FY02 EPS of $1.51 [sources as in the bottom line, via D05].
    • GE Power Systems was 16% of three-year revenue and 21% of earnings. It was hit by "the U.S. power bubble… peaking during 2002" [S1: GE 2003 10-K ex13] [S2: GE 2004 dex99b, same wording].
    • In Q1 2003, GE revenue was down 1%, "reflecting lower U.S. gas turbine sales at Power Systems" [S1: GE Q1'03 release, ge.com] [S2: GE ex99a, sec.gov/…/000004054503000056].
    • Sequence: 1. Multiple compressed from Aug-2000. 2. Segment earnings peaked in 2002 (+29%). 3. Earnings fell in 2003.

    The de-rating ran roughly 1.5–2 years ahead of the earnings decline. - Caveat: the de-rating also reflected the conglomerate, Enron-era trust and the "Welch premium" [D05, NY Post; Inc. 2002-10-01]. It is not a clean gas-cycle test. - Scale then vs now: GE shipped ">60 GW" in 2001 [SINGLE-SOURCE: web analysis, corpus src:296]. GEV targets 20–24 GW, rising toward 30 GW by 2030 [S1: PR2Q] [S2: T2Q]. Today's capacity discipline is tighter, which works against the bust analogy.

    Q3

    AI-capex sentiment

    • GEV's direct exposure is 20% of GW under contract ("~80% are traditional customers and 20% are for data centers") [S1: T2Q p.3] [S2: web analysis, corpus src:238]. Indirect exposure through utility load forecasts is larger but not quantified.
    • 2026-09-14 had a co-driver the GLJ framing leaves out. The heads of the model provider, OpenAI and xAI called for slowing AI development. Chip stocks fell 3–7%, and a Reuters source said: "Markets are punishing the picks-and-shovels layer harder" [S1: Reuters via KRRO 2026-09-15] [S2: Gate News 2026-09-14; CNBC 2026-09-14 via V08].
    • Other shocks since mid-August:
    • WSJ report of ~$3T in off-balance-sheet AI commitments; GEV, Vertiv and Bloom all fell [S1: Startup Fortune 2026-09-03] [S2: 24/7 Wall St, via D05 (GEV −6% on 08-18)].
    • Three data-center-related IPOs were delayed [S1: Bisnow 2026-09-22, citing the NYT] [S2: NYT, not read directly].
    • Hyperscaler capex is still rising: ~$795B in 2026 and ~$1.08T in 2027 (BofA) [S1: Reuters 2026-09-15] [S2: Gate News (~$700B figure; definitions differ)].
    • Precedent: the DeepSeek sell-off (−21.5% in one day) "proved to be a short-lived hiccup" [S1: Reuters 2026-09-15] [S2: Chartloom trough-to-peak recovery by Aug-25, D05].
    • Takeaway: sentiment shocks are frequent and large, but so far they have reversed.
    Q4

    Gas-turbine cycle history

    • 1997–2002: orders peaked in 2002, then about 46 GW was cancelled between Nov-2001 and Aug-2002 [V07: Power Engineering 2002-09; PEi 2002].
    • 2006–16: GE averaged about 20 GW a year [SINGLE-SOURCE: src:296].
    • 2017–18: GE Power profit fell 45% after a bullish guide against flat demand [V07: Reuters 2018-02-23; POWER 2018-02-28].
    • In both busts, earnings broke only after orders turned. No order turn is visible yet: the CEO says 2031 slots are more than half sold by year-end [T2Q p.3] [S2: Laguna via MarketBeat, V07].
    • The one early warning: H2'26 signings are set to roughly halve (Q5).
    Q5

    SRA conversion (54% of GW is reservations)

    Quarterly roll [S1: PR3Q25, PR4Q, PR1Q, PR2Q bullets] [S2: T2Q p.3 for Q2]:

    Quarter SRA opening New SRAs Converted SRA closing Conversion % of opening Firm new orders Shipped Backlog
    Q3'25 25 12 7 29 28% 1 4 29→33
    Q4'25 29 21 8 43 28% 3 3 33→40
    Q1'26 43 19 6 56 14% 2 4 40→44
    Q2'26 56 18 10 63 18% 2 3 44→53

    Findings: - No SRA cancellations are visible. The roll residuals (−1, +1, 0, −1 GW) look like rounding. - Nearly all new demand enters as SRAs. Firm direct orders were 8 GW over four quarters, against 70 GW of new SRAs [computed]. - The 10-K flags conversion as a risk: - "slot reservation agreements may not result in orders" (10K Item 1A, offset ~65k). - "some counterparties… may not place orders equal to the value of their reservation amount or at all" (10K Item 1A, offset ~80.8k). - Both quotes are from the same filing, so they are one source. The SRA-share comparison is confirmed by Siemens Energy's Q3 FY26 presentation p.6 (GEV 54.3% of GW vs Siemens Energy 27.4%) [FACTS RQ-16]. - Deposit terms: the deposit is "non-refundable… credited toward the final purchase price" [SINGLE-SOURCE: web analysis src:238]. A second example is Maxim Power's 7HA.02 reservation with a non-refundable deposit (web, src:3490). No GEV filing states the deposit size or its refundability. - Dated test: the CEO says H2'26 will be the point "where orders in backlog will be greater than gigawatts on slot reservation agreement" [T2Q, Strazik, 2026-07-22]. - Meeting ≥125 GW with backlog above SRAs needs backlog ≥62.5 GW. - Assuming ~10 GW shipped in H2 (research assumption from the 20 GW run-rate), that needs ~19.5 GW of H2 conversions plus orders. H1 delivered 20 GW. - Gross H2 signings implied by 125 GW are only ~19 GW, against 41 GW in H1 [computed]. The "peak orders" headline risk is real. - Timing: the Q3 print on 2026-10-28 is after the finals. - FY27 impact is limited. SRAs mostly deliver in 2029 and later, so conversion misses hit the multiple and the orders narrative, not FY27 EBITDA (research inference).

    Q6

    Fixed-price contracts, no escalation

    • Equipment is fixed-price. The filing says GEV enters "contracts that commit to a fixed price well before project completion." In the FY25 10-K, "escalation" appears only in the lease note [S1: 10K Item 1A] [S2: FY24 10-K -25-000011, same language, via D02].
    • Customer evidence: a $25M LG&E/KU reservation was paid "to lock in firm pricing" [S1: KY PSC order 2025-10-28] [S2: evidence brief].
    • Services escalate only at a fixed rate: "annual 2.5% escalation" in a 2019 CSA [SINGLE-SOURCE: Talen 8-K/EX 0001622536-25-000013].
    • Implication: margin on the older backlog cannot be repaired by escalation clauses. This supports GLJ's view on timing.
    Q7

    Deposit-funded cash

    • Balances at 6/30/26 [S1: 10Q balance sheet] [S2: 10Q Note 9 table; IR deck src:3159 repeats it]:
    • Contract liabilities $39,944M (Power $27,679M, of which $25,799M is equipment).
    • Cash $13,120M; equity $13,115M.
    • Contract liabilities are about 3.0x cash [computed].
    • H1'26 cash:
    • The deposit line was $13,695M of $10,680M operating cash flow. OCF excluding it was −$3.0B [FACTS; brief §3].
    • Treasury stock rose from $3,385M to $7,057M, i.e. ~$3.67B of H1 buybacks funded while OCF excluding deposits was negative [computed from 10Q balance sheet; average price $854.43, FACTS].
    • FY27 consensus FCF is $7,417M, down 38% [SINGLE-SOURCE: MarketScreener].
    • Offset the long can claim: net cash still builds. Implied H2'26 FCF is about $2.1B at the guide midpoint, and FY27 Q1–Q3 is about $5.6B at consensus. That is ~$7.7B, or +$29/share (+3%), by Sep-2027 [computed].
    Q8

    Services profit revisions

    • Net unfavourable CSA profitability changes:
    Period Change
    FY24 −$319M
    FY25 −$151M
    H1'26 −$218M

    Sources: [S1: 10Q Note 9] [S2: 10K Note 9 (FY25 −$151M); FACTS RQ-13]. - Trend: H1'26 alone already exceeds the whole of FY25. This cuts against the services-pricing narrative. - Scale: it is small against $9.6B of EBITDA. It works as a quality signal more than an estimate driver.

    Q9

    Wind

    • Q2'26 Wind orders were −40% organic, and losses widened [S1: PR2Q via MarketScreener] [S2: Utility Dive 2026-07-23].
    • Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.25B against a $1.28B estimate, a miss driven by Wind [S1: Reuters 2026-07-22] [S2: Investing.com, FACTS RQ-32].
    • The ~−$400M FY26 Wind guide needs a +$257M H2 improvement [FACTS RQ-10]. Wind missed its final FY25 guide by $198M [FACTS BR-42; PR4Q].
    • Vineyard Wind settled on confidential terms [FACTS RQ-11: GEV release; Boston Globe].
    • Takeaway: repeated Wind misses are a credible Q3/Q4 risk. Company-level guidance has absorbed them before.
    Q10

    Tariffs

    • 2026 tariff cost is $100–200M, down from $250–350M, with FY25 actual ~$250M [S1: 10Q MD&A] [S2: Reuters 2026-07-22].
    • That is ≤2% of FY27 consensus EBITDA. Tariffs are noise for this thesis.
    • The Q2 call noted that pre-tariff onshore orders "had fewer contractual protections" [D02, T2Q; single-source inference].
    Q11

    Rebutting the long's other pillars

    • Competitors are "sold out", but capacity is rising.
    • Siemens Energy goes from ~110 to ~160 units a year and reaches 210–230 in FY28–30 [S1: SE CFO deck src:3179] [S2: trade press src:1699, via D02].
    • MHI is doubling capacity [S1: Utility Dive 2026-08-13] [S2: MHI Q&A, via D02].

    • Book-to-bill fell from ~2.5 in Q1 to ~1.7 in Q2, and organic order growth from +86% to +66% [S1: PR1Q] [S2: PR2Q].
    • The H1 margin of 18.2% flatters: it is ~16.3% excluding Prolec, which runs at ~25% [D02].
    • The spring-2027 CMD has a high bar.
    • It needs a 2028 raise of about 17% just to reach Street.
    • A raise below Street repeats the Q2'26 pattern (−8.69%).
    • Framework-raise days were +5.01% and +15.62%, but those raised the plan above where Street stood [D05; FACTS BR-38].
    • Correction: Ken Parks, not the new CFO, presents the Jan-2027 guide [S1: GEV release 2026-08-27] [S2: MarketScreener/CFO Dive 2026-08-28, via V07/V08].
    Q12

    Probabilities and the most likely failure

    • Headline probabilities are in §4-B. The most likely single cell is (mild cut, 21–23x) at ~18%, giving about 0% before cash and +3% after.
    • Most likely failure: "dead money." 1. The Jan-2027 FY27 outlook lands around 16.5–17% margin against Street at 18.15% (straight-line to plan, per D04). 2. Street trims. 3. The multiple drifts to the grid-peer range.
    • Tail failure (~25%): an AI-sentiment shock pushes the multiple to 15–18x.
    • Drawdown frequency: GEV has had five closing drawdowns of 15%+ in about 2.5 years since the spin (median −24.6%) [FACTS BX]. At that rate (~2 a year), the chance of at least one ≥15% drawdown within 12 months is about 86% [computed, Poisson]. Even a winning long probably has to sit through one.

    Arithmetic

    A. Price grid. P = (m × E + 9,113) / 266.33, with net cash and shares taken from the 10Q. - Example: 21 × 12,191 = 256,011; plus 9,113 = 265,124; divided by 266.33 = $995. - NTM definitions: - Today: 0.25 × 6,359 + 0.75 × 9,574 = 8,770. - Sep-27: 0.25 × 9,574 + 0.75 × 13,064 = 12,191, i.e. +39%. - Plan path: 10,794 (brief §7), i.e. +23% on 8,770.

    B. Probability grid (research judgement; estimates and multiple treated as independent, which understates the tail because the two are positively correlated): - Estimate rows: consensus 0.35 / −7.5% 0.40 / plan path 0.25. - Multiple columns: 25x 0.30 / 22x 0.45 / 17.7x 0.25. - Row returns (25x, 22x, 17.7x): - Consensus: +22.4%, +8.2%, −12.3% - −7.5% cut: +13.5%, +0.3%, −18.6% - Plan path: +8.8%, −3.8%, −21.9% - Expected return: 0.35 × 7.34 + 0.40 × (−0.47) + 0.25 × (−4.55) = +1.25%. Adding ~+3.0% for the net-cash build gives ≈ +4%. - P(> +10%) = 0.105 + 0.12 = 0.225. - P(< −10%) = 0.0875 + 0.10 + 0.0625 = 0.25.

    C. H2 SRA test. - Needed backlog: 125 / 2 = 62.5 GW. - 62.5 − 53 + 10 (shipped) = 19.5 GW of conversions plus orders. - Gross signings: 125 − 116 + 10 = ~19 GW in H2, against 41 GW in H1.

    D. Cash build to Sep-27. - H2'26 FCF: 12,000 (guide midpoint) − 9,897 (H1) = ~2.1B. - FY27 Q1–Q3: 0.75 × 7,417 = ~5.6B. - Total ≈ 7.7B / 266.33 = $29/share.

    E. Drawdown frequency. λ = 5 / 2.5 years = 2 per year; P(at least one in 12 months) = 1 − e^−2 = 0.86.

    What would change this
    1. The FY27 outlook (late Jan 2027) has a margin midpoint ≥18% and EBITDA ≥ ~$9.5B.
    2. The 2028 framework is raised to ≥$13B EBITDA, or a 2030 outlook at the spring CMD implies it.
    3. YE26 backlog GW exceeds SRA GW, and the ≥125 GW target is met, confirming conversion.
    4. The Q3/Q4 CSA profitability revision turns favourable, and Wind hits ~−$400M.
    5. Peer multiples re-rate: the US grid median rises above 24x.
    6. AI-capex guides for 2027 are confirmed at ≥$1T with no cancellations.

    Jan-2027 guide presenter: Ken Parks, not Claire McDonough, presents the guide (per V07/V08 sources). - GLJ-day drop: the brief attributes the Sep-14 fall to GLJ plus the 10-year yield, but the AI-lab slowdown call was a third, and probably larger, co-driver. - Tariffs and SRAs: they appear on the brief's attack list but carry little FY27 EBITDA weight.

    What we asked

    Bottom line

    No public source gives a GE turbine-only price by contract year.     Historical analog: the 1999–2002 US "power bubble" at GE Power Systems.

    AskedWhat historical analog fits best (gas-turbine cycles, capex-boom suppliers), and what does it say?

    • Earnings peaked after orders turned.
    • GEPS still grew earnings 29% in 2002 [S1: GE 2003 annual report ex99b, SEC 0000797463-04-000012].
    • About 46,000 MW of gas projects were cancelled from Nov-2001 [S2: Power Engineering, 2002-09].
    • GE forecast US gas-turbine orders and shipments down 80% or more over two years [GE release 2002-07-23].
    • Lesson: earnings follow orders and shipments; the stock follows order signals. Orders are still accelerating now ($200B backlog "very early in 2027"). So the analog does not support a cycle short inside 4 months, only a narrower guide-timing short.

    Margin path to 2028 - Straight line from the FY26 guide midpoint: (13 + 20) / 2 = 16.5%. - Consensus step from the guide midpoint: 18.15 − 13.0 = +5.15 pts, against +4.6 pts, the largest step so far.

    Research FY27 base: 17% × $52.5B = $8,925M, rounded to $8.9B. Gap to consensus: −$674M (−7.0%).

    What would change this

    FY27 margin guide low end of at least 18%, or a 2028 plan raise: this flips the view to long. - Pre-positioning: a cut in the Street FY27 to $9.0B or less before January would take away the surprise, which weakens the short. - A Q3 print with an orders and pricing beat: this is the risk E02 flagged; it would move probability toward the in-line and bull paths.

    Disagreements with the master brief

    CFO: Parks, not McDonough, is scheduled to present the January call (sources in row 10). The "new-CFO reset" angle is weaker than the brief says. - Framework wording: the Q4'25 call says "at least $56B." The 8-K release says "$56B."

    Bottom line

    Over 12 months this is close to a coin flip. My research call leans slightly long (p_long 0.52), and the short edge is a 4-month trade. - The best-evidenced finding runs against consensus: FY27 adjusted EBITDA of about $8.8B vs $9,574M, about −8% [S1: MS] [S2: GF "Street $9.45B"]. - That gap is worth about −$60 to −90 per share. The consensus roll-forward from FY27 to an FY28-weighted NTM is worth more (+27%) [computed A1, A6]. - The price needs only about 20.3x NTM EV/EBITDA in Sep-2027 if consensus holds, or about 22.8x on the research path. Today the stock trades at 28.2x [computed A6] [S1: MS] [S2: CL 27.7x]. - Consensus FY27 needs a Power segment margin of about 23%. Management's target for 2028 is 22% [S1: Q4REL] [S2: corpus src:671, 2028 outlook text]. H1'26 actual was 17.6% [S1: Q2REL segment table] [S2: 10Q MD&A]. - The January FY27 guide is likely to disappoint: P(margin midpoint < 18.15%) ≈ 80–85% [D04A/B via D10]. Historical reaction on such days is −4% to −12% [D04B; BX-13]. That argues for a short into January, not for a 12-month short. - The spring-2027 Capital Markets Day (CMD), with a 2030 outlook, falls inside the 12-month window. It prices the 2029–30 margin step the CEO himself has pointed to ("mostly sold out through '30") [S1: CALL2Q chunk 251595] [S2: LAG p.10, SINGLE for the "'29 and '30" line]. Both past investor-event framework resets were raises (+4 and +6 margin points) [S1: facts BR-28] [S2: Dec-24/Dec-25 releases]. - Analog: in GE's 2001–02 gas bust, earnings rose about 30% in the shipment-peak year while orders collapsed [S1: GE02AR] [S2: GE7/02, orders −80%]. Reported EBITDA is therefore a lagging tell. The item that would flip the call is orders/commitments, not margin.

    Historical analog.

    AskedWhat historical analog fits best (gas-turbine cycles, capex-boom suppliers), and what does it say?

    • In the GE Power Systems boom and bust of 1999–2002:

    • US orders and shipments were forecast to fall "80 percent or more over the next two years" [S2: GE7/02].
    • The collapse came through merchant IPP cancellations: Calpine restructured about $3.4B of turbine commitments in Feb-2003 [S1: PE02] [S2: Calpine 8-K Feb-2003, SEC 0000916457-03-000003].
    • GE's stock went from $60 (42.6x) to $31.85 (21.1x) while EPS rose 19% (D05, from GE ex-99 filings and the NY Post). That is a single-publisher chain through D05, so treat it as medium confidence.
    • What the analog implies here:
    • The bust signal is orders and cancellations, not EBITDA.
    • GEV's orders are still accelerating: Power orders +134% organically in Q2 [S1: Q2REL] [S2: CALL2Q].
    • GEV's customers today are regulated utilities and hyperscalers, not merchant IPPs; I did not verify this mix. SRAs (54% of contracted GW) are the soft spot.

    Bottom line

    FY27 adjusted EBITDA range: $7.7B–$9.6B (base ~$8.7B, 16.7% margin). That is a statistical band combining each segment's low/high swing (root-sum-square). If every segment lands low or high at once, the extremes are $7.0B and $10.1B. - Consensus of $9,574M [MS; FACTS CT-02] sits at the top of the band. - For consensus to hold, Power needs ~21.5–23.5% and Electrification ~21–22% in 2027. That is close to the 2028 targets of 22%/22% [REL-4Q25; DEC25]. - FY28 range: $9.7B–$12.6B (base ~$11.2B, 19.2%). Corners are $8.8B–$13.3B. - The base matches management's framework ($11.2B = 20% × $56B) [REL-4Q25; DEC25]. - Consensus of $13,064M is above the statistical high. It needs Power and Electrification together at ~24.4% on consensus revenue, about 2.4 points above both 2028 targets. - Power margin is the biggest driver. 1 point of Power margin in FY27 ≈ $275M; the 18.5%→21.5% range is worth ~$825M. - The trend cuts against an easy short. Power margin rose +2.6 pts in FY24, +2.2 in FY25 and ~+3.3 in FY26 (guide mid) [10K-24; 10K-25; REL-2Q26]. Another +2.5 pts reaches ~20.5% in FY27. - The 2028 target of 22% implies the pace slows to ~+2 pts over two years. Either management is conservative or the Street is early. - Power services are not a smooth compounder. - Revenue from contractual service agreements (CSAs) was flat to down: $5,473M in FY24, $5,412M in FY25, $2,720M in H1'25 and $2,689M in H1'26 [10K-24 Note; 10K-25 Note 9; 10Q-2Q25; 10Q-2Q26 Note 9]. - Revisions to CSA profitability were negative in every period. H1'26 (−$218M) already exceeds all of FY25 (−$151M). - Services growth of ~5–6% comes from non-CSA work (transactional, nuclear, upgrades), which grew ~10–11%. - Shipments lag the "20 GW" run-rate. - Gas shipments ran 1.5–5.2 GW a quarter from Q1'24 to Q2'26, and H1'26 (7.5 GW) was below H1'25 (8.2 GW) [10Q-2Q26; 10Q-2Q25]. - The CEO said GEV will ship "at least 30 gigawatts" over the six quarters Q3'26–Q4'27 [CALL-2Q26], and gave the cadence of 5 GW a quarter, rising to 6 in H2'27 [LAGUNA; FACTS PP-22]. That implies ~20–22 GW in 2027. - Wind is the second-largest swing in FY27, with the weakest guidance record. - The FY26 guide of about −$400M needs +$257M in H2 [FACTS RQ-10]. - The CEO expects Wind to be "materially better in 2027 than in 2026" [MB-LAG; LAGUNA]. - Wind missed its FY24 and FY25 guides, and its 2028 margin target was cut from 10% to 6% [DEC25; FACTS BR-11].

    Q2

    Realised price per kW in the backlog, and SRA pricing

    AskedWhat realised price per kW is embedded in the equipment backlog today, how has it moved by quarter, and how does new SRA pricing compare with the backlog (management: "10 to 20 points", ">20%")?

    No gas-only $/kW is disclosed. Two proxies, both upper-bounded because Power equipment also includes nuclear, hydro and steam:

    • Power equipment RPO ÷ firm gas backlog GW: Q3'25 $575, Q4'25 $618, Q1'26 $648, Q2'26 $741 per kW, i.e. +29% in three quarters [FACTS RV-25, built from the RPO tables in 10K-25 / 10Q-2Q26 and GW from REL-2Q26].
    • Power equipment revenue ÷ gas GW shipped: FY24 $480/kW (5,708/11.9), FY25 $437 (6,686/15.3), H1'26 $511 (3,834/7.5) [10K-25 segment table; 10Q-2Q26 segment note]. H1'26 is flattered by an aero-heavy mix.
    • New slot reservation agreement (SRA) pricing vs backlog: "another 10 to 20 points of pricing strength" [CALL-4Q25]. H1'26 orders were priced ">20%" above 4Q'25 orders, which is not like-for-like because of aero and combined-cycle mix [CALL-2Q26; FACTS PMX-30].
    • Independent checks:
    • LG&E/KU, same site, GE 7HA: all-in plant cost rose +53–57% between April 2024 and June 2026, including escalation [KY PSC Case 2025-00045; FACTS TP-05].
    • LG&E/KU market indications for a combined-cycle plant without a reservation: $2,800/kW (May) to $3,000–3,200/kW (July) [KY PSC Case 2025-00313; FACTS TP-12].
    • Siemens Energy's CFO: orders are "still coming in at higher margins than older backlog" [FACTS TP-30].
    Q3

    Vintage share of 2027 Power equipment revenue: dollars vs GW

    AskedWhat share of 2027 Power equipment revenue comes from orders signed before 2025, in 2025, and in 2026 — by dollars AND separately by GW? Where do the two views differ, and why?

    • By dollars (prior verified work, RPO-curve method): pre-2025 orders 8–20%, 2025 orders 47–62%, 2026+ orders 29–35% [FACTS GLJ-21 with the vintage model; 10K-25 RPO note].
    • By GW — computed, first-in-first-out (FIFO) bound:
    • Firm backlog at 6/30/26 = 53 GW [REL-2Q26; CALL-2Q26].
    • Implied YE25 backlog = 53 − 20.1 (H1'26 orders) + 7.5 (H1'26 shipments) ≈ 40.4 GW.
    • Implied YE24 backlog = 40.4 − 29.8 (FY25 orders) + 15.3 (FY25 shipments) ≈ 25.9 GW.
    • Order and sales GW come from 10K-25 and 10Q-2Q26. These backlog figures are derived and ignore cancellations and conversions.
    • Shipments from 1/1/25 through YE26 ≈ 15.3 + 7.5 + ~10 = ~32.8 GW, which exceeds the 25.9 GW pre-2025 backlog. So under strict FIFO the pre-2025 GW share of 2027 is ~0%, and 2025-vintage orders (29.8 GW) fill essentially all of 2027.
    • Under management's own description, 2024–25 high-margin orders deliver "'27 and beyond" [CALL-4Q25; WEB-UD]. That points to non-FIFO slotting, with aero shipping fast and HA units waiting for their slots. A plausible pre-2025 GW share is 0–25%, but it cannot be computed from disclosures.
    • Why the two views differ:
    • Dollars include nuclear, hydro and steam; GW is gas only.
    • 2025 orders are priced higher per kW, so their dollar share exceeds their GW share.
    • Revenue on long projects may be recognised over time, before shipment; the over-time vs point-in-time split is not disclosed.
    • HA units ordered in 2023–24 (33) roughly equal HA units sold in FY25 plus H1'26 (32) [10K-25; 10Q-2Q26]. But the HA backlog at YE22 is unknown, so HA-level FIFO cannot be closed.

Power SG&A plus R&D runs at 11.5% of revenue [10Q-2Q26].

    Q6

    Operating leverage from ~15 GW to 20–24 GW

    AskedHow much operating leverage comes from going from ~15 GW to 20-24 GW a year? Quote management.

    • Power costs, H1'25 → H1'26 [10Q-2Q26 segment note, both periods]:
    • Cost of revenues fell from 73.8% to 71.8% of revenue (6,818/9,234 → 7,504/10,449): +2.0 pts.
    • SG&A plus R&D went from 1,172 (12.7%) to 1,204 (11.5%) while revenue grew +13.2%: +1.2 pts.
    • Other items (equity income) added ~+0.3 pts.
    • The organic margin gain was +4.1 pts [FACTS PMX-19].
    • FY27 opex leverage (computed): if Power SG&A plus R&D grows ~6% against revenue growth of ~16%, the opex ratio falls from ~10.4% to ~9.5%, adding ~+0.9 pts from opex alone.
    • Management's wording (Power section of CALL-2Q26): margins expanded on "favorable price and higher volume, more than offsetting inflation, as well as additional expenses to support capacity investments at Gas". On Q3: "volume, price and productivity should more than offset inflation" [CALL-2Q26; REL-2Q26].
    • A GW-to-margin leverage figure has not been quantified by management [not found in CALL-2Q26, CALL-4Q25, LAGUNA].
    Q7

    Cost headwinds and contract terms

    AskedWhich cost headwinds (tariffs, materials, labour, liquidated damages) are embedded, and are equipment contracts escalated or fixed-price? Quote contract-term evidence.

    • Fixed price [10K-25 Item 1A; 10K-24 Item 1]: "We enter into contracts that commit to a fixed price well before project completion." The 10-K lists "inflation, labor and material cost increases" and "liquidated or other damages" as risks.
    • Liquidated damages are estimated inside variable consideration, using "specified liquidated damages rates" [10K-25 Item 8; 10K-24 Item 8]. The amounts are not disclosed.
    • Tariffs: the 2026 estimate is $100–200M, down from $250–350M at Q1; the FY25 actual was ~$250M [10Q-2Q26 MD&A; FACTS RQ-01].
    • Wind tariffs: H1'26 onshore volume "had fewer contractual protections for tariffs since we signed these orders before their implementation" [CALL-2Q26]. This implies newer contracts carry tariff protection (single-source for that inference).
    • Firm pricing at reservation: a customer paid a $25M reservation partly "to lock in firm pricing for the equipment" [KY PSC Order, 2025-10-28; FACTS VF-03].
    • Escalation clauses in gas contracts: not found in filings or transcripts searched [SINGLE-SOURCE gap].
    • CSA cost overruns: FY24 −$319M "due primarily to higher costs"; H1'26 −$218M [10K-24; 10Q-2Q26].

    General questions answered along the way

    G2: Consensus FY27 needs Power margin about +3.5–5.5 pts in one year (18% → 21.5–23.5%). History shows +2.2 to +3.3 pts a year (items 1–2). - G6: The evidence differs from consensus in FY27 Power margin (~1–3 pts, $275–825M) and in FY28 Power plus Electrification margin (24.4% needed vs 22% targeted). - G11: Shipments ran 1.5–5.2 GW a quarter from Q1'24 to Q2'26, and H1'26 shipments were below H1'25. The capacity ramp is not yet visible in shipments (Q1 table). - G12: CSA revenue is flat while revisions are negative. Deposits sit outside EBITDA. - G16: CSA profitability revisions (−$218M in H1'26) are a Power margin risk that is being treated as noise. - G20: Definition traps: - Power $/kW includes non-gas equipment. - Siemens Energy and MHI margins are after D&A (profit before special items / business profit), unlike GEV's segment EBITDA. - Consensus EBITDA is single-source. - Recurring stock-based compensation is not added back to adjusted EBITDA. - G22: The FY27 guide on the January 2027 call must show a margin of ~18% or higher (not the Power figure alone) for consensus to stand. For FY28 consensus, a raise of the 2028 plan is needed. - G24: Recurring stock-based compensation ($257M) is expensed inside adjusted EBITDA. The one-time option grant is excluded via separation costs [10K-25; FACTS VF-12].

    What would change this

    Power margin at 19% or higher in Q3'26 (guide 17–18% [CALL-2Q26]), or a Q4'26 margin at 20% or higher, supports the high case of 21.5%. - CSA revisions turning favourable, or CSA revenue growing, would move the services margin up and the base up. - Q3/Q4'26 shipments of 5 GW or more a quarter confirm 21–22 GW for 2027. Shipments at or below 4 GW point to the low case. - Wind at breakeven or better in Q3'26 and H2 of +$257M supports FY27 Wind above zero. Another miss supports the low case. - Disclosure of equipment vs services margins (possible at the spring 2027 CMD [LAGUNA]) would replace the Q5 grid. - A January 2027 FY27 guide at 17% or higher adjusted EBITDA margin would put the base below management's guide.

    Disagreements with the master brief

    Section 3 ("20 GW/yr run-rate from Q3'26"): this describes production capacity. Recognised shipments were 7.5 GW in H1'26, below H1'25's 8.2 GW. The team should model GW shipped, not output. - Section 6: services pricing and growth are treated as uniformly positive. The filings show CSA revenue flat for two years and negative profitability revisions in every period, with H1'26 the worst half since FY24. - Section 8 frames the long case as "Power margin gains are real": they are, and the trend pace (+2–3 pts a year) supports ~20.5% in FY27. That is stronger for the long side than the brief implies. The 2028 22% target, not the trend, is what makes consensus look early. - Otherwise none.

    Open items

    Q2

    Price per kW.

    AskedWhat realised price per kW is embedded in the equipment backlog today, how has it moved by quarter, and how does new SRA pricing compare with the backlog (management: "10 to 20 points", ">20%")?

    All series include non-gas Power equipment, so read them as upper bounds and trends, not like-for-like gas prices.

    Measure Values
    Power equipment RPO ÷ firm gas backlog GW Q3'25 $18,977M/33 GW = $575/kW; YE25 $24,707M/40 = $618; Q1'26 $28,530M/44 = $648; Q2'26 $39,261M/53 = $741

    Q3

    Vintage share of 2027 equipment revenue.

    AskedWhat share of 2027 Power equipment revenue comes from orders signed before 2025, in 2025, and in 2026 — by dollars AND separately by GW? Where do the two views differ, and why?

    • By dollars (brief, RPO curve): pre-2025 8–20%, 2025 vintage 47–62%, 2026+ 29–35%.
    • By GW, new work: backlog GW rolls forward exactly (§4-E). YE23 17.2 GW, YE24 25.5, YE25 40; Q3'25 ties to 33, Q1'26 to 44, Q2'26 to 53. On FIFO, 2026's 17.5 GW is 10.2 GW of 2024 vintage plus 7.3 GW of 2025 vintage. 2027's 20 GW is then ~100% 2025 vintage and 0% pre-2025.
    • Why the two views differ:
    • Delivery follows slot dates, not order dates. 2024 HA orders reserved 2027–28 slots, so FIFO understates pre-2025 HA content.
    • Dollar RPO includes nuclear, steam, hydro and over-time scope.
    • Aero orders placed in 2026 ship quickly.
    • Neither view gives vintage margin share. The filings cannot determine the true GW vintage split. Research range for pre-2025 GW share in 2027: 0–35%.

    • Power services revenue: FY24 $12,419M, FY25 $13,081M (+5.3%), H1'26 $6,598M (+5.8%) [facts PMX-07; 10-K Note 24; Q2'26 10-Q].

There are 130 HA units running and 195 on contract, and each HA GW is worth "$0.5 billion of high-margin services revenue over the first 20 years" [S1: Laguna transcript 2026-09-16, earningscalls.dev] [SINGLE-SOURCE]. That is about $25M/GW/yr, so installed-base growth mostly lands after 2027.

    General questions answered along the way

    G2: Consensus FY27 at 18.15% implies a +4.4-point step in one year. GEV's largest step so far is +4.6 points (FY25 actual to the FY26 guide) [D04, computed]. - G11: Capacity caps 2027 at about 20–21 GW. There are 325 machines installed and about 400 planned by YE26 (chunk 251611). - G12: CSA cumulative catch-ups flow straight into EBITDA (−$218M in H1'26). Revenue per GW shipped lags backlog value per GW by about 45% ($513 vs $741/kW). - G20: These numbers rest on a single source: the '29–'30 quote, GLJ's 20.7% Power consensus, the FY26 Corporate guide and the HA services economics.

    Arithmetic

    A. Q4 derivations. Q4'24 = FY24 (75 units / 15 HA / 11.9 GW) − 9M (50 / 7 / 7.1) = 25 / 8 / 4.8. Q4'25 = (81 / 24 / 15.3) − (60 / 19 / 12.2) = 21 / 5 / 3.1.

    B. Revenue per GW shipped. Power equipment revenue = Power revenue − services. - FY23: (17,436 − 11,838) / 13.8 = $406/kW. - FY24: 5,708 / 11.9 = $480/kW. - FY25: 6,686 / 15.3 = $437/kW. - H1'25: 2,996 / 8.2 = $365/kW. - H1'26: 3,851 / 7.5 = $513/kW. - Q2'26: 1,957 / 3.3 = $593/kW.

    C. Backlog value per GW. The values in §2 Q2 = row-4 RPO ÷ row-3 GW.

    D. Bookings per GW. - H1'26: (39,261 − 24,707 + 3,851) / 20.1 = $916/kW. - FY25: (24,707 − 12,461 + 6,686) / 29.8 = $635/kW. - FY24: (12,461 − 13,636 + 3,900 EDF + 5,708) / 20.2 = $417/kW.

    Answers 14

    Q1

    Escalation and pass-through in existing contracts

    AskedDo existing equipment contracts carry price-escalation or inflation pass-through terms? Search filings and transcripts for 'escalation', 'price adjustment', 'index'. How much does that soften the "old cheap book" problem?

    Finding: mostly no for gas equipment. Yes for services, but at fixed rates. This does little to soften the "old cheap book" problem on equipment.

    Equipment is fixed-price. - The 10-K says: "We enter into contracts that commit to a fixed price well before project completion." It lists "inflation, labor and material cost increases" as a risk. [S1: 10-K -26-000015 Item 1A, offset ~81.8k] [S2: 10-K 0001996810-25-000011 Item 1A (same language; D01 Q7)] - The word "escalation" appears in the FY25 10-K only in the lease note. "Price adjustment" and "indexed" do not appear at all (searched). - Billing adjustments cover project delays and performance guarantees only, not inflation [10-K -26-000015 Item 8, revenue estimates].

    Customer evidence points to firm pricing, not indexation. - An LG&E/KU reservation of $25M was paid in part "to lock in firm pricing for the equipment" [S1: KY PSC order 2025-10-28, facts VF-03] [S2: evidence brief Test on LG&E/KU].

    Strategy since the spin. - The spin filings say GEV is "improving protections embedded in customer agreements to protect against inflation" and is shortening bid cycles. For Wind, they point to "better inflation protection mechanisms". [S1: S-1 0001193125-24-066951] [S2: Form 10 exhibit 8-K 0001193125-24-063739 ex99.1 — same issuer, so weak independence] - The Q2'26 call says H1'26 onshore Wind "had fewer contractual protections for tariffs since we signed these orders before their implementation". That implies newer orders carry protection [CALL-2Q26, via D01 Q7; SINGLE-SOURCE inference].

    Services do escalate, but at a fixed rate. - Talen's Guernsey 8-K exhibit describes a 25-year GE CSA signed 2019-06-28: "a monthly fixed fee… and variable fees… per gas turbine fired hour with an annual 2.5% escalation on both fees", plus spare parts "$20,000 plus escalation" [S1: 8-K/EX 0001622536-25-000013 ex99.4, note (c)]. - Company-level corroboration: "margin enhancement potential in our services business due to price escalation" [S2: GEV S-1 0001193125-24-066951]. - A fixed 2.5% escalator ran below 2022–24 cost inflation. That fits the unfavourable CSA profitability revisions: FY24 −$319M ("due primarily to higher costs"), FY25 −$151M, H1'26 −$218M [S1: 10-Q -26-000148 Note 9, offset ~40.1k] [S2: 10-K -26-000015 Note 9 / D01 Q4].

    Net effect. - There is no evidence that escalation lifts pre-2025 equipment margins. - The long argument has to rest on dollar share: pre-2025 orders are only 8–20% of 2027 equipment revenue [brief §5; vintage model]. Escalation adds nothing to it. - On services, a fixed ~2.5% escalator turns from a drag to neutral if cost inflation settles near 2.5–3%. That is a research inference and is not quantifiable from disclosures.

    Answers 14

    Q1

    What the CEO's "'29 and '30" timing implies for FY27–28

    AskedThe CEO said the 2026 change in margin in backlog "tells you the equipment margins for '29 and '30, largely". What FY27-28 margin does that timing imply versus what consensus requires?

    • The CEO maps the 2026 backlog-margin change to 2029–30 equipment margins [S1: Laguna p.10; also p.5, "most of when that equipment delivers"] [S2: facts VF-02/PP-06; MarketBeat src:681]. He expects that change to exceed 2025's "low double digits", i.e. more than 11 points [S1: Laguna p.5] [S2: facts PP-04].

The Power backlog's average contribution margin was about +6 points above the YE22 base at YE24 and about +17 at YE25 [S1: GEV 4Q'25 deck slide 5 (01282026.pdf)] [S2: Q4'25 transcript, CEO "starting point is approximately breakeven"; facts PMX-25/26].

    Q2

    Margin guide misses while revenue and FCF beat: pattern or noise?

    AskedWhy did GEV's margins finish slightly below its first numeric guide in FY24 and FY25 while revenue and FCF beat? Is that a pattern or noise?

    • Brief correction: the first annual guides were qualitative, and GEV met them. Numeric ranges came later: FY24 5–7%, narrowed to 5.5–6% in Dec-2024; FY25 8–9% [S1: Dec-2024 release src:2653, "5.5%-6%, narrowed from 5%-7%"] [S2: Dec-2025 release as reported, src:2711, "8% to 9%"; facts BR-23].
    • Outcomes: FY24 5.83% and FY25 8.40%. Both are inside the range and below its midpoint. The misses were ~$61M (FY24) and ~$40M (FY25), about 2–3% of H2 EBITDA [computed, §4-B].
    • Beats elsewhere: revenue +1.3% and +4.3%; FCF +89% and +65% vs initial guides [facts BR-21, BR-24].
    • Mechanism, in part:
    • FCF beats come from deposits, which are a working-capital item.
    • Margin carries negative CSA revisions: FY24 −$319M "due primarily to higher costs", FY25 −$151M, H1'26 −$218M [S1: 10-Q -26-000148 Note 9, "net unfavorable changes in estimated profitability of $218 million"] [S2: 10-K -26-000015 Note 9; 10-K -25-000011].
    • Wind missed its guide in both years [S1: 8-K -25-000159 (Wind guide cut Q3'25)] [S2: Dec-2025 release, Wind 2028 margin cut from 10% to 6%].
    • Verdict: a consistent small pattern in two of two years, but the sample is n=2 and the misses are small. This year matters more because consensus FY26 ($6,359M, 13.74%) sits in the upper half of the 12–14% range, whereas GEV has twice finished in the lower half.

    • GEV's own guiding philosophy: "I always have an expectation that we do better internally relative to what we commit to you externally" (Strazik, Laguna, 2026-09-16, p.4) [S1: Laguna PDF] [S2: MarketBeat src:681 (Laguna coverage)].

    Q5

    SRA conversion and cancellation terms

    AskedSRA conversion: 54% of 116 GW is reservations (27% at Siemens Energy). What happens to orders and deposits if data-center or utility demand cools? What are the cancellation terms?

    • Terms:
    • Maxim–GEV SRA: a "non-refundable deposit" holds the slot. The parties agree only to "negotiate in good faith" a definitive sale, and "the purchase price… will be agreed to in the definitive agreement" [S1: Maxim Power release 2026-02-09, corpus src:232] [S2: corpus src:3490/249 coverage].
    • This contrasts with LG&E/KU, where a $25M reservation locked firm pricing [facts VF-03, KY PSC order 2025-10-28]. Terms vary. Some SRAs do not fix price or bind the purchase.
    • GEV's own risk factor: "orders may be deferred, reduced, or canceled and slot reservation agreements may not result in orders" [S1: 10-K -26-000015 Item 1A] [S2: none; GEV's own risk-factor language].
    • Where the deposits sit: in contract liabilities: "down payments on orders and slot reservation agreements at Power" [S1: 10-Q -26-000148 MD&A] [S2: 10-Q -25-000073 MD&A].
    • What cooling would do:
    • The 63 GW SRA pool is 54% of 116 GW, vs Siemens Energy's 27% (26/95) [S1: 8-K -26-000147] [S2: SE Q3 FY26 presentation p.6].
    • Unconverted SRAs would stop adding deposits. The existing non-refundable deposits stay, so the cash hit is to future inflows, not a reversal.
    • Orders (SRA → order conversion: 10 GW in Q2'26) and the ≥125 GW YE26 target are the observables.
    • Aggregate SRA cancellation experience: not disclosed.

    AskedCash: operating cash excluding deposits was negative in FY23-H1'26, and consensus FY27 FCF falls 38%. What happens to the stock when deposit inflows slow?

    Q10

    The 1999–2002 boom and bust

    AskedThe 1999-2002 US gas-turbine boom and bust: orders, cancellations, GE Power's margins and stock afterward. What rhymes today and what doesn't?

    • GE shipped more than 60 GW in 2001 [SINGLE-SOURCE: corpus src:296].
    • July 2002: GE cut about 2,500 jobs and forecast US gas-turbine orders and shipments down "80 percent or more over the next two years" [S1: GE Power Systems release 2002-07-23].
    • Power Systems was 17.3% of GE revenue in 2002 and 13.8% in 2003. Its EPS contribution was +$0.09 in 2002 but −$0.14 in 2003 on the shipment decline [S1: GE 2003 10-K/Annual Report ex13] [S2: GE 2004 10-K revenue-share text].
    • What rhymes:
    • A demand narrative (then "The Internet Begins with Coal"; now AI).
    • New non-utility buyers placing block reservations.
    • OEM capacity adds.
    • Profits peaked the year after orders collapsed, because backlog kept shipping.
    • What does not:
    • Non-refundable deposits.
    • A much larger services annuity.
    • Regulated-utility IRPs.
    • Supply bottlenecks deeper in the chain.
    • Implication: an order bust would hit the multiple first, not EBITDA, inside 12 months.

    AskedThe 2017-2019 GE Power collapse: what were the early signs, and are any present now?

    • 2017 Power profit fell 45% on "softer than expected" markets [S1: GE 2017 10-K] [S2: POWER magazine 2018-02-28].
    • The SEC found more than a quarter of 2016 Power profit, and almost half of 9M'17, came from reducing cost-to-complete estimates on service agreements [S1: POWER magazine 2020-12-10 on the SEC order] [S2: GE's SEC settlement, $200M].
    • Early signs vs today:
    • Favorable CSA revisions: absent. GEV's are unfavorable.
    • Overcapacity into falling demand: capacity is building, but demand is still rising.
    • Inventory build: +$1.7B in H1'26 [10-Q -26-000148].

    • Verdict: the analogy is mostly not present. Using it would invite a rebuttal.

    A. Plan path for FY27 - Guide midpoint: 13% × $46,000M = $5,980M. - Linear: (5,980 + 11,200) / 2 = $8,590M. Consensus is +11.5% above it. - Geometric: √(5,980 × 11,200) = $8,184M. Consensus is +17.0% above it. - On the consensus FY26 base of $6,359M: linear $8,780M (+9.0%), geometric $8,439M (+13.4%). - Value = (m × EBITDA + 9,113) / 266.33: - 25 × 8,184 → $802 - 25 × 8,780 → $858

    B. H2 margins - FY24: - H1 revenue ≈ 714 / 0.046 = 15,522. H2 = 34,935 − 15,522 = 19,413. - H2 EBITDA = 2,035 − 714 = 1,321 → 6.8%. - Needed for 6.0%: 0.06 × 34,935 − 714 = 1,382 → 7.1%. Gap $61M. - FY25: - H1 revenue ≈ 17,042. H2 = 21,026. - H2 EBITDA = 3,196 − 1,227 = 1,969 → 9.4%. - Needed for 8.5%: 3,236 − 1,227 = 2,009 → 9.6%. Gap $40M. - H1 revenue is derived from rounded margins (±~$150M). - FY26: - Guide midpoint H2: (5,980 − 2,146) / (46,000 − 20,442) = 15.0%. - Consensus H2: 4,213 / 25,840 = 16.3%.

    C. Q14 - 0.95 × 9,574 = 9,095. - 25.8x: (234,651 + 9,113) / 266.33 = $915. - 23x: $820. - 20x: $717.

    D. FY28 excess - Total: 13,064 − 11,200 = 1,864. - Margin part: 1.59% × 60,500 = 962. - Revenue part: 4,500 × 20% = 900. - In Power equipment margin terms: 962 / 13,000–16,000 = 6.0–7.4 pts.

    E. −10% thresholds ($866) - Required: m × EBITDA ≤ 866 × 266.33 − 9,113 = 221,529. - At 25x: FY27 ≤ $8,861M (−7.4% vs consensus). - At consensus FY27: m ≤ 23.1x. - Sep-27 on consensus NTM $12,191M: m ≤ 18.2x. - On the plan-path NTM $10,794M: m ≤ 20.5x.

    F. Other - Market cap: 962.49 × 266.33 = $256.3B. - FCF yields: 12,017 / 256.3B = 4.7%; 7,417 / 256.3B = 2.9%.

    What would change this

    Arguments 1–2: a Jan-27 guide at or above ~$9.1B, or a 2028 plan raised toward $13B. - Argument 3: Q3 (10-28) at or above consensus with Wind at or above breakeven. - Argument 4: hyperscaler 2027 capex guides rising. - Argument 6: ≥125 GW at YE26 and Q3 orders above Q2. - Argument 7: a 2026 backlog-margin change well above +11 pts, confirming pricing still rising.

    GE Vernova (GEV): what the January 2027 FY27 outlook is likely to show against consensus

    What we asked

Label all probabilities as research judgement.

    • Q1. What was consensus just before GEV issued its FY2025 guide (Dec 2024) and its FY2026 guide (Dec 2025, raised 2026-01-28)? Did each guide land above, at, or below? Stock move the next day?

    Research input only. Every probability is research judgement, and every forecast is a research estimate. The team chooses its own number.**

    Bottom line

    I disagree with the brief on who presents the January call. GEV's own release says Ken Parks "will continue as GE Vernova's CFO through 2026 inclusive of the third and fourth quarter earnings calls and the publishing of the 2026 10-K." [S1: GEV press release, 2026-08-27, gevernova.com/news/press-releases/ge-vernova-announces-chief-financial-officer-transition] [S2: CFO Dive, 2026-08-28: Parks "will remain as finance chief through its remaining two 2026 earnings calls"] - McDonough formally becomes CFO on 2027-01-01 [8-K 0001996810-26-000153, Item 5.02]. But the FY27 guide will be built, and most likely presented, by Parks's team with McDonough joining. The "new CFO resets expectations" angle is weaker than the brief says. - January has never been where GEV issues a first annual guide. The FY25 and FY26 first guides came at December investor updates, each alongside a raise to the multi-year framework. - The reaction days were driven by the framework: +5.01% (2024-12-11) and +15.62% (2025-12-10) [S1: evidence_lanes BR-36 / PP-36, corpus price table] [S2: Proactive 2025-12-10, "+16.5% … at about $730"; Morningstar 2025-12-10, framework margins "surpassed our and the market's expectations"]. - No December 2026 event is listed, and the 2030 outlook waits for the spring CMD [S1: GEV IR events page, PP-02] [S2: Laguna transcript p.10–11; MarketBeat 2026-09-18]. The FY27 guide will therefore land without a framework raise to cushion it. That has not happened before at GEV. - Consensus of 18.15% needs about 74% of the 13%→20% path to be covered in one year (+5.15 pts, against +1.85 pts in 2028). - A straight line puts 2027 at 16.5% (from the FY26 guide midpoint) or 16.9% (from FY26 consensus of 13.74%). - GEV's largest yearly step so far is +4.6 pts (FY25 actual to FY26 guide midpoint) [computed; inputs §4]. - GEV guides margin as whole-number ranges, 1–2 points wide: 5–7%, 8–9%, 11–13%, 12–14% [S1: 8-K releases BR-03, BR-10, BR-12, BR-19] [S2: Dec-2025 investor update PDF; TheFly/TipRanks 2026-04-22]. - On that convention the midpoint only reaches ≥18.15% if the low end is ≥18% (an 18–19% or 18–20% range). - A 17–19% range has a midpoint of 18.0%, which is essentially in line (-$79M). - Research-judgement distribution for the FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guide midpoint:

    <15% 15–16% 16–17% 17–18% 18–19% ≥19%
    4% 10% 22% 34% 23% 7%
    • P(midpoint < 18.15%) ≈ 85%.
    • P(midpoint ≤ 17.5%, i.e. at least ~0.65 pt / ~$340M below) ≈ 66%.
    • P(midpoint ≤ 17.0%) ≈ 56%.
    • The EBITDA-dollar miss is less likely than the margin miss, because GEV's revenue guides tend to come in at or above consensus.
    • One-day reaction base rates. Across 10 earnings days the mean was +2.48%, the mean absolute move 5.42%, and the range −8.69% to +14.58%. Every day that brought a new guide or framework was positive (4 of 4).
    • The closest analogues for a cautious guide are −8.69% (Q2'26: margin held, reversed +4.69% the next day) and −8.6% (the GLJ day, about −3% versus peers, 106% recovered in 11 sessions).
    • Research-judgement range for a guide ≥0.5 pt below consensus: −4% to −11%, with a high chance of partial reversal inside a week.

    Evidence on first guides after a CFO change

    AskedIs there reliable evidence on how first guides after a CFO change compare with consensus? If not, say so.

    No reliable direct evidence was found that a first guide after a CFO change lands above or below consensus. Indirect evidence: - "Manager-Specific Effects on Earnings Guidance: An Analysis of Top Executive Turnovers" (2011): CFOs take part in forming guidance, and breaks in guidance after CFO turnovers "likely reflect uncertainty on the part of the newly appointed executive." [S1: exa research-paper index] [S2: not re-verified — SINGLE-SOURCE] - Geiger & North (2006), 712 new-CFO firms from 1994–2000: discretionary accruals fall significantly after a new CFO arrives. That points to conservatism, but it is about accruals, not guidance. [S1: exa index] [S2: not re-verified] - The 2025 "CEO turnover, sequential disclosure" paper covers forced CEO exits and does not apply here. - Conclusion: treat the new CFO as a weak tilt toward caution at most. It is further weakened because Parks remains through the Q4 call (see §1).

    Q6

    Where 2027 sits on a straight line to 2028

    AskedOn a straight line from the FY26 guide (~13%) to the 2028 framework (20%), where does 2027 land? What does consensus's 18.15% require relative to that line?

    • From the FY26 guide midpoint of 13.0% to the 2028 framework of 20%: 2027 = 16.5%.
    • From FY26 consensus of 13.74% (6,359/46,282): 2027 = 16.87%.
    • Consensus of 18.15% needs +5.15 pts in 2027 (73.6% of the path) and +1.85 in 2028. From FY26 consensus, it needs +4.41 (70.4%).
    • History: FY24→FY25 +2.57 pts; FY25→FY26 guide midpoint +4.60 pts. Consensus FY27 would be the largest step since the spin.
    • By segment, a straight line gives Power 20% (18→22), Electrification ~20.5% (19→22), Wind ~breakeven, corporate about −$0.6–0.7B. That comes to about 16% on ~$52B [computed, research estimate].
    • D01's bottom-up base is 16.7% ($8.7B), and it needs Power at 21.5–23.5% in 2027 to reach consensus [D01 §1].
    Q7

    Range or point, and how range width affects the midpoint test

    AskedDoes management usually give a margin range or a point? Revenue range width? What range width would make "below consensus at the midpoint" likely even if the top of the range matches?

    • Margin is always a range, with whole-number endpoints (5.5–6% was a narrowing): FY24 5–7%; FY25 "HSD", then 8–9%; FY26 11–13%, then 12–14%. Segment ranges are 2 points (Power 17–19%, Electrification 18–20%). [sources in §1]
    • Revenue range is always $1B wide: $34–35B, $36–37B, $41–42B, $44–45B, $44.5–45.5B, $45.5–46.5B. That is 2.9% → 2.2% of the midpoint; at $52.7B, a $1B band would be 1.9%.
    • The test: if the top of the range equals consensus (18.15%), the midpoint is 18.15 − w/2 for any positive width w.
    • With 2 points, the midpoint is 17.15% (−$527M, −5.5% on $52.74B).
    • With 1 point, it is 17.65% (−$264M, −2.8%).
    • With whole-number endpoints, a midpoint of at least 18.15% needs the bottom ≥18%.
