    General questions answered along the way

    G13: The dated test is the late-January call (date not yet announced; 2026-01-28 and 2025-01-22 in prior years). Pass mark for a short: midpoint ≤17.5%. Pass mark for a long: bottom of the range ≥18%. - G14: The Q3 call on 2026-10-28 may frame 2027 early. In October 2025 management "framed things up" before the guide (src:2660). Consensus may cut before January, which would shrink the surprise. - G17: Management controls range width, the revenue scope (Prolec precedent), and which items get excluded as unproven. - G22: The FY27 margin midpoint must come in below ~17.65% for the gap to be more than rounding. - G23: One-day reversals (+4.69% the day after Q2'26; 106% recovery after GLJ) suggest the dated event alone may not carry a 3–12-month short.

    Arithmetic

    FY26 consensus margin = 6,359 / 46,282 = 13.74% [CT-01/02]. - Straight lines: (13.0 + 20) / 2 = 16.5%; 13.74 + (20 − 13.74) / 2 = 16.87%. - Consensus step: 18.15 − 13.0 = 5.15 (5.15 / 7.0 = 73.6%); 18.15 − 13.74 = 4.41 (4.41 / 6.26 = 70.4%). - Historical steps: 8.40 − 5.83 = 2.57; 13.0 − 8.40 = 4.60 [BR-08, BR-19, 10-K FY25]. - EBITDA on $52,740M (difference vs $9,574M):

    Margin EBITDA vs consensus
    15% $7,911M −17.4%
    16% $8,438M −11.9%
    16.5% $8,702M −9.1%
    17% $8,966M −6.4%
    17.5% $9,230M −3.6%
    18% $9,493M −0.8%
    18.5% $9,757M +1.9%
    19% $10,021M +4.7%
    • Revenue sensitivity at a 17% margin: $54B gives $9,180M (−4.1%); $51.5B gives $8,755M (−8.6%).
    • Midpoint when the top of the range equals 18.15: 18.15 − 1.0 = 17.15 → $9,045M (−5.5%); 18.15 − 0.5 = 17.65 → $9,309M (−2.8%).
    • Jan-2026 guide excluding Prolec: 44.5 − ~3.0 = 41.5; 41.5 / 41.97 − 1 = −1.1%.
    • Earnings-day statistics: sum = 24.78 → mean 2.478%; absolute sum = 54.24 → 5.42%; sorted absolute median = (2.73 + 3.07) / 2 = 2.90%.
    • Excess returns: Dec-24 5.01 − 0.77 = +4.24; Q2'26 −8.69 − (−0.12) = −8.57.
    • Distribution weights by likely range: ≤14.5 4%; 15.0 6%; 15.5 4%; 16.0 14%; 16.5 8%; 17.0 24%; 17.5 10%; 18.0 17%; 18.5 6%; ≥19.0 7%.
    • P(<18.15) = 87% before rounding; reported as ~85% to allow for uncertainty.
    • P(≤17.5) = 66%; P(≤17.0) = 56%.

    Reasoning behind the weights: - The mode is 17.0–17.5%. That is where a "grounded" +3.5 to +4 pt step from FY26 of about 13.5% lands, and it matches the size of past initial steps (+3.6 pts: FY26 first-guide midpoint of 12% against FY25's 8.4%). - The 16–17% band holds the straight line and D01's base. - 18% and above needs Power guided at about 22% in 2027, i.e. hitting the 2028 target a year early. - The tail below 15% reflects equipment mix dilution, tariffs and capacity-ramp cost.

    What would change this

    Q3'26 call giving 2027 Power margin language of about 22%, or a Power Q3 margin well above 19%: shift weight to 18%+. - A December 2026 event being announced: it restores the framework cushion, so the base rate becomes the +5% to +16% December days. - FY26 exiting at ≥14% with Q4 ≥17%: the step to 18.15% becomes about +4 pts, which is consistent with history. - Consensus drifting to ≤17.5% before January: the "below consensus" probability falls sharply. - The GEV-hosted Q2'26 transcript showing a 2027 margin comment I did not find.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The January call is not clearly "the first under the new CFO": Parks is contracted to present the Q4 call (see §1).
    2. The January call has never been a first-guide venue. Past first-guide days came with framework raises, so the guide-day history overstates upside cushions.
    3. "Never cut" needs a footnote: in December 2024 the FY24 margin guide midpoint was cut 25bp (5–7% narrowed to 5.5–6%) [BR-05].

Use the GEV PDF directly. - Correct date and venue of the "outperform in '27 and '28" Prolec quote (corpus src:3771). - Options-implied move for the late-January expiry: not available through these tools. - The late-January 2027 earnings date: not yet announced; watch GEV IR. - Named authors of the 2011 guidance-turnover paper: not verified.

That weakens a "new CFO resets expectations" argument. [S1: GEV press release, 2026-08-27, gevernova.com/news/press-releases/ge-vernova-announces-chief-financial-officer-transition] [S2: CFO Dive, 2026-08-28: Parks "will remain as finance chief through its remaining two 2026 earnings calls"] - The CEO has confirmed the FY27 outlook comes on the January call. The same call will carry the 2026 change in equipment margin in backlog, "likely" the date of the next Capital Markets Day (CMD), and full FY26 results. [S1: Laguna transcript, 2026-09-16, GEV-hosted PDF p.10-11, research file PP-03] [S2: GuruFocus/Yahoo coverage of Laguna, corpus src:686 and src:681] - Consensus FY27 margin of 18.15% needs a year-on-year step no first guide has ever shown. Consensus FY27 18.15% vs consensus FY26 13.74% is +4.4 pts. The first FY26 guide stepped +3.5 to +3.6 pts over FY25. On a straight line from the FY26 guide midpoint (13%) to the 2028 framework (20%), 2027 lands at 16.5%. Consensus sits 1.65 pts above that line. [computed; inputs in Section 4] - A segment cross-check points the same way. Getting to 18.15% in FY27 roughly requires Power and Electrification both at their 2028 targets (22%/22%) a year early, plus positive Wind and lower corporate cost. This is a sensitivity with stated assumptions, not a model the team must use. [computed; inputs: Q2'26 transcript segment guides, Dec-2025 framework] - Research-judgement distribution for the FY27 adj EBITDA margin guide midpoint:

    <15% 15-16% 16-17% 17-18% 18-19% ≥19%
    5% 10% 25% 30% 22% 8%
    • P(midpoint below 18.15%) ≈ 80% (plausible band 70-85%).
    • P(midpoint 17.5% or lower, i.e. clearly below) ≈ 65-70%.
    • A 17-19% range (18.0% midpoint) is technically below consensus but would probably trade as in line.
    • Reaction base rate: GEV's stock has traded on the margin line, not on revenue or cash.
    • Days when margin guidance or the 2028 framework was raised: +14.58%, +15.62%, +13.75%.
    • The one raise day with margin held: −8.69% (−12.55% over 5 days).
    • Mean absolute move over 10 earnings days: 5.4% (median 2.9%).
    • Research range for a clearly-below-consensus margin guide with no offsets: roughly −4% to −12%. With a strong backlog-margin page and a 2028 raise: about −3% to +5%.
    • [S1: corpus price table, research file BX-13/BR-38] [S2: TipRanks, AInvest, Livemint, Barron's, Investing.com coverage per event, see evidence table]

    Answers 9

    Q1

    FY2025 guide (2024-12-10, after the close) - Guide: revenue $36-37B (midpoint $36.5B); adj EBITDA margin "high-single digits" (qualitative); FCF $2.0-2.5B. [S1: GEV Dec-2024 investor update press release PDF p.1, research file BR-06] [S2: GEV 2024 Investor Update Recap, gevernova.com, 2024-12-11] - Consensus revenue before the guide: $37.25B (Benzinga). JPMorgan (via The Fly/TheStreet) called FY25 guidance "slightly below consensus expectations, driven by the wind segment". [S1: Benzinga, 2024-12] [S2: TheStreet/Yahoo Finance, 2024-12-14; also corpus chunk 246097] - Verdict: below on revenue (midpoint −2.0% vs $37.25B). No pre-guide margin consensus was found, and the qualitative "HSD" guide cannot be compared numerically. - Next day: 2024-12-11 +5.01%, lifted by the 2028 framework raise (to $45B and 14%, from about 10%), a new dividend and a $6B buyback. [S1: research file BR-38, corrected for the after-close release] [S2: Investing.com, "shares rose to over $347 on Wednesday following its investor day" (direction only, no %)]

    FY2026 guide (2025-12-09, after the close; raised 2026-01-28) - Guide: revenue $41-42B (midpoint $41.5B); margin 11-13%; FCF $4.5-5.0B. [S1: GEV Dec-2025 press release] [S2: Markets Insider/The Fly, 2025-12-09] - Consensus revenue: $41.3B → guide midpoint +0.5%, i.e. at or slightly above. [S1: Markets Insider/TipRanks (The Fly), "GE Vernova sees FY26 revenue $41B-$42B, consensus $41.3B", 2025-12-09] [S2: TipRanks/The Fly, UBS note "credible floor"] Both sources trace to The Fly, so the $41.3B is effectively [SINGLE-SOURCE]. Reuters and MarketScreener were checked but are paywalled. - Pre-guide FY26 margin consensus: not found. Morningstar: "EBITDA margins [2028] easily surpassed our 17% forecast" and "the magnitude surpassed our and the market's expectations". That is about the 2028 framework, not FY26. [S1: Morningstar, 2025-12-10] [S2: Bastion Fiduciary, 2026-01-15, also calls it "too conservative"] - Next day: 2025-12-10 +15.62%. [S1: GEV 2025 Investor Update transcript PDF, gev_webcast_transcript_12092025.pdf (Exa highlight)] [S2: Bastion Fiduciary, 2026-01-15, corpus chunk 246324]
    • Same event, Q&A: "Now can there be some conservatism in our approach? Yes. But at the same time, we haven't experienced this much volume growth." The context is variable-cost productivity being excluded from the plan. [S1: Bastion Fiduciary transcript excerpt, corpus chunk 246348] The blog says the CFO; the transcript excerpt does not name the speaker. [SINGLE-SOURCE, speaker unverified]. The team should confirm speaker and wording in the GEV-hosted Dec-2025 transcript PDF.

    • Revealed behaviour, not quotes:
    • Margin guides have been raised only in mid-year steps: FY24 5-7% in July 2024; FY25 8-9% in July 2025; FY26 12-14% in April 2026.
    • One margin guide was narrowed downward: FY24 to 5.5-6% in Dec-2024.
    • Wind 2028 margin was cut from 10% to 6%.
    • [S1: 8-Ks 0001996810-24-000065, -25-000132, -26-000063; Dec-2024/Dec-2025 PDFs] [S2: research files BR-03, BR-05, BR-10, BR-11]
    • Read-across: management calls its multi-year plan "grounded" with "opportunity to outperform". On that language, a FY27 guide that leaves room under the 20% 2028 framework is more consistent than one that front-loads it.

    Q5

    Evidence on first guides after a CFO change

    AskedIs there reliable evidence on how first guides after a CFO change compare with consensus? If not, say so.

    • No reliable evidence found on the direction of the first guide vs consensus after a CFO change.
    • Nearest academic results:
    • "Manager-Specific Effects on Earnings Guidance: An Analysis of Top Executive Turnovers" (2011): guidance changes after CFO turnovers cluster in the two quarters after the change, depend on the new CFO's background, and affect guidance precision. It does not show a sign of bias vs consensus.
    • "Does Hiring a New CFO Change Things?" (2006; 712 firms, 1994-2000): discretionary accruals fall after a new CFO. That is a reporting-conservatism result, not a guidance-vs-consensus one.
    • [S1/S2: Exa research-paper index entries for each] Treat as [SINGLE-SOURCE each]; the full papers were not read.
    • It is only marginally relevant anyway, since Parks presents the January call. Put little weight on a "new-CFO kitchen-sink" story.
    Q6

    Straight-line path from the FY26 guide to the 2028 framework

    AskedOn a straight line from the FY26 guide (~13%) to the 2028 framework (20%), where does 2027 land? What does consensus's 18.15% require relative to that line?

    • From the FY26 guide midpoint of 13% (12-14%): 2027 = 13 + (20−13)/2 = 16.5%.
    • From FY26 consensus 13.74% ($6,359M / $46,282M): 2027 = 16.87%.
    • Consensus 18.15% is 1.28-1.65 pts above the line. It needs 70-74% of the two-year step in year one, leaving only +3.45 pts to FY28 consensus 21.6% (which is itself above the 20% framework). [computed; inputs: S1 8-K 0001996810-26-000147 FY26 guide / S2 Q2'26 transcript; framework: Q4'25 release 0001996810-26-000012 / Dec-2025 PDF; consensus: MarketScreener, research file CT-01/02]
    • Counterpoint (long side):
    • The implied Q4'26 consensus margin is 18.2% ($2,535M / $13,905M). So consensus FY27 roughly equals the Q4'26 exit rate held for a full year. [S1: MarketScreener quarterly table, 2026-09-29, research file VF-10] [S2: research file PP-20 derivation, 18.1%]
    • Q4 is seasonally GEV's strongest quarter ("the highest revenue and EBITDA in 4Q'26"). [S1: Q2'26 transcript, chunk 251607] [S2: FY25 actuals: Q4'25 margin 10.6% vs FY25 8.4%, 8-K 0001996810-26-000012]
    • History of first guide vs the prior Q4 margin:
    • FY25: "HSD" (~8% midpoint, qualitative) vs Q4'24 10.2% → about −2.2 pts.
    • FY26: 12% vs Q4'25 10.6% → +1.4 pts.
    • Applied to an 18.2% Q4'26 exit, that gives a first-guide midpoint of about 16.0-19.6%, centred near 17.8%. [S1: 8-K 0001996810-25-000004 (Q4'24 10.2%), 8-K 0001996810-26-000012 (Q4'25 10.6%)] [S2: research files BR-06/BR-12]
    Q7

    Range vs point, and range widths

    AskedDoes management usually give a margin range or a point? Revenue range width? What range width would make "below consensus at the midpoint" likely even if the top of the range matches?

    • Margin: always a range once numeric. FY24 5-7% (2 pts, then narrowed to 5.5-6%); FY25 8-9% (1 pt; the first FY25 guide was the qualitative "HSD"); FY26 11-13% and 12-14% (2 pts). [S1: 8-Ks listed in Q2] [S2: research files BR-03/05/10/12/19]
    • Revenue: always $1B wide ($34-35B, $36-37B, $41-42B, $44-45B, $44.5-45.5B, $45.5-46.5B). [same sources]
    • Width math:
    • With a 2-pt margin range, the midpoint sits below 18.15% whenever the top is below 19.15%. A range of 17-19% "matches consensus at the top" but has an 18.0% midpoint. A 16-18% range (top ≈ consensus) has a 17.0% midpoint, 1.15 pts below.
    • With a 1-pt range, the midpoint is below consensus unless the top is ≥18.65%.
    • Given GEV's record of 2-pt first numeric margin ranges, "top of range roughly equals consensus" mechanically means "midpoint about 1 pt below".
    • Revenue: a $1B range around $52-53B is about ±1%. Consensus $52,740M falls inside most plausible ranges; the first two revenue guides landed −2.0% and +0.5% vs consensus.
    Q8

    What else the January call brings, and possible offsets

    AskedWhat will the January call also contain (FY26 actuals, 2026 margin-in-backlog page, CMD date), and could those offset a cautious FY27 guide in the stock's reaction?

    • FY26 actuals. Consensus needs Q4'26 at about 18.2% and FY26 at about 13.7%, above the 13% guide midpoint. Wind needs about +$257M in H2. A Q4 beat would soften a cautious FY27 guide; a Q4 miss would compound it. [S1: research file PP-20/21] [S2: Q2'26 transcript, Wind ~−$400M guide]
    • 2026 equipment margin-in-backlog page. The CEO pre-signalled a Power change larger than 2025's low double digits and at least $8B of equipment margin dollars added. That is likely a positive headline, but by management's own framing it speaks to 2029-30. [S1: Laguna p.5/p.10] [S2: Q4'25 transcript p.5/p.12, PP-09]
    • Orders and backlog. $200B backlog "very early in 2027"; at least 125 GW gas by YE26. [S1: Laguna] [S2: Q2'26 release]
    • CMD date. Spring 2027, with a 2030 outlook and an equipment/services split. [S1: Laguna p.11, PP-07] [S2: GuruFocus src:686]
    • Could these offset a cautious guide?
    • Precedent says yes: in Dec-2024 the revenue guide was below consensus, yet the day was +5.01% on the framework raise.
    • But in January 2027 the long-dated number (2030) is deferred to the CMD, so the one lever that historically overrode near-year numbers is probably not on the table. A 2028 re-set in January is possible; Jan-2026 did re-set 2028, though only for Prolec.
    • Research judgement: offsets are more likely to narrow a negative reaction than reverse it, unless 2028 is raised.

    General questions answered along the way

    G2 (margin pace): consensus FY27 needs +4.4 pts year on year. The largest first-guide step GEV has given is +3.5 to +3.6 pts. The largest delivered step, FY25→FY26 on consensus, is +5.3 pts, so the pace is not unprecedented as an outcome, only as a first guide. [Section 4, step 5] - G13 (dated catalyst): the January 2027 FY27 outlook. One way to set a pass mark from these numbers: guide midpoint ≥18% = consensus holds; ≤17% = a clear gap. [Laguna p.10-11; GuruFocus src:686] - G14 (what could push the reveal out): management could guide conservatively in January and move the "real" number to the spring-2027 CMD. The CMD is inside a 12-month horizon but after a 3-6 month one. [Laguna p.11] - G17 (management discretion): GEV has a pattern of mid-year margin raises and one downward narrowing, and uses "grounded" language for its plan. The FY27 range width alone (1 pt vs 2 pts) moves the midpoint by about 0.5 pt. [Q7] - G22 (what must change): consensus FY27 18.15% vs a probable guide midpoint of 16.5-18%. Either the Street cuts toward the guide, or GEV guides at the Q4 exit rate. [Q6/Q7] - G23 (why the move can exceed the gap): 1 pt of margin is about 5% of the share price at 25x. The stock's past margin-event moves (−8.7% to +15.6%) are 2-3x that, which is consistent with multiple changes stacking on top of estimate changes.

    Arithmetic
    1. FY26 consensus margin = 6,359 / 46,282 = 13.74% (MarketScreener, CT-01/02).
    2. FY27 consensus margin = 9,574 / 52,740 = 18.15%.
    3. Straight line from the guide midpoint = 13.0 + (20.0 − 13.0)/2 = 16.5%. From consensus: 13.74 + (20 − 13.74)/2 = 16.87%.
    4. Share of the two-year step taken in year one: (18.15 − 13)/(20 − 13) = 73.6%; (18.15 − 13.74)/(20 − 13.74) = 70.4%.
    5. Year-on-year steps: - FY24→FY25 actual: 8.40 − 5.83 = +2.57. - First FY26 guide vs FY25: 12.0 − 8.40 = +3.6 (vs the then-guide midpoint of 8.5: +3.5). - FY27 consensus vs FY26 consensus: +4.41.
    6. First guide vs prior Q4: - FY25: ~8.0 − 10.2 = −2.2 (the "HSD" midpoint taken as 8% is an assumption). - FY26: 12.0 − 10.6 = +1.4. - Applied to an 18.2% Q4'26 exit: 16.0% to 19.6%, mean 17.8%.
    7. Segment sensitivity (research estimate; the team chooses its own split): - FY26 implied corporate/eliminations: guide midpoint 13% × $46.0B = $5.98B. Segments: Power $24B × 18% = $4.32B (Laguna, "$24 billion of revenue"); Electrification $14.75B × 19% = $2.80B; Wind −$0.40B. Segment total $6.72B, so corporate plug ≈ −$0.74B. - 2027 revenue split (assumption): Power $27.5B, Electrification $16.8B, Wind $8.4B ≈ $52.7B. - Case A, linear to 2028 (Power 20%, Elec 20.5%, Wind 0, Corp −0.74): 5.50 + 3.44 + 0 − 0.74 = $8.20B → 15.5%. - Case B, Power at 22% a year early (Elec 21%, Wind +0.2): 6.05 + 3.53 + 0.2 − 0.74 = $9.04B → 17.1%. - Case C, both at 2028 targets (22%/22%), Wind +0.3, Corp −0.6: 6.05 + 3.70 + 0.3 − 0.6 = $9.45B → 17.9%. - Consensus of $9.574B with Elec at 21%, Wind +0.2 and Corp −0.74 needs Power at (9.574 + 0.74 − 3.53 − 0.2)/27.5 = 23.9%.
    8. Price sensitivity to the margin guide: - 1 pt of FY27 margin = 0.01 × 52,740 = $527M EBITDA. At 25x that is $13.2B of EV; /266.33M shares = $49.5/share (5.1% of $962.49). - A 17.0% midpoint vs 18.15%: −$607M → −$57/share (−5.9%) at 25x if the Street moves to the midpoint.
    9. Q9 statistics: - Sum of the 10 earnings-day moves = +24.78 → mean +2.48%. - Absolute sum 54.24 → mean 5.42%; median of the sorted absolutes (2.73, 3.07) = 2.90%. - Adding the two December events: (54.24 + 5.01 + 15.62)/12 = 6.24%.
    10. P(midpoint below consensus): P(<18%) = 5 + 10 + 25 + 30 = 70%, plus the part of the 18-19% bucket at exactly 18.0% (research judgement ≈ 10-12 of the 22) → ≈80%.

    Reasoning behind each bucket (research judgement): - <15% (5%): needs a Wind or Q4 execution problem, or a deliberately low guide. GEV has never cut company revenue or FCF guidance, and a guide below FY26's exit would contradict "'27 much better" for Wind. - 15-16% (10%): the straight line from FY26 actuals minus about 1 pt of cushion (Case A). This fits the "grounded" style and the CEO's timing of margin step-ups to '29-'30. - 16-17% (25%): the straight line (16.5-16.9%), or a 16-18% range. This is what a 2-pt range with its top near consensus looks like, and it leaves room under a 20% 2028 plan. - 17-18% (30%): centre of the "first guide vs prior Q4" history (17.8%) and Case B. It lets management guide a big step while keeping the 2028 framework credible before the CMD. - 18-19% (22%): mostly a 17-19% range (18.0% midpoint). It would be justified by the ~18% Q4'26 exit and H1'26 Power at 17.6-18.8%. It implies only about +2 pts to 2028, which effectively signals a framework raise. - ≥19% (8%): requires guiding above consensus and pulling 2028 forward. GEV did something similar with the margin at Q2'25 and Q1'26, but never on a first annual guide.

    What would change this

    Consensus drifts toward 16.5-17.5% before January (for example after the 2026-10-28 Q3 print). The surprise then shrinks, even if the probability that the guide is below today's 18.15% stays the same. The relevant benchmark is consensus on the eve of the call. - A December 2026 investor event is announced. The guide could move there, or come with a 2028 raise that offsets it (both prior first guides came in December). - Q3'26 comes in at or above the top of its guide, Q4 commentary points to ≥18%, and Power margin exceeds 19%. That raises the 18-19% and ≥19% weights. - Management raises the 2028 framework before or at the January call. A higher 2028 margin makes an 18%+ FY27 guide consistent with a straight line. - The primary transcript shows the "conservatism" quote in a different context or from a different speaker. That would weaken the Q2 evidence. - McDonough, not Parks, delivers the outlook, or GEV revises the transition plan. That would bring the new-CFO question back.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. "The first [call] under the new CFO (Claire McDonough)": contradicted by GEV's own release. Parks stays CFO "inclusive of the... fourth quarter earnings call[s]". McDonough becomes CFO on 1 Jan, but the outlook will have been built under Parks, who probably presents it. The two sources describe the title on the call date slightly differently (GEV release vs the 8-K's strategic-advisor-from-1-Jan wording). The team should not rely on a "new-CFO reset".
    2. "Adj EBITDA margin finished slightly BELOW the first numeric guide in both years": - The first FY24 and FY25 margin guides were qualitative ("MSD, higher end" and "HSD"), and both were met. - The numeric baselines (6.0%, 8.5%) were mid-year raised guides (research file BR-23, flagged as a definition mismatch). - FY26 is tracking above its first numeric midpoint (12%): consensus is 13.74%. - So "GEV never beats its first margin guide" is weaker than stated.
    3. "First FY26 guide" framing: the 12-14% margin came from a Q1'26 raise (2026-04-22, +13.75% day). It was then held at Q2 (−8.69%). The brief lists 12-14% only as "held".
    Open items

    Pre-guide margin consensus for FY25 (Dec-2024) and FY26 (Dec-2025): not found in free sources. Look in Bloomberg/FactSet snapshots or broker previews dated 2024-12-09 and 2025-12-08. - Second independent source for the $41.3B FY26 revenue consensus: Reuters/LSEG copy, 2025-12-09 (paywalled on MarketScreener). - The "some conservatism" quote: verify speaker and wording in gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_transcript_12092025.pdf. - Exact daily closes for the event days: confirm with a vendor (Yahoo chart API or Bloomberg), and compute peer- and market-adjusted moves. The corpus table is the only full source. - Segment-level FY27 consensus (Power, Electrification, corporate): not available free. GLJ's "20.7% Power 2027" is still unverified. A Power consensus of ~20.7% would imply a total well below 18.15% on the assumptions above, so either the aggregator totals or GLJ's figure is inconsistent. - Whether GEV announces a December 2026 investor event: check gevernova.com/investors/events after the Q3 call on 2026-10-28. - Implied volatility / options-implied move for the late-January expiry: not retrieved. It would be a useful market-based check on the reaction range.

    What 28x and 20x each require in Sep-2027

    AskedWhat would have to happen for GEV to hold ~28x NTM EV/EBITDA a year from now? For ~20x?

    Equipment vs services margin inside Power

    GEV Power segment: equipment vs services margins (FY23–H1'26), and whether GLJ's ~3 pts on old equipment holds up

    What we asked

    GEV does not disclose equipment and services margins inside the Power segment, yet the bull/bear debate is about equipment margins on old versus new orders. Close this gap as far as public evidence allows. Deliver the implied equipment margin path FY23-H1'26 under the range of services margins the evidence supports, and state whether GLJ's ~3 points on old equipment is plausible, implausible, or undeterminable.

    • Q1. Every statement in GEV filings, releases, investor-event decks (Dec 2024, Dec 2025), transcripts and conferences about equipment margins, services margins, "low single digit", "breakeven", "mid-teens", contribution margin, or margin by product line in Power — quoted with sources.
    • Q2. Siemens Energy Gas Services: service share, new-unit vs service margins, trend — two sources.
    • Q3. MHI Energy Systems and Baker Hughes IET/Gas Technology: equipment vs service margins.
    • Q4. Historic GE Power (pre-spin, e.g. 2015-2019 GE 10-Ks): equipment vs services profitability disclosure?
    • Q5. Solve the Power series (revenue split, segment EBITDA, FY23-H1'26) for implied equipment margin under each supported services-margin assumption. Show the grid.
    • Q6. What does a heavy-duty gas turbine unit sale typically earn versus its lifetime services (the "razor/razor-blade" economics)? Sources.
    • Q7. Is GLJ's ~3 points on old equipment plausible, implausible, or undeterminable — and why?

    Bottom line

    GEV's filings pin down the Power services margin better than the earlier work assumed. Since the ASU 2023-07 segment disclosure, Note 24 gives Power's cost of revenues (excluding D&A), SG&A, R&D and other items. The income statement gives company-wide services gross margin, and Note 24 gives services revenue for Wind and Electrification. Put together, these limit Power's services EBITDA margin to about 18–32%, central ~22–27%, in every period from FY23 to H1'26. With a constant services margin, the plausible band is the s=20–29% rows of the old grid, not 15–35%. [S1: FY25 10-K 0001996810-26-000015, Note 24 "SEGMENT EBITDA" tables, p.72] [S2: FY24 10-K 0001996810-25-000011, Note 24, same tables; Q2'26 10-Q 0001996810-26-000148, p.23] - Implied Power equipment EBITDA margin, central case: FY23 −27%, FY24 −13.5%, FY25 −4.8%, H1'25 −2.5%, H1'26 +3.6%, Q2'26 about +4%. Full ranges are in the Q5 grid (FY25 −13% to +3.5%; H1'26 −4% to +11%). Every scenario rises about 25–30 pts from FY23 to H1'26. This is research arithmetic; the team chooses the scenario (computed, Section 4). - Management's own history matches a thin-margin equipment book. In 2020 Strazik (then Gas Power CEO) described Gas Power's roughly $4B equipment business expanding margins "from low single digits to mid-single digits". In January 2026 GEV agreed its Power equipment backlog margin started at YE2022 "approximately breakeven". Neither statement gives a vintage margin level. [S1: UBS conference transcript, 2020-06-03, earningscalls.dev] [S2: GEV Q4'25 webcast transcript, 2026-01-28, gevernova.com] - GLJ's "3 pts" is described as "backlog margin", which is GEV's contribution-margin metric, not EBITDA. On that basis, GEV's slide data put the 2024 order vintage at about 5.5–7.5 pts above an ~breakeven YE22 base, and 2.5–10.5 pts once you allow ±3 pts of uncertainty in the base. Verdict: plausible as a low-end figure, not proven, and undeterminable as a point estimate. 3 pts is also exactly GEV's own FY24 year-over-year increment (+3), so GLJ may be reading a change as a level. [S1: Investing.com GLJ summary, 2026-09-14] [S2: GuruFocus/Yahoo, 2026-09-15; GEV 4Q'25 deck slide 5] - Peers disclose no equipment/services margin split either. Siemens Energy Gas Services (66% service, FY25 13.0% margin before special items) says its margin gains come mainly from new-unit backlog. In Q2 FY26 its service ratio fell from 67% to 57% with the margin "on a comparable level", which suggests new-unit margins on processed backlog are now close to the segment average. MHI says GTCC "original equipment margins at the time of order booking have improved significantly". [S1: SE CMD Gas Services deck, Nov 2025, slides 5/14] [S2: SE Annual Report 2025 Note 26; SE pre-close call transcript 2026-06-29; MHI FY2025 results Q&A] - The "razor/blade" economics are asserted, not quantified. The only direct management claim, from the December 2025 investor-update Q&A (speaker not verified), is that "the blade is still more lucrative than the razor in our gas business over the long term, including on an NPV basis." No public source splits unit-sale versus lifetime-service margin. [S1: corpus chunk 246348 (src:2686)] [SINGLE-SOURCE] for the quote; the direction is supported by the 2020 Strazik transcript and the GE Q4'23 call.

    Q7

    GLJ's ~3 pts on old equipment

    AskedIs GLJ's ~3 points on old equipment plausible, implausible, or undeterminable — and why?

    Verdict: undeterminable as a point estimate. Plausible only as a low-end figure on its own contribution basis. Why:

    1. Basis. GLJ's wording is "approximately 3 percentage points of backlog margin on the 2027 vintage" [Investing.com 2026-09-14; GuruFocus/Yahoo 2026-09-15]. That is GEV's contribution metric (Q1c), not EBITDA.
    2. As a level on the contribution basis: - The EDF-corrected 2024 vintage is about 7.5 pts above the YE22 base (about 5.5 pts under FIFO), per PMX-29. - The base is "approximately breakeven" but not exact. With b = −3 to +3, the 2024 vintage is about 2.5–10.5. - 3 pts is inside the envelope only at its low corner (FIFO plus a negative base).
    3. As an increment, it matches GEV's FY24 +3 exactly. GLJ may be citing the change as a level.
    4. As an EBITDA check: - H1'26 shipments are mostly older vintages (Q1b). They earn a central +3.6% equipment EBITDA (range −3.9% to +11.1%). - If the 2024 vintage earned ~3 pts of EBITDA, it would be no better than what ships today, which runs against the +8 pt within-equipment trend from FY25 to H1'26 (central case). - It is still possible if price gains are absorbed by cost inflation or tariffs.
    5. What matters for FY27 is the spread and the timing, not the level. The research has already established that the old-vs-new spread (~12–15 pts) is larger than GLJ's, and that management's timing statements favour GLJ.

    General questions answered along the way

    G2: Street FY27 Power ~20.7% (GLJ-sourced). The GAAP-anchored split says H1'26 equipment is about +4% EBITDA (central) and services about 26%. Reaching ~21% segment margin with equipment at ~40% of revenue needs equipment EBITDA of about 14% at s = 26% (computed: (0.207 − 0.6 × 0.26) / 0.4 = 12.75%; about 14% if s = 25%). That is roughly +9–10 pts more within-equipment gain in about 18 months, versus about +8 pts FY25→H1'26 (central). A similar pace has happened before, so this is not unprecedented. - G12: Deposits and percentage-of-completion revenue timing are unaffected by this split. The segment cost excludes D&A, so the equipment/services split lives in cost of revenues only. - G19: The GE gas equipment book ran low/mid single-digit margins in 2019–20, and "negative high single-digit" segment operating margins in 2018 (Strazik, 2020). Thin equipment margins are the historical norm outside booms. - G20: Definition traps: - "backlog margin" (contribution, average of the whole book) vs segment EBITDA; - GEV segment EBITDA vs SE profit before special items; - Note 24 external revenue (6,420) vs MD&A equipment including intersegment (6,686). - G21: If equipment were flat and services drove the gains, the company services gross margin would have needed to rise about 7–10 pts. It rose only +1.7 pts from H1'25 to H1'26 and fell from FY23 to FY25 (PMX-21/35). That points against services as the driver.

    Arithmetic

    Power segment gross profit ex-D&A = segment revenue − cost of revenues (Note 24). For FY25: 19,767 − 14,627 = 5,140 (26.0%).

    Opex = SG&A + R&D + other items. For FY25: 1,836 + 549 − 147 = 2,238 (11.32%). Check: 5,140 − 2,238 = 2,902 = reported EBITDA ✓. - Other periods: FY24 2,251 (12.42%); FY23 2,290 (13.13%); H1'26 1,104 (10.57%); H1'25 1,113 (12.05%); Q2'26 472 + 154 − 45 = 581 (10.6%).

    Consolidated services gross profit (incl. D&A): FY25 5,360; FY24 5,122; FY23 5,265; H1'26 2,755; H1'25 2,405; Q2'26 1,515.

    Non-Power services revenue (Note 24): FY25 4,026; FY24 3,565; FY23 3,221; H1'26 2,122; H1'25 1,801; Q2'26 1,128.

    Power services GP = consolidated services GP + d_s − g_n × non-Power services revenue. Unallocated "other" services revenue (36/14) is ignored.

    • FY25 central (d = 350, g = 25%): 5,360 + 350 − 1,006.5 = 4,703.5 → x = 35.96% of 13,081 → s = 35.96 − 11.32 = 24.64%.
    • Equipment GP = 5,140 − 4,703.5 = 436.5 → 6.53% of 6,686 → e = −4.79%.
    • Tie-out: 0.2464 × 13,081 − 0.0479 × 6,686 = 2,903 ✓.
    • FY25 corners (equipment GP margin): d200: 2.8 / 8.8 / 14.8% for g_n 15 / 25 / 35%; d350: 0.5 / 6.5 / 12.5%; d500: −1.7 / 4.3 / 10.3%. Subtract 11.32 for EBITDA.
    • H1'26 central (d = 175, g = 25%): 2,755 + 175 − 530.5 = 2,399.5 → x = 36.37% → s = 25.80%.
    • Equipment GP 545.5 / 3,851 = 14.17% → e = 3.60%.
    • Tie-out: 1,702 + 139 = 1,841 ✓.
    • Corners: equipment EBITDA from 0.0 / 5.6 / 11.1% (d100) to −3.9 / 1.7 / 7.2% (d250).
    • FY24 central: 5,122 + 350 − 891.25 = 4,580.75 → s = 24.47%; equipment GP −61.75 → e = −13.50%. Tie-out 2,268 ✓.
    • FY23 central: 5,265 + 350 − 805.25 = 4,809.75 → s = 27.50%; equipment GP −798.75 → e = −27.40%. Tie-out 1,721 ✓.
    • H1'25 central: 2,405 + 175 − 450.25 = 2,129.75 → s = 22.09%; equipment 286.25 → e = −2.50%. Tie-out 1,303 ✓.
    • Q2'26 central (d = 90): 1,515 + 90 − 282 = 1,323; equipment 1,611 − 1,323 = 288 / 1,965 = 14.7% → e ≈ 4.0%.

    GLJ contribution envelope: from PMX-29, v24 = (12,461 × 6 − 4,220 × 3) / 8,241 ≈ 7.5 pts above the base (FIFO ≈ 5.5). With the base b ∈ [−3, +3], the range is 2.5–10.5.

    What would change this

    Any disclosure of Wind or Electrification services margins, or of D&A inside cost of services, would narrow Method 2. A Wind services margin below 15% pushes Power services up and equipment down. - A GEV statement quantifying Gas Power equipment EBITDA or contribution margin (the January 2027 call or the spring-2027 Capital Markets Day) would supersede everything above. - GLJ's full note defining "backlog margin" as EBITDA, or as a level rather than an increment, would change the Q7 framing. - A Q3'26 Power margin of 17% or less with equipment-led revenue growth, or services-only MD&A drivers, would argue for a lower equipment margin. - A Q3'26 margin of 18% or more on revenue growth of +17% or more would argue for a higher one.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. "GEV does not disclose equipment vs services margins inside Power" is true, but Note 24 (ASU 2023-07) gives enough cost data to bound the split. Combined with the consolidated services gross margin, it limits services EBITDA to about 18–32% rather than leaving it a free assumption.
    2. The brief treats GLJ's "3 pts" as a margin on old equipment. GLJ calls it "backlog margin", so it should be tested against contribution-margin vintages, not EBITDA, and it is plausible at the low end of that range.
    3. PMX Grid A's footnote "Steam moved out" is wrong: Steam was realigned within Power (the verifier already flagged this).
    Open items

    d_s and the non-Power services margin: look for a DISE (ASU 2024-03) early adoption, or for any Wind/Electrification services margin commentary in the Dec-2024 and Dec-2025 investor decks, which the corpus search did not reach. - The 2020 UBS quote: find a second copy (ge.com transcript PDF) and confirm which margin definition Strazik meant. - The razor/NPV quote: confirm the speaker and page. The inpayvantage.com Dec-2025 transcript is a candidate; I did not read it all. - GLJ's full note: its definition of "backlog margin" and its FY27 Power build. - Other definitions: GE 10-K statements of the gas equipment margin before 2018; SE new-unit margin levels (not disclosed); MHI GTCC split (not disclosed). - Q3'26 10-Q (2026-10-28, after the finals): re-run Method 2 with the new Note 24 lines.

    Q5

    Which line moves the stock most

    AskedWhich reported line has moved the stock most on earnings days?

    • Margin guidance and EBITDA/EPS against consensus.
    • The three largest up-days all came with a margin raise: Q2'25 +14.58%, Q1'26 +13.75%, and the Dec-2025 framework day +15.62% (+6 margin points on the 2028 framework).
    • The largest down-day, Q2'26 at −8.69%, is the only print where revenue and FCF were raised but the margin guide was held and EPS missed.
    • Orders do not separate outcomes. Q1'26 orders +71% gave +13.75%. Q2'26 orders +88% gave −8.69%.
    • FCF does not either. The biggest FCF raise ever (+$5.0B at the midpoint, Q2'26) coincided with the worst print-day reaction.
    • Reaffirm-only days stayed within −1.6% to +3.1% in all five cases.
    • Caveat. n = 10. Returns are raw, with no measure of surprise size. Research's verifier concluded this supports "no reliable link" statistically, not causation (evidence_lanes, test 4 audit).
    • Research inference on Q2'26. The EBITDA miss was small: $1,250M actual vs a press figure of $1.28B, about −2.3%. The $1.28B is itself unverified (research RQ-32). Most of the EPS gap was below EBITDA. D&A was $418M vs $202M a year earlier, after Prolec (Q2 release reconciliation). The headline EPS line can "miss" even when EBITDA is roughly in line.

    EPS consistency check (research estimate): - Start from Q2's bridge (Q2 release reconciliation): D&A $418M; non-operating benefit income +$119M; net interest income +$73M; restructuring and separation about −$47M; tax rate about 30% ($279M on $928M pre-tax). - Consensus EBITDA of $1,706M then gives pre-tax income of about $1,433M. - Net income is about $1.00B at a 30% tax rate, or $1.07B at 25%. - Using Q2's EPS-to-net-income ratio (2.47/649), that is about $3.82–4.09. - So the $4.08 consensus is consistent with $1,706M EBITDA only at about a 25% tax rate or with other below-EBITDA help. At Q2's tax rate, EBITDA in line with consensus would still print EPS of about $3.8, roughly 7% below.

    What each outcome means for the positions (research framing, not a recommendation):

    • Long:
    • A beat plus a margin raise matches the only reaction pattern above +10%. It also puts H2 at the Street's 16.3% with evidence behind it.
    • In-line plus reaffirm has historically gone flat, between −1.6% and +3.1%.
    • A miss or held margin guide at ~2x the market multiple is the Q2'26 pattern (−8.69% that day, −12.55% over 5 days).
    • Short:
    • Q3 does not test the FY27 thesis; January does. A Q3 beat does not refute "Street 2027-28 margins ahead of management". It does weaken it if management raises FY26 margin or signals the 2028 framework moving toward consensus, for example by announcing a December event.
    • The in-quarter tells for a short:
      • the margin guide held while Q4 needs 18%
      • the Wind Q4 +$257M hurdle unchanged or widened
      • falling RPO conversion percentages
      • a Vineyard Wind charge
    • The risk for a short is that Q3 is the quarter management leaned into ("very strong" orders, gas "conservative"), and positive order/backlog headlines land 5 days after the pitch.
    Q7

    3. "GEV has raised at every print. Why would Q3 be different?" Base rate: both previous Q3 prints were reaffirms, and Q3'25 worsened the Wind guide.
    4. "Q2'26 raised FCF by $5B and the stock fell 8.7%. What does that tell you about what the market prices?" Tests Q5.
    5. "Wind needs +$257M in Q4. Has it ever done that?" Best quarter since the spin: +$19M. Also, the Vineyard Wind settlement cost.
    6. "Management says Q3 orders will be very strong and the $200B backlog comes early. Doesn't that break a short?" Separate orders and backlog, which are not in the model, from margin and timing.
    7. "What EPS basis is your consensus on?" GAAP-comparable. FY26 is either $15.4–15.5 or $30.5 depending on the Prolec gain.
    8. "Did buybacks in Q3 change your share count?" $3,037M left at 6/30; Q3 activity will be in the 10-Q.
    9. "The new CFO starts 11-01. Does that change the Q3 call or the January guide style?" Parks still reports Q3.

    General questions answered along the way

    G13 (dated reveal): Q3 on 10-28 tests the H2 path (Q4 at 18% margin, Wind +$257M) and prints RPO conversion. The FY27 test is the January call (Laguna p.10-11; MarketBeat). - G14 (what could push the reveal out): management's statement that 12 GW of contracting slips into Q4, and no December event listed. Q3'25 announced its December event in the release, so watch whether Q3'26 does the same. - G17 (management levers): buyback cadence, margin-guide wording, Wind charge placement and settlement disclosure; CFO handover. - G22 (what has to change): for the Street's H2 16.3% to hold, the FY margin guide must reach at least its upper half. A reaffirmed 12–14% leaves consensus needing the top. - G24 (cash): the Q3 FCF guide is only "positive". H2 FCF implied by the FY guide is $1.6–2.6B, against H1's $9.9B.

    Arithmetic

    H2 margin: (FY guide EBITDA − 2,146) / (FY revenue − 20,442). Corners shown in Q2. Consensus: (6,359 − 2,146) / (46,282 − 20,442) = 4,213 / 25,840 = 16.30%. - Q4 implied: revenue 46,282 − 20,442 − 12,013 = 13,827; EBITDA 6,359 − 2,146 − 1,706 = 2,507; 2,507 / 13,827 = 18.13%. - Wind: −400 − (−657) = +257 for H2. - Q3 range: see Q2 (inputs PP-12..17). - Guide percentile: (6,359 − 5,460) / (6,510 − 5,460) = 85.6%. - Q2 bridge check: 1,250 − 9 − 48 − 38 + 119 − 418 + 73 − 279 = 650, against a reported $649M. - Q3 EPS estimate: pre-tax = 1,706 − 418 + 119 + 73 − 47 = 1,433. Net income = 1,433 × (0.70–0.75) = 1,003–1,075. EPS = NI × (2.47 / 649) = $3.82–4.09. - Gas net add: 125 − 116 = +9 GW net. Plus ~10 GW shipped in H2 (5 GW × 2) gives ~19 GW gross, consistent with the ~20 GW H2 guide. - Earnings-day stats: sum of returns +24.78% / 10 = 2.48% mean; absolute sum 54.24 / 10 = 5.42%. - Buyback capacity: 3,037 / ~950 ≈ 3.2M shares.

    What would change this

    "Margin guide is the line that matters": a Q3 with a margin raise and a negative close, or a reaffirm with a ±10% move. - "Consensus at the top of the guide range": if MarketScreener or ChartMill revise Q3 EBITDA below $1,650M before 10-28, the bar resets. - EPS consistency check: if the Q3 tax rate or D&A differ materially from Q2 (for example, the Prolec amortization schedule). - Wind hurdle: if management widens the FY Wind loss (the Q3'25 precedent) while holding the company margin guide.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. H2 range. "13.2–16.9%" holds as stated. The low end is 13.2% with any revenue pairing (13.18% at high revenue). The high end drops to 16.75% if 14% is paired with top-end revenue.
    2. Q3 EBITDA. The brief says consensus "sits at the top" of the guide range. On ChartMill ($1,728M) it sits above the top ($1,716M). ChartMill's historical EBITDA basis also differs from GEV's adjusted basis.
    3. EPS basis. The brief's Q3 context gives no EPS. Quarterly consensus ($4.04–4.09) is GAAP-comparable, but FY26 EPS consensus comes on two bases ($15.4–15.5 vs $30.5). The brief's FY27 EPS figure ($24.85) should carry its basis; ChartMill shows $24.75 and Zacks $24.09.
    4. Q2'26 EPS consensus is not a single number: $3.04 vs $3.17 depending on source.

    Q4

    Definition traps (highest impact first):

    AskedWhich are definition traps (GAAP vs adjusted, gross vs EBITDA vs contribution margin, diluted vs outstanding, calendar vs fiscal)?

    1. FY26 EPS basis: GAAP-type $30.49 (Zacks) or $30.78 (MarketScreener) vs ex-items $15.16 (S&P). FY27 is consistent across vendors at $24.78–25.13.
    2. "Consensus EBITDA" means GEV-adjusted EBITDA. MarketScreener's FY24 and FY25 actuals ($2,035M and $3,196M) match GEV's adjusted figures exactly [Q4'25 release]. Segment EBITDA ≠ company adj EBITDA.
    3. GLJ's "38.9x forward EV/EBITDA" is the FY26 multiple, not FY27. Check: $247,230M ÷ $6,359M = 38.9x.
    4. Backlog margin vs segment margin. "Contribution margin in backlog, change vs prior year" (+11 pts Power FY25; "low double digits" at Laguna) is not a segment EBITDA margin.
    5. Cash of $13,120M includes restricted cash (~$0.4B). yfinance shows $12.72B. Debt of $2,849M excludes operating leases (~$0.87B). Together they move EV by +$1.3B (+0.5%).
    6. Shares: 266.33M outstanding vs 270M diluted weighted-average (−1.4% per share on the diluted count).
    7. 52-week high of $1,195.94 is intraday. The record close is $1,174.86, and the drawdowns are measured on closes.
    8. RPO "within 2 years" at 12/31/25 is calendar 2027 exactly. At 6/30/26 the 1–2-year bucket (65% − 36%) is mid-2027 to mid-2028, not calendar. It is all-segment equipment, not Power.
    9. The "20 GW run-rate" is 5 GW/quarter in Q3–Q4'26. Laguna says early 2027 "will feel generally very similar", with 6 GW/quarter "sometime in the second half of next year". That makes calendar-2027 output about 22 GW at most (research estimate, computed), not 24.
    Q5

    Which single error would flip the direction call.

    AskedWhich single error, if it exists, would change the direction call?

    The short lean rests on two legs: - (a) Street FY27–28 EBITDA sits above management's plan. This is robust: two vendors agree within ~1–2%, and FY28 is +16.6% over the framework either way. - (b) Management's own timing, where margin uplift lands in '29–'30. This is fragile: one document, and it maps the 2026 backlog-margin change to '29–'30. The claim that 2024 orders dominate FY27 margin is an extrapolation of that lag, not a statement.

    If the p.10 wording or context turns out to differ (for example, it refers only to 2026 SRA conversions, or the lag is shorter for aeroderivatives), the timing leg falls away. The case then reduces to the Street being above the plan, which the brief itself says is roughly fairly priced on the plan at ~23x. Re-read p.10 in full, and one independent transcript, before relying on it.

    General questions answered along the way

    G11 (physical constraint). Output steps up by ladder: 5 GW/quarter through early 2027, 6 GW/quarter from H2'27. That caps FY27 gas volume growth at roughly +14–26%, so FY27 Power growth needs price and mix as well as volume. [Laguna transcript, gevernova PDF and stockanalysis copy] - G12 (accounting timing). H1 FCF of $9,897M includes $13,695M of contract-liability inflow. Management guides H2 FCF much lower as SRAs convert to orders. [10-Q CF; Q2 transcript src:3161] - G13/G14 (catalyst). Q3 results are on 2026-10-28, after the finals [Kalkine 9/29; IR events]. The FY27 outlook and the 2026 backlog-margin change come on the January 2027 call [Laguna]. The new CFO starts 2027-01-01 [8-K -26-000153]. - G15 (downside path). The trough-to-date on the open drawdown was −25.5% on closes ($1,174.86 → $874.76). [Fool 9/29; stockanalysis history] - G20 (evidence quality). See the single-source list in Q2 and the definition traps in Q4.

    Arithmetic

    Market cap: 266,333,581 × 962.49 = $256,343M. EV: 256,343 + 2,849 + 1,158 − 13,120 = $247,230M. - Variant: exclude ~$400M restricted cash (13,120 − 12,720) and add ~$871M operating leases → ~$248.5B. - Power margins: 1,722/17,436 = 9.88%; 2,268/18,127 = 12.51%; 2,902/19,767 = 14.68%; 1,842/10,449 = 17.63%; 1,031/5,477 = 18.82%. - FCF check: 10,680 − 783 = 9,897. - 2027 equipment RPO: 64,245 × 0.32 = 20,558. Rounding band 31–33% gives 19,916–21,201. - Multiples: - FY27 EBITDA: 247,230 / 9,574 = 25.8x. At GLJ's Street figure: 247,230 / 9,450 = 26.2x. - FY26 EBITDA: 247,230 / 6,359 = 38.9x (matches GLJ's "38.9x forward"). - P/E: 962.49 / 24.85 = 38.7x; / 25.13 = 38.3x; / 24.78 = 38.8x. - FY28 cross-check: 3,196 × 1.6³ = 13,091 vs 13,064 (−0.2%). - Consensus vs framework: FY28 13,064 / 11,200 = +16.6%. On GLJ's FY27 Street figure the gap is unchanged; FY28 has no second level source. - GLJ gap: 7,420 / 9,450 − 1 = −21.5%. GuruFocus rounds this to "22%". - GLJ-day moves: 874.76 / 957.27 − 1 = −8.62%. 9/29: 962.49 / 949.77 − 1 = +1.34%. - Implied H2'26 FCF at guide midpoint: 12,000 − 9,897 ≈ $2.1B. This fits the CFO's "first half … substantially higher than the second half". - Gas output (research estimate, computed from Laguna): 2026 ≈ 7.5 (H1 actual) + 5 + 5 = 17.5 GW. 2027 at most 5 + 5 + 6 + 6 = 22 GW, i.e. +14% to +26% year on year.

    What would change this

    p.10 wording. If the full Laguna text limits "'29 and '30" to 2026 SRA conversions, or to heavy-duty gas only, the timing leg weakens. - A second consensus EBITDA feed. If Visible Alpha, FactSet or Bloomberg shows FY27 below ~$9.2B or FY28 below ~$12.5B, the "Street above plan" gap shrinks by a third or more. - The Q3 10-Q (after 10/28). New RPO conversion percentages and Q3 buyback counts will make the share count and RPO buckets stale.

    Disagreements with the master brief

    The 2027 RPO bucket is shown to the dollar. It is ±~$0.6B from rounding and covers all segments. It should be presented as a range (research estimate). - "20 GW/yr run-rate from Q3'26" should not be read as 2027 output of 20+ GW rising fast. Laguna implies about 22 GW at most for calendar 2027. - The "'29–'30" quote is listed as verified. On two-source standards it is single-source. - GLJ's FY27 build figures are single-wire, even though facts.csv marks them "verified". - FY26 EPS labels: the brief's P/E framing should state the basis. FY27 is consistent across vendors; FY26 is not. - Minor: corpus src:2660 is dated 2026-01-23, but the Q4'25 call was on 2026-01-28.

    Judge Q&A preparation for both directions

    GEV Q&A preparation for both pitch directions: research input only, as of 2026-09-30

    What we asked

    Prepare the team for a 10-minute Q&A with Citadel PMs, for BOTH a short and a long version of the pitch. Use search_pitch_winners for the questions judges actually asked winners, and the verified research for GEV specifics. For each direction: the 25 hardest questions, ordered by likelihood x damage. For each: (a) the facts and numbers an answer would rest on, with two citations each; (b) the weakest point in that answer — where a follow-up would hurt; (c) the one piece of evidence that would most strengthen it. No scripted answers — facts and weak points only.

    • Q1. What in guidance or consensus must change, and when?
    • Q2. Why is the price move you expect larger than your estimate gap?
    • Q3. How do you treat SBC, deposits and cash conversion?
    • Q4. What if management buys back less, or does an acquisition?
    • Q5. Why hasn't the market seen your point? Who is on the other side of your trade?
    • Q6. Is the Power margin climb price, mix or productivity?
    • Q7. What is your kill rule, and when would you know?
    • Q8. What happens at Q3 (2026-10-28)?
    • Q9. What does the stock's own history say about your downside?
    • Q10. Did you use AI, and what did you verify by hand?
    • Q11-Q25. Add the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.
    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    This is research input, not memo text. Every probability is research judgement. Every forecast range is labelled "team's choice". I've written no answer scripts, only the facts an answer would rest on and where it breaks.

    Bottom line

    The first question in both directions is the gap between the Street and management's plan. - Consensus FY27 adjusted EBITDA is $9,574M (18.15% margin). - A straight line from the FY26 guide midpoint ($5,980M) to the 2028 framework ($11.2B) gives about $8.59B. - Consensus FY28 of $13,064M is 16.6% above the framework. - Sources: [S1: MS] [S2: GF-GLJ, which puts the "Street" at $9.45B, within 1.3%]; framework [S1: REL4Q25] [S2: Prolec news, corpus src:3806]. - A short has to explain why that gap closes downward in January. A long has to explain why the Street, not management, is right. - The single most damaging follow-up for the short is not about evidence. It is the +39% NTM EBITDA roll-forward. - On consensus, the stock is flat at 20.3x NTM in Sep-2027 [computed from MS, §4-A3]. - So the short needs an estimate cut AND a de-rating. GLJ's 8.6% drop was 106% recovered within about 11 sessions [S1: BX] [S2: Motley Fool, 2026-09-14]. - The single most damaging follow-up for the long is "what is your variant view?" - A long built on consensus numbers is a pure multiple bet at 38.7x FY27 EPS, about 2x the S&P [S1: MS] [S2: FactSet mean $24.78 via cnyes; D08]. - The winners' study shows judges press exactly this ("your beat is 16%; why is the upside 63%?", asked of the Baker Hughes team) [S1: winners_playbook §6] [S2: psc-2026-bkr transcript]. - Correction to the brief: the "new CFO" angle is weaker than stated. Ken Parks stays CFO "through 2026 inclusive of the third and fourth quarter earnings calls" and the 2026 10-K. McDonough formally becomes CFO on 2027-01-01. - Sources: [S1: GEV release, 2026-08-27] [S2: CFO Dive, 2026-08-28] [S3: 8-K 0001996810-26-000153, Item 5.02]. - New accounting fact that bears on the GLJ "shipping" framing. Gas equipment revenue and margin are recognised over time, by percentage of completion (costs incurred), not at shipment [S1: 10K25 Note 1, revenue recognition, offset ~250k]. - So "2027 ships a 2024-priced book" really means 2027 recognises cost-to-date on those contracts. The RPO 1/2/5-year schedule already reflects that [S2: 10K25 Note 9 RPO paragraph, "expected to be recognized within 1, 2, and 5 years"]. - History cuts both ways. In the 2001–02 US gas bubble, GE Power Systems earnings kept growing in 2002 (+29%) and fell only in 2003. Cancellations showed up first as termination-fee income: a $70M after-tax benefit in Q2'02. - Sources: [S1: GE 2003 annual report financial section, SEC 0000797463-04-000012 ex99b] [S2: GE Q2'02 earnings release, SEC 0000040545-02-000031]; order-collapse forecast of 80% or more [S3: GE Power Systems release, 2002-07-23]. - Implication: a demand turn shows up in orders and SRAs before EBITDA. That makes a 12-month EBITDA-based short harder, and makes orders/SRA conversion the long's key leading indicator.

    Answers 26

    Q1

    What in guidance or consensus must change, and when?

    AskedWhat in guidance or consensus must change, and when?

    (a) Facts

    The FY27 guide event - No FY27 guidance exists yet. The FY27 outlook comes on the late-January 2027 call: "We'll also provide you a '27 financial outlook in our January earnings call" [S1: LAG] [S2: InsiderFinance, 2026-09-16, "January 2027 call to provide detailed 2027 guidance and equipment-margin expectations"]. - GEV guides margin in whole-number ranges 1–2 points wide: 5–7%, 8–9%, 11–13%, 12–14% [S1: REL2Q26 guidance box and prior releases] [S2: Dec-2025 investor update; TheFly/TipRanks, 2026-04-22; via D04]. - So consensus of 18.15% is matched only by a guide with a low end of at least 18%. A 17–19% range has an 18.0% midpoint, about $79M below consensus [computed, §4-A5].

    FY26 guide vs consensus - The FY26 guide is margin 12–14% on revenue of $45.5–46.5B [S1: REL2Q26] [S2: Reuters, 2026-07-22]. - H2 margins implied by the guide run 13.2–16.9% (midpoint 15.0%), against 16.3% implied by consensus [computed, §4-A4; inputs S1: 10Q2Q26 H1 non-GAAP table] [S2: MS].

    No cushion before January - The first FY25 and FY26 guides came at December investor events, each paired with a framework raise. Reaction days were +5.01% (2024-12-11) and +15.62% (2025-12-10) [S1: corpus price table, BR-36] [S2: Proactive and Morningstar, 2025-12-10]. - No December 2026 event is listed. The 2030 outlook waits for a spring-2027 Capital Markets Day [S1: LAG p.10–11] [S2: InsiderFinance, 2026-09-16].

    What each side needs - Short: a FY27 guide midpoint below 18.15% and no framework raise. - Long: a guide low end of 18% or higher, or a 2028 framework raised to Street levels (about 21.6%) at the spring CMD.

    (b) Weakest point. GEV's revenue guides tend to land at or above consensus (first guides were beaten by +1.3% in FY24 and +4.3% in FY25) [S1: REL4Q25] [S2: facts BR-21]. So a margin miss can come with an EBITDA-dollar match. A PM will ask: "what if it's 17–19% on $54B?" That is roughly $9.7B, in line.

    (c) Would most strengthen it. Any management statement on FY27 margin or the phasing of 2027 equipment margin. At the Q3 call (10-28), watch whether management frames 2027 against the 2028 framework.

    Q2

    Why is the price move you expect larger than your estimate gap?

    AskedWhy is the price move you expect larger than your estimate gap?

    (a) Facts - The price move is the estimate change times the multiple change. - A 10% FY27 cut at a constant 25x gives about −9.6% vs the 25x-consensus value [computed, §4-A6]. - The same cut plus a de-rating to 22x gives $746 (−22.5% vs $962.49) [computed]. - GEV has de-rated fast before. - NTM EV/EBITDA troughs: 15.6x (2025-04-04), 22.8x (DeepSeek day), 25.4x (2026-09-14) [S1: Chartloom via D05] [S2: point-in-time P/E cross-checks on Yahoo; D05]. [Near SINGLE-SOURCE for EV/EBITDA history: only Chartloom.] - Five closing drawdowns of 15% or more; median −24.6% [S1: Yahoo chart API] [S2: Nasdaq historical]. - Long version. The upside comes mostly from the roll-forward (+39%), not from a beat. - Sep-2027 at 22x on consensus NTM $12,191M is $1,041 (+8.2%) [computed from MS]. - The consensus target of $1,237 equals about 26.3x NTM [S1: D05, from MS] [S2: TIKR, 2026-09-21].

    (b) Weakest point. - Short: the only evidence for de-rating is analogy (own drawdowns, peer multiples). Cautious-guide analogues (−8.69%, −8.6%) partly reversed within days [S1: BX] [S2: Reuters, 2026-07-22]. - Long: the upside rests entirely on the multiple holding at 22x or more, with no beat.

    (c) Would most strengthen it. A guide-day analogue where GEV (or Siemens Energy) de-rated and did not recover within 30 days. None has been found in GEV's 10 earnings days.

    Q3

    How do you treat SBC, deposits and cash conversion?

    AskedHow do you treat SBC, deposits and cash conversion?

    (a) Facts - SBC (pre-tax): FY24 $155M, FY25 $257M, H1'26 $135M [S1: 10K25 equity statement] [S2: 10Q2Q26 equity statement]. - GEV's adjusted EBITDA reconciliation has no general SBC add-back. The separation-cost add-back ($180M FY25, $61M H1'26) includes a "one-time stock option grant" [S1: REL2Q26 footnote (a)] [S2: 8-K Q2'25 release, 0001996810-25-000132, same footnote]. Both sources are the same issuer, so independence is weak. - FY25 SBC was 8.0% of adjusted EBITDA; H1'26 was 6.3%. Capitalised at 25x, FY25 SBC is about $24 a share [computed]. - Deposits. - The H1'26 contract-liability inflow in operating cash flow was $13,695M; OCF was $10,680M; so OCF ex-deposits was −$3,015M [S1: 10Q2Q26 cash-flow statement] [S2: Q2 call on mechanism only: "received a significant amount of down payments"]. The $13,695M line itself is [SINGLE-SOURCE] (10-Q only). - Current contract liabilities are $39.9B (Power $27.7B) vs cash of $13.1B, about 3.0x [S1: 10Q2Q26 Note 9] [S2: 10K25 Note 9 base $25.8B]. - Cash conversion. - FCF/adjusted EBITDA: FY25 1.16x; H1'26 4.61x [computed; S1: REL4Q25] [S2: REL2Q26]. - Consensus FCF falls from FY26 $12,017M to FY27 $7,417M (−38%) [S1: MS] [SINGLE-SOURCE; stockanalysis/S&P paywalls FY27].

    (b) Weakest point. Deposits are real, non-refundable cash. SRA deposits are "non-refundable" per a third-party customer, Maxim Power [S1: Maxim release, corpus src:232] [S2: corpus src:238 explainer]. A PM can argue net cash of $9.1B belongs to shareholders. Treating it as debt-like takes about $34 a share off at the net-cash line [computed: $9,113M / 266.33M].

    (c) Would most strengthen it. Q3 10-Q contract-liability roll: whether inflows slow as H2 commitments fall below H1's ~40 GW [LAG p.3; the H1 ~40 GW figure is SINGLE-SOURCE].

    Q4

    What if management buys back less, or does an acquisition?

    AskedWhat if management buys back less, or does an acquisition?

    (a) Facts - Buybacks. - H1'26: 4,266,417 shares for $3,645M, average $854.43. Cumulative $6,963M; $3,037M remaining at 6/30 [S1: 10Q2Q26 Part II Item 2 / Note 17] [S2: TradingView, 2026-07-23, Q2 "~2.5M shares for ~$2.3B"]. - Cumulative plus remaining is $10.0B [computed]. - The remaining $3,037M at $962.49 buys about 3.16M shares, 1.2% of the share count [computed]. - The CEO called Q3 "another good opportunity" for buybacks [S1: LAG] [S2: MB-LAG, via D07]. - Diluted weighted-average shares: 270M in Q2'26 vs 276M in Q2'25 (−2.2%) [S1: 10Q2Q26 Note 18] [S2: release-implied $668M / $2.47 = 270.4M]. - M&A. - Prolec GE remaining 50% bought for $5,254M cash ($9,656M total consideration).     Q6

    Is the Power margin climb price, mix or productivity?

    AskedIs the Power margin climb price, mix or productivity?

    (a) Facts - Power segment EBITDA margin: 9.88% (FY23), 12.51% (FY24), 14.68% (FY25), 17.63% (H1'26), 18.82% (Q2'26) [S1: 10K25 / 10Q2Q26 segment tables] [S2: REL2Q26; Q2 call "320 basis points to 18.8%"]. - Not segment mix. Or YE26 gas contracts below 125 GW [S1: REL2Q26 "at least 125 GW"] [S2: Utility Dive, 2026-07-23]. - Earlier read, Q3 on 10-28 (after the finals): the FY26 margin guide stays at 12–14% vs a raise.

    What happens at Q3 (2026-10-28)?

    AskedWhat happens at Q3 (2026-10-28)?

    (a) Facts - Date: 2026-10-28, 7:30am EDT [S1: Kalkine, 2026-09-29] [S2: ChartMill; InsiderFinance]. - Consensus - Revenue $12.01–12.12B [S1: MS] [S2: ChartMill; Zacks $12.07B]. - Adjusted EBITDA $1,706M / $1,728M [S1: MS] [S2: ChartMill]. - EPS $4.08–4.09 on a GAAP basis [S1: Zacks/Yahoo, 2026-09-16] [S2: ChartMill]. - EPS revisions −1.5% to −2.9% over the last month [S1: ChartMill] [S2: Zacks]. - The rebuilt guide range ($1,535–1,716M) puts consensus at its top [D07, from Q2 call segment guides] [S2: REL2Q26]. - Management framing - "Very strong" Q3 orders [S1: LAG] [S2: TIKR article]. - H2 commitments of about 20 GW "likely… conservative" [S1: LAG] [S2: TIKR / MB-LAG]. - Shipments at 5 GW a quarter vs 3.3 GW in Q2 [S1: LAG p.4] [S2: MB-LAG]. - Past Q3 prints only reaffirmed guidance: +1.25% and −1.59%. The Q2'26 print closed −8.69% after missing adjusted-EBITDA estimates [S1: corpus prices, BX-13] [S2: Reuters, 2026-07-22, "misses core profit estimates as Wind weakness persists"]. - The Q3 10-Q prints new data points: - 9/30 RPO conversion percentages - Q3 buyback - possibly a Vineyard Wind settlement charge (terms confidential) [S1: GEV release, 2026-09-16] [S2: Reuters, 2026-09-16].

    (b) Weakest point. Q3 comes after the finals, so the team cannot show it. Consensus sitting at the top of the range cuts both ways: a small beat is possible if Wind recovers.

    (c) Would most strengthen it. Q3 Wind EBITDA. The guide needs about break-even in Q3 and about +$257M across H2 [S1: REL2Q26 Wind table] [S2: New Energy Weekly, 2026-07-23, H1 −$657M].

    Q9

    What does the stock's own history say about your downside?

    AskedWhat does the stock's own history say about your downside?

    (a) Facts - Drawdowns: −38.3% ($437.71 → $270.13, Jan–Mar 2025), −17.5%, −15.0%, −24.6%, and an open −25.5% ($1,174.86 on 6/30 → $874.76 on 9/14). The stock is −18.1% from that peak today [S1: Yahoo chart API] [S2: Nasdaq historical]. - Three of the five drawdowns came while the S&P rose [same sources]. - Short-side risk: the 52-week high of $1,195.94 is +24% from here [S1: ad-hoc-news, 2026-08-25] [S2: brief/yfinance]. - Day moves: DeepSeek day −21.5%; GLJ day −8.6% [S1: Motley Fool] [S2: BX]. - Multiple history: NTM P/E since the spin runs 33.75–68.94x, median 50.85x; today about 46.85x [S1: Chartloom] [S2: Yahoo point-in-time spot checks 49.4x/40.4x; D05]. Chartloom is not point-in-time.

    (b) Weakest point. Every past drawdown recovered to new highs. The history supports "volatile", not "permanently re-rated".

    (c) Would most strengthen it. An out-of-sample analogue. GE's multiple went from 42.6x FY01 EPS (Aug-2000) to 21.1x (Apr-2002) while EPS rose 19% [S1: GE 2000/2002 ex-99b on SEC] [S2: NY Post, 2002-04-16; via D05].

    GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask

    AskedAdd the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.

    Q11

    Half of the 116 GW is reservations. What if SRAs don't convert?

    AskedAdd the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.

    • (a) Facts
    • Q2'26: 20 GW signed (18 SRA + 2 orders), 10 GW converted, 3 GW shipped; 53 GW backlog + 63 GW SRAs [S1: REL2Q26] [S2: Utility Dive, 2026-07-23].
    • SRAs are 54.3% of GEV's total vs 27.4% at Siemens Energy (26 of 95 GW) [S1: SE Q3 FY26 presentation p.6] [S2: REL2Q26].
    • RPO excludes orders cancellable "without incurring a substantive penalty" [S1: 10K25 MD&A RPO definition]. Risk factor: "slot reservation agreements may not result in orders" [S2: 10K25 Item 1A].
    • (b) Weak point. A cumulative SRA conversion rate is not disclosed. Deposits are non-refundable, but the size of deposit relative to turbine price is not public.
    • (c) Strengthen. Q3/Q4 SRA-to-order conversion GW. Management said more than half of 2031 slots would be sold by YE26 [S1: Utility Dive, 2026-07-23] [S2: thegridreport, 2026-07-23].
    Q12

    Can the factory actually deliver 20 → 24 GW?

    AskedAdd the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.

    • (a) Facts
    • 20 GW annual output from Q3'26, 24 GW in 2028, 30 GW by 2030 [S1: REL2Q26] [S2: LinkedIn post by the CEO, 2026-07-22].
    • Q2 shipped 3.3 GW vs 5 GW a quarter targeted for Q3–Q4 [S1: LAG p.4] [S2: MB-LAG].
    • Industry casting bottleneck: GE Aerospace agreed to buy CPP for about $11.75B; "severe casting capacity shortages through 2030" [S1: corpus src:3864, 2026-09-06] [S2: corpus src:3849, 2026-08-30].
    • (b) Weak point. GEV's specific casting suppliers and exposure are not disclosed. The link is inferred.
    • (c) Strengthen. Q3 gas units/GW shipped in the Q3 release.
    Q13

    Isn't this 2001 again?

    AskedAdd the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.

    • (a) Facts
    • GE Power Systems forecast US gas turbine orders and shipments down "80 percent or more over the next two years" and cut 2,500 jobs [S1: GE release, 2002-07-23].
    • About 46,000 MW of gas projects were shelved or cancelled from Nov-2001 to Sep-2002 [S2: Power Engineering, 2002-09].
    • Power Systems earnings still rose 29% in 2002 before dropping in 2003 [S1: GE 2003 ex99b]. Q2'02 included a $70M after-tax benefit from order terminations [S2: GE Q2'02 release].
    • Today: BNEF says announced expansions lift global output by more than half by 2030, and "today's scarcity could become tomorrow's overcapacity" [BNEF, 2026-09-10] [SINGLE-SOURCE for the figure].
    • (b) Weak point. Today's buyers are regulated utilities and hyperscalers, not 2001-style merchant IPPs. The analogy's customer mix differs. GE shipped more than 60 GW in 2001 [corpus src:296] [SINGLE-SOURCE].
    • (c) Strengthen. 2001–02 order data from GE 10-Ks (open item).
    Q14

    What does percentage-of-completion accounting do to *when* the old book shows up?

    AskedAdd the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.

    • (a) Facts
    • Equipment revenue is recognised over time as costs are incurred: "percentage of completion method, which is based on our costs incurred to date" [S1: 10K25 Note 1].
    • Liquidated-damages estimates are included in variable consideration [S1: same]. The RPO schedule shows 37%/69%/97% recognised within 1/2/5 years [S2: 10K25 Note 9].
    • Cumulative catch-ups on estimate changes hit current-period margin (the CSA line in Q6).
    • (b) Weak point. The over-time vs point-in-time split is not disclosed. How much of 2027 margin is already "baked" at YE26 is unknowable from outside.
    • (c) Strengthen. The 9/30 RPO percentages in the Q3 10-Q.
    Q15

    GLJ says 3 points on 2024 orders. Right or wrong?

    AskedAdd the 15 hardest GEV-specific questions a Citadel PM would ask (physics, accounting, competition, customers, policy), each with the same (a)(b)(c) treatment.

    General questions answered along the way

    G1. Holding $962.49 at 20.3x in Sep-2027 needs consensus FY28 of $13.1B (21.6% margin on $60.5B), plus gas output of about 20–24 GW (A3; REL2Q26; LAG). - G5.     Bottom line

    The evidence is close to a coin flip. It tilts slightly long (p_long ≈ 0.52), and I have low conviction (2/5). This disagrees with the brief's lean of 55–60% short; the reasons are in §7. - The gap between the evidence and consensus is real but small next to the multiple. - My FY27 adjusted EBITDA base is about $8.8B, roughly 8% below the MarketScreener consensus of $9,574M. It sits between the straight-line path to management's plan ($8.2–8.8B) and the bottom-up build ($8.7B) [D03 §1; D01 §1]. - At a constant NTM multiple, that cut is about the same size as the roll-forward from the current NTM (about $8.77B) to FY27. So by January a short needs the stock to de-rate as well, not just the estimates to fall [computed, A3]. - The short rests on FY27. The 12-month price rests on FY28 and later, and the evidence on those years leans constructive. - The CEO says the 2026 change in backlog margin will be larger than 2025's "low double digits", and called the equipment-margin growth "a floor with an opportunity for it to be substantially higher" [Q2'26 call transcript, corpus src:3796] [Laguna PDF p.5, 2026-09-16; facts PP-04]. - The spring-2027 Capital Markets Day with a 2030 outlook falls inside the horizon [facts CT-39, Laguna PDF] [corpus src:1747, 2026-09-17]. - Both of GEV's past organic framework events raised targets, and the stock rose +5.01% and +15.62% on the days after [facts BR-38/BR-28] [Proactive 2025-12-10 via D04]. - To be flat in 12 months, the stock needs about 22x NTM EBITDA on FY28 EBITDA about 5% above management's $11.2B framework. - That means the Street does not have to be fully right (consensus FY28 is $13,064M, +16.6%). But the multiple has to fall no further than about 22x from 28.2x today [computed, A2]. - The drawdown record makes a short painful to hold, and a long painful when it goes wrong. - Five closing drawdowns of 15% or more since the spin, median −24.6% [facts BX-03..08, Yahoo and Nasdaq closes]. The worst was −38.3% [same sources]. - The GLJ-day drop of −8.6% had been 106% recovered by 2026-09-29 [brief §5] [TIKR 2026-09-27: close $957.63 on 9/25].

    Arithmetic

    Straight-line FY27: FY26 $5,980M (guide midpoint, 13% × $46.0B) or $6,359M (MS); FY28 $11,200M. The midpoints are $8,590M and $8,780M. D03's $8.2–8.8B band is not the plain midpoint: it follows from D03's own path assumptions. - Value per share = (multiple × EBITDA + 9,113) / 266.33: - 25 × 10,600 = 265,000 → $1,029 - 23 × 10,600 → $950 - 20 × 10,600 → $830 - 24 × 10,825 → $1,010 - 22 × 10,825 → $928 - 26 × 10,825 → $1,091 - Brief's NTM check: 0.25 × 9,574 + 0.75 × 11,200 = 10,794, which confirms it embeds consensus FY27. - Accrued cash: 12,017 − 9,897 = 2,120; plus 0.75 × 7,417 = 5,563; total 7,683 / 266.33 = $28.8/share.

    Against the long: a FY27 guide midpoint ≤16%, or the stock breaking below its 2026-06-10 low of $867 on a sector de-rating (10-year at 5%). - For a stronger long: a 2026 backlog-margin change well above 11 pts, or a framework lift at the CMD.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. Who presents the January guide. The FY27 guide will not be the new CFO's first print: Parks stays through the Q4 call [GEV release; CFO Dive]. That weakens the "new CFO reset" angle.
    2. The "management's plan" NTM of $10,794M. It uses consensus FY27. With a plan-consistent FY27 it is about $10.6B, lowering each valuation row by about $18–30.
    3. The direction. The brief's short lean judges value at a January frame (FY27 multiple). Over 12 months, the roll-forward and the history of positive guide days make the long slightly more likely. This rests on research judgement, not new data.
    Open items

    A second EBITDA consensus vendor (Visible Alpha or LSEG). - GLJ's full note. - The margin split inside Power between services and equipment. - Whether a December 2026 investor event will be held (check the GEV IR events page). - Q3'26 buybacks: the 10-Q is due 2026-10-28.

    General questions answered along the way

    G5 (stock flat for 12 months): by construction, a flat price on the plan path means the multiple compresses to ~23x NTM [computed]. - G7 (why the market hasn't seen it): interpretation, not information (R5). - G19 (historical analog): see R12. - G23 (why the price move is bigger or smaller than the estimate gap): the multiple swing (±$100 a share) dominates the estimate gap (~$60 a share).

    Arithmetic

    Market cap and EV today - Market cap = 962.49 × 266.33 = $256,340M. - EV = 256,340 − 9,113 = $247,227M.

    NTM EBITDA - Today: $8,755M [VF-08]. - Research path at Sep-2027 = 0.25 × 8,900 + 0.75 × 11,600 = $10,925M, i.e. +24.8% vs $8,755M. - Research FY28 base = $56B × 1.035 (the historical revenue beat, taken between +1.3% and +4.3%) × 20% = $11.6B. This is a research estimate; the team chooses.

    Net cash at Sep-2027 - 9,113 + H2'26 FCF (12,000 guide midpoint − 9,897 H1) + 0.75 × 7,417 (FY27 consensus FCF) − ~530 dividends ($2.00 × 266M; P3, period unverified) ≈ $16.2B. - Buybacks are treated as neutral per share. - Caveat: much of this cash is customer deposits (contract liabilities). Excluding the build, $9.1B of net cash lowers every value by ~$27 a share.

    Value per share - Formula: value = (multiple × NTM EBITDA + 16,200) / 266.33. - Research base: 20x $881; 22x $963; 23x $1,004; 25x $1,086. - Consensus path at 23x: (280,393 + 16,200) / 266.33 = $1,114.

    Price-flat multiples - On the plan path, price-flat needs 247,227 / 10,794 = 22.9x. - On consensus, it needs 247,227 / 12,191 = 20.3x.

    Estimate gaps - FY27: 8,900 / 9,574 − 1 = −7.0%. - FY28: 11,600 / 13,064 − 1 = −11.2%.

    Rough scenario expected value (research judgement): 30% × $1,160 + 40% × $985 + 30% × $805 ≈ $983 before cash build, i.e. +2%. That is why p_long is only 0.53.

    What would change this

    Toward a short: - The January guide midpoint ≤16.5%. - The ≥125 GW target missed. - Visible SRA cancellations or deferrals, which is the 2001–02 pattern. - An NTM multiple below 20x on unchanged numbers, driven by rates or AI-capex sentiment. - Toward a stronger long: - A FY27 margin guide ≥18%. - The CMD's 2030 outlook implying FY28 of ≥$13B. - Q3 EBITDA at or above $1,706M with Power ≥19%.

    Disagreements with the master brief

    Direction. The brief leans short at 55–60%. I lean a thin long at 0.53. The brief's estimate evidence is right, but its price mechanism (the January guide causing a de-rating) has no precedent at GEV. The evidence available shows cautious-margin days being bought back. - CFO. The January call is presented with Parks still CFO, not McDonough alone [GEV release 2026-08-27; CFO Dive 2026-08-28]. The "new CFO resets expectations" angle is weaker than the brief says. - Consensus target. $1,237.34 is panel-specific. MarketBeat shows $1,145.83.

    Open items

    A second vendor for FY27/FY28 EBITDA consensus (try Visible Alpha, or the LSEG/Refinitiv panel via Reuters). - GE Power's 2017–19 share-price path vs its orders, as a second analog. - Peer forward EV/EBITDA for Siemens Energy and Vertiv, to anchor the 20–25x band (not found). - H2'26 commitments vs H1's 40 GW needs a second source (the Q3 call on 2026-10-28). - The dividend-per-share period for the net-cash bridge (10Q-2Q26 equity note).

Cancellations hit from late 2001 to April 2002 as merchant-developer financing broke [powerengineeringint.com 2002-01; Fortnightly 2002-06; power-eng.com 2002-06]. - 2017–18: GE sold 12 gas turbines in Q1'18 vs 20 a year earlier, followed by a ~$23B writedown [FT 2018; Boston Globe 2018-10-01]. - Lesson: both busts started with orders falling.
