    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    This is research input only. Probabilities, ranges and EBITDA paths are research estimates. The team chooses its own numbers and writes its own words.

    Bottom line

    I would fund the short, but only as a small, time-limited position that runs into the January 2027 FY27 outlook. I would not fund the 12-month long. My probability that the long works is about 0.43, so this is barely better than a coin flip. - The long is a bet on the multiple using consensus numbers, with no view that differs from the Street. - The short leans on management's own documents but works against a +39% NTM EBITDA roll-forward. - The best-evidenced gap is FY27 adjusted EBITDA. Consensus is $9,574M, an 18.15% margin [MarketScreener, 2026-09-29]. GLJ's "Street" figure is $9,450M [Yahoo/Investing.com, 2026-09-14]. A straight line from the FY26 guide midpoint ($5,980M) to the 2028 framework ($11,200M) gives about $8.6B, which is 10% below consensus. - Sources: 8-K 0001996810-26-000147 guidance box; 8-K -26-000012; Prolec news, corpus src:3806. - Consensus FY28 of $13,064M is 16.6% above management's own $11.2B plan. Management raised that plan organically only at December investor events, and no December 2026 event is listed. - As I read the evidence, the most likely January outcome is a margin guide below 18.15% with revenue at or above consensus. An earlier run tonight put P(guide midpoint below 18.15%) at about 85% [D04]. That is research judgement, not data. - Every past guide or framework day closed up (4 of 4). - The ones I'd compare it with fell only 8.6–8.7% and partly reversed within days. - The long side's strongest points are real but already in the price: - Power segment margin went 9.9% → 17.6%, and none of it came from mix. - Pricing is rising at all three heavy-duty makers. - The stock is near the bottom of its own post-spin NTM P/E range. - Correction to the brief: the January call will most likely be presented by the outgoing CFO, Ken Parks, not the new CFO. That weakens the "new CFO resets expectations" angle [D04, citing GEV release 2026-08-27 and CFO Dive 2026-08-28].

    Answers 14

    R1

    What does $962.49 require?

    AskedWhat does today's price require (physical and financial terms)?

    Financial terms - Enterprise value is about $247.2B: 962.49 × 266.33M − $9,113M net cash. - That is 25.8x consensus FY27 EBITDA ($9,574M) and 28.2x NTM EBITDA (0.25 × FY26 + 0.75 × FY27 = $8,770M) [computed]. - Price: yfinance quote 2026-09-30 and brief §2. - Share count: 10-Q -26-000148 Note 18. - Consensus: MarketScreener. - It is 38.7x FY27 EPS of $24.85 [MarketScreener]. Barchart has $24.24 (39.7x) and Erste $24.55 [Barchart 2026-08-04; MarketBeat 2026-09-21]. - To hold the current price in 12 months at a lower multiple, the business must deliver roughly consensus. - Sep-2027 NTM EBITDA on consensus is $12,191M. At 20x that gives $950, which is flat. - So the price needs consensus FY28 of $13.1B, i.e. a 21.6% margin on $60.5B of revenue, and a multiple of at least ~20x.

    Physical terms - Gas shipments go from 15.3 GW (FY25) to about 20–22 GW in 2027 and 24 GW in 2028. - Sources: 10-K -26-000015 GW table; Q2'26 call ("at least 30 GW" over Q3'26–Q4'27); Laguna write-up, MarketBeat src:681 (5 → 6 GW a quarter in H2'27). - Power margin has to be about 21.5–23.5% in FY27 for consensus to hold [D01, computed from consensus and the FY26 guide].     3. Competitors are capacity-constrained. Siemens Energy is "sold-out until FY28"; MHI's backlog has grown to 35 GW [SE CFO deck src:3179; Utility Dive src:1743].
    4. The mechanics favour the long. - The NTM roll is +39%. On consensus, 22x in Sep-2027 gives $1,041 (+8%). - The NTM P/E of ~46.9x is below the post-spin median of 50.9x [Chartloom, not point-in-time [SINGLE-SOURCE]].
    5. Electrification is the cleanest growth line. Organic growth +29%; equipment RPO +69% year on year [10-Q -26-000148; Q2'26 call].

    Weakness: all of this is consistent with consensus. The long has no variant view and needs the Street to be right where it already sits above management.

    R7

    Strongest short argument

    AskedWhat is the strongest short argument, with its best evidence?

    1. Consensus FY27 is 9–11% above the straight path to management's own 2028 plan, and FY28 is 16.6% above the plan itself. The CEO's timing puts the next step in equipment margin in 2029–30.
    2. GEV has never delivered a margin above its guide midpoint. Consensus H2'26 (16.3%) is already above the midpoint path (15.0%).
    3. There is a dated event with no cushion. - The January FY27 guide arrives with no December framework raise beforehand (no December 2026 event is listed). - GEV guides margin in whole-number ranges, so it needs a range with an 18%+ low end just to match consensus [D04, citing 8-K releases].
    4. Cash is funded by deposits. - Operating cash flow excluding the contract-liability inflow was −$3.0B in H1'26 [10-Q -26-000148]. - Consensus FY27 FCF falls 38% [MarketScreener [SINGLE-SOURCE]].
    5. The multiple is fragile. - Five closing drawdowns of 15%+ since the spin, median −24.6%. - DeepSeek day was −21.5% [facts BX-03..08; Yahoo/Nasdaq closes]. - Hedge-fund holders fell from 118 to 106 in Q2'26 [Insider Monkey 2026-09-18 [SINGLE-SOURCE]].

    Weakness: a 5–10% estimate gap does not become a price drop unless the multiple also compresses. GLJ's own drop was 106% recovered within about 11 sessions.

    R8

    Which side has the better evidence?

    AskedWhich side's evidence is higher quality (primary, independent, recent), and why?

    The short, on evidence quality. - Its core inputs are management's own primary documents: the 2028 framework, the guide format and the CEO's timing quote. They are recent (Jan–Sep 2026) and can be checked. - The long rests on consensus, which is a single vendor for EBITDA. Its independent pricing evidence (LG&E/KU, Siemens Energy) supports the direction, not the size, of margin gains in 2027.

    The long, on mechanics. The roll-forward, momentum, the never-cut record, and positive reactions on 4 of 4 guide days all favour it.

    Net: the short has better evidence and worse mechanics. That is why I size it small and keep it short in time.

    R9

    AskedWhat dated event inside 12 months reveals the answer, and what is the pass mark?

    Primary: the Q4'26 call, late January 2027, which gives the FY27 outlook. - Short pass mark: FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guide midpoint at or below 17.5% (at least ~$340M below consensus), with no raise to the 2028 framework. - Long pass mark: a guide low end of at least 18%, or the framework raised to at least 21%. - D04's research-judgement probabilities: P(midpoint ≤17.5%) about 66%; P(below 18.15%) about 85%. - CT-39 confirms the event: "We'll also provide you a '27 financial outlook in our January earnings call" (Laguna).

    Secondary: Q3'26 results on 2026-10-28. Consensus Q3 EBITDA is $1,706M, at the top of the range the guide implies. A FY26 margin guide still at 12–14% after Q3 would support the short.

    The best historical analog

    AskedWhat historical analog fits best (gas-turbine cycles, capex-boom suppliers), and what does it say?

    • 1999–2002 US gas-turbine bubble.
    • GE shipped more than 60 GW in 2001 [src:296 web].
    • In July 2002, GE Power Systems said U.S. orders and shipments would "decline by 80 percent or more over the next two years" [GE press release 2002-07-23].
    • Power Systems operating profit went from about $6.2B (2002E) to $3.8–3.9B (2003F) [GE Dec-2002 investor deck].
    • Earnings peaked in 2002, after orders had already fallen, because the backlog carried them [GE 10-K exhibit, SEC 000079746304000012 ex99b: 2002 +29%, then the 2003 decline].
    • What it says for GEV:
    • Backlog protects earnings over 3–12 months, and the stock turns on orders or the multiple.
    • GEV's orders and SRAs are still rising (target at least 125 GW; 12 GW added for 2030–31, per the Q2'26 release and src:681). So the cycle-bust version of the short has no in-horizon trigger.
    • The analog supports only the smaller "estimates too high on timing" version.

    The second is Street behaviour after a light guide. GEV's revenue guides usually beat, so an EBITDA-dollar miss is less likely than a margin miss.

    Bottom line

    The outside view on its own leans slightly long, not short. Two effects pull against each other: - Expensive stocks do badly over 5 years. - But for expensive stocks that have been rising (winners), the value signal is weakest and momentum is strongest over the next 6–12 months [S1: Asness, "The Interaction of Value and Momentum Strategies", FAJ 1997, AQR PDF p.1] [S2: Siegel/Schwartz via WisdomTree, 2023-08-31: the "highest multiple stocks often see momentum enabling them to outperform for the following year"]. - GEV fits that profile: up about 50% over 12 months and down about 14% in the month before 2026-09-20 [S1: Yahoo Finance 2026-09-20] [S2: 52-week range $530.16–$1,195.94, master brief §2; the price sits 82% above the low, computed]. - Sell-side forecasts two or more years out are biased upward. McKinsey found analysts forecast 10–12% a year of profit growth against 6% actual [S1: McKinsey, "Equity analysts: Still too bullish", 2010-04] [S2: City AM, 2010-04-25]. This base rate supports the claim that Street FY27–28 runs ahead of management. - GEV-specific evidence moves the ~52% outside-view prior to p_long ≈ 0.47. That is a coin flip leaning slightly short, and weaker than the brief's 55–60% short lean. - The biggest negative is Street FY28 EBITDA $13,064M against management's $11,200M framework (+16.6%) [S1: MS] [S2: PR4Q]. - The biggest positive is a record of never cutting, with organic framework raises at events. The spring-2027 Capital Markets Day (CMD) falls inside the horizon [S1: FACTS BR-28] [S2: Dec-2024 and Dec-2025 investor-update PDFs]. - The gas-turbine bust analogs (2001–03, 2017–18) do not fit a 3–12-month short. In both, earnings or guidance broke after demand or orders turned. - In 2002, GE Power Systems' earnings rose 29% while US orders were forecast to fall 80% or more [S1: GE 10-K 2003, ex13 MD&A] [S2: GE Power Systems release, 2002-07-23]. - GEV shows no sign of orders turning. The CEO said 2032 slots are selling [S1: FACTS GLJ-35, Laguna transcript] [S2: MarketBeat 2026-09-18, corpus src:681]. - Research estimate of the gap: FY27 adjusted EBITDA about $8.9B (range $8.0–9.7B) vs consensus $9,574M, i.e. −7% or about −1.3 margin points (16.9% vs 18.15%) [computed; D01 base $8.7B; D04 straight-line 16.5–16.9%]. - On today's EV the gap is worth about −7%. The +39% forward roll of next-twelve-month (NTM) EBITDA means a 12-month short also needs the multiple to fall below about 23x on this path (computed, §4). - Correction to the brief: Ken Parks, not the new CFO, presents the January 2027 call [S1: GEV release 2026-08-27] [S2: MarketScreener 2026-08-28].     What would change this

    FY27 guide midpoint ≥18%, or 2028 plan raised to ≥$12.5B → the short's estimate leg is dead; the lean flips to long. - Q3 (2026-10-28) shows contracted GW growth stalling below the 125 GW path, or SRA conversions falling → strengthens the long-failure chain; the 12-month lean moves to short. - Street FY27 drifts down to ≤$9.0B before January → the surprise is already priced and the short's catalyst weakens. - Another AI-capex shock with peers down ≥15% → de-rating risk dominates; a long fails regardless of estimates.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. January presenter. It is Parks's team, not a new CFO (row 12). The "new-CFO reset" is weaker.
    2. "Never beaten its first margin guide." The first guides were qualitative and were met. The numeric-midpoint misses were ~$40–61M (D03). The pattern holds but is small.
    3. GLJ's Power 18.5% for FY27 is at or below the current run-rate (Q2'26 at 18.82%). GLJ is too bearish on Power level, not only "right about when".
    4. "At management's plan the stock is about fairly priced." The brief's $10,794M NTM uses consensus FY27. On a straight-line FY27 the breakeven is 22.8x NTM (A6).
    5. Lean. I rate it closer to a coin flip. The short is favoured only on a ≤4-month horizon through the January guide; at 12 months there is a slight long edge (P ≈ 0.55–0.57 above entry).

    GEV: long or short from $962.49 over 3–12 months — research ladder R1–R14 (no web layer)

    What we asked

    Core question. Over the next 3-12 months from $962.49 (2026-09-29 close), is GE Vernova (GEV) more likely to work as a LONG or as a SHORT?

    This variation. Do NOT use any web search tool (neither exa_search, exa_read_page nor the generic web search). Use only the filing corpus, the research files, and FinRobot's market-data and valuation tools. Your second citation must therefore come from a second filing, transcript or data tool. This tests how much the web layer changes the answer. Answer the core question. Do not read other V0x outputs.

    The ladder (R1–R14).

    • R1. What does today's price require (physical and financial terms)?
    • R2. What does consensus assume for FY27 and FY28, and how does that compare with management's own plan?
    • R3. What has GEV actually delivered versus its own guidance since the spin — on revenue, margin and cash?
    • R4. Where does the evidence most clearly differ from consensus: which line, which year, by how much?

    • R11. What would the market pay for GEV a year from now under each estimate path?
    • R12. What historical analog fits best (gas-turbine cycles, capex-boom suppliers), and what does it say?
    • R13. What single observation would flip your view?
    • R14. How confident are you, and what drives the uncertainty most?

    Bottom line

    The lean is a modest short, and it only holds if the horizon ends at the late-January 2027 FY27 outlook. p_long = 0.45. Over a full 12 months, the spring-2027 Capital Markets Day and the ~+39% NTM EBITDA roll-forward push the answer toward neutral or long. - New arithmetic this run: consensus FY27 needs Power + Electrification together at about 21.4–22.8% segment EBITDA margin in 2027. Management's 2028 target is 22% for each segment, so the Street needs that level a year early. H1'26 actual was 17.85% [10Q segment note; PR2Q six-month segment table]. - That required step is about the size of FY26's step. It is roughly +3.6 pts year on year, against about +3.8 pts FY25 → FY26 guide midpoint [PR4Q; PR2Q guidance]. So the Street is not assuming anything unprecedented. It is assuming no slowdown, while a straight line to management's 2028 plan implies about +1.75 pts a year. - A straight line to management's plan puts FY27 adj EBITDA at about $8.4–8.9B, 7–12% below MarketScreener's $9,574M. GLJ's $7,420M is 22.5% below [GuruFocus via corpus src:679; MarketScreener per market_briefing_0923]. - Timing statements from management lean GLJ's way. The CEO said most higher-margin '24–'25 orders deliver "'27 and beyond" [Q4'25 remarks, corpus src:2660; Latitude-type web reprint src:149]. He also said the 2026 backlog-margin change "tells you the equipment margins for '29 and '30" [Laguna transcript PDF p.10 — SINGLE-SOURCE in this run; the corpus news items src:681/src:1747 confirm the event, not the quote]. - The dated test is the January 2027 call: FY27 outlook, first under the new CFO. Pass mark for a short: an FY27 margin-guide midpoint below ~17.5% (≈$9.2B on consensus revenue). Q3 (2026-10-28) falls after the finals [8-K 0001996810-26-000153 (CFO); news src:681 (Jan outlook/CMD)].

    R1

    What $962.49 requires.

    • P/E is 38.3x on forward EPS $25.13 [YF]; 38.7x on $24.85 [MarketScreener].
    • In physical terms the price needs:

    Variation experiment — what is robust and what is framing

    GEV robustness audit: the nine V0x variants (V01–V09), as of 2026-09-30

    What we asked

    Read every output whose name starts with V0 (list_overnight_outputs, read_overnight_output; read each fully, including its FINAL_BLOCK). Then: 1. Tabulate every FINAL_BLOCK: direction, p_long, FY27 EBITDA low/base/high, FY28 base, target range, confidence, top reason. 2. Measure: (a) noise — V01 vs V02 (identical prompts); (b) anchoring — V03 (told long) vs V04 (told short): how far p_long and FY27 EBITDA moved; (c) brief effect — V05 (cold start) vs V01/V02: does our prior research pull the answer, and which way; (d) persona effect — V06; (e) base-rate effect — V07; (f) pre-mortem effect — V08; (g) web effect — V09 vs V01/V02. 3. Compare the ladder answers R1-R14 across variants: which rungs got the same answer everywhere, and which rungs changed with framing? Which citations recur across independent variants (strong) and which appear once (weak)? 4. Conclude: which conclusions are ROBUST (hold across framings, beyond noise) and which are FRAMING-DRIVEN. Give the median and range of p_long and of FY27 EBITDA across all variants, and say whether the direction call is robust. If anchoring moved the answer by more than the noise band, say so plainly: it means the evidence does not settle the question. No memo prose. Tables first.

    Source key: what the short names in the citations mean

    Research input only. The team writes every memo sentence and picks every forecast number. I read all nine V0x outputs in full, including each FINAL_BLOCK. I checked one point of disagreement between variants against primary sources (the CFO on the January call).

    A caveat on independence. All nine runs used the same model and the same corpus. Seven of them also read tonight's D01–D04 outputs. So when a finding recurs across variants, that shows it survives different framings. It does not show independent confirmation. V05 (no brief, no prior research) and V09 (no web) are the least dependent runs, so findings they reach on their own count most.

    Bottom line

    The FY27 EBITDA estimate is robust; the direction call is not. FY27 adj. EBITDA base: median $8,800M, range $8,700–8,900M across all nine, about −8% vs MarketScreener's $9,574M. Direction splits 3 long / 6 short. p_long: median 0.46, range 0.43–0.55. [V01–V09 FINAL_BLOCKs; consensus per MarketScreener, cross-checked against the GLJ-cited $9,450M in V01/V04/V06/V08] - Anchoring moved the answer by more than the noise band. - Noise (V01 vs V02, identical prompts) was 0.03 on p_long. - Anchoring (V03 told long vs V04 told short) was 0.07, and the direction flipped. - FY27 EBITDA did not move with the anchor (Δ$100M). - On the brief's own criterion, the evidence does not settle the direction question. - Horizon explains most of the split in direction. - Every variant with a 4–5-month horizon is short: V04, V06, V07, V08, V09. Median p_long 0.45. - Of the four 12-month horizons, three are long (V01, V02, V03) and one is short (V05). - Where a variant gave a 12-month probability in its body text, the median is about 0.51 (§4). - V08 states the split explicitly: about 0.45 at 4 months, about 0.57 at 12 months. - Framing mostly worked by pushing the model toward a shorter horizon. - Every short target embeds a de-rating. The short targets (V06–V09) put about 24–26x on FY27 in a January-2027 frame, against 28.2x NTM today. - At a constant 28.2x on the research path, January value is about $991 (V04 A3). - About $100–110 per share of each short target comes from the assumed multiple cut, not from the estimate gap (A4). - One brief premise is technically true but misleading. The "first FY27 guide under the new CFO" framing: - McDonough becomes CFO on 2027-01-01 [8-K 0001996810-26-000153, Item 5.02]. - But GEV's own release says Parks stays through "the third and fourth quarter earnings calls and the publishing of the 2026 10-K" [gevernova.com CFO-transition release, 2026-08-27; eletric-vehicles.com 2026-08-27; CFO Dive 2026-08-28 via D04]. - The two variants without that web evidence (V05, V09) kept the "new CFO" angle. The other seven dropped it. - The research's own confidence never moved. All nine rate confidence 2/5. Eight of nine name the multiple, not EBITDA, as the biggest uncertainty (V09 names management behaviour).

    Q4

    Robust vs framing-driven

    ROBUST. These held across all nine framings and beyond noise: 1. FY27 adj. EBITDA base ≈ $8.7–8.9B, about −7% to −9% vs consensus. 2. Street FY28 is +16.6% above management's $11.2B plan. 3. The margin record: revenue and cash beat; margin lands inside the range, below the midpoint. 4. The gap is interpretation/timing, not information. 5. The late-January FY27 guide is the reveal, and a low end ≥18% kills the short. 6. The price mechanism dominates the estimate gap. A 12-month short needs a de-rating to about 20–23x NTM. 7. The gas-turbine bust analogs do not support an in-horizon bust. 8. Confidence is 2/5.

    FRAMING-DRIVEN: 1. Direction. p_long median 0.46, range 0.43–0.55. The anchoring swing (0.07) is more than twice the noise swing (0.03). 2. Horizon choice. It fully sorts direction among the brief-fed runs. 3. Target ranges. Short targets depend on an unstated de-rating; long targets on a ~23x hold. 4. FY28 base ($10.8–12.0B). 5. The short pass mark in January (16.5–17.5%). 6. The CFO-presenter angle. It depends on whether the variant saw the 2026-08-27 release.

    Is the direction call robust? No. It is robust only when conditioned on horizon: - At 4–5 months (through the January guide), 5/5 variants lean short at about 0.45. - At 12 months, the framings split, and the median is about 0.51.

    Disagreements with the master brief
    1. The research lean is horizon-specific, not a clean 55–60% short. - Across nine framings: median p_long 0.46, about 54% short. - That holds only for a 4–5-month window. At 12 months the median is about 0.51. - The brief's §8 lean survives only if the team's horizon ends at the January guide.
    2. "First under the new CFO" is misleading. - The title changes 2027-01-01 [8-K -26-000153]. - But Parks presents the Q4 call and signs off the 10-K [GEV release 2026-08-27; CFO Dive 2026-08-28].
    3. The §7 "management plan" NTM of $10,794M uses consensus FY27. On a plan-consistent FY27 it is $10,548–10,625M (V02, V06, V08).
    4. The §8 short range (−9% to −14% at 25x) values on FY27 without the four-month roll. - At a constant 28.2x NTM the January value is about $991 on the research path. - So the short needs an explicit de-rating assumption (A4; V04 §7).
    5. The FY26 margin guide was raised once (11–13% → 12–14%) (V04, V05). The "never beat the first margin guide" claim still holds for FY24 and FY25.

    Question banks

    The questions every task carried

    Every deep task got the general bank as a checklist. Every variation answered the core ladder.

    G

    General question bank (G1–G25)

    • G1. What does $962.49 require the business to deliver — in physical terms (GW, $/kW, margin) and by when?
    • G2. What does consensus assume about margins, and has GEV ever delivered that pace before?
    • G3. Who is the marginal buyer of GEV today, why do they own it, and what would make them sell?
    • G4. What is the market's story in one sentence, and which single number would falsify it?
    • G5. If the stock went nowhere for 12 months, what would have happened to estimates and the multiple?
    • G6. Where exactly — which line, which year, by how much — does the evidence differ from consensus?
    • G7. Why hasn't the market seen it: is it information, interpretation, or timing?
    • G8. Is the gap big enough to matter after the multiple (estimate gap vs price move)?
    • G9. What would the smartest person on the other side say, and what evidence answers them?
    • G10. What is the causal chain from the variant to the share price, step by step — and which step is weakest?
    • G11. What do the physics and engineering constrain: lead times, factory capacity, slot economics, outages?
    • G12. What does the accounting do to WHEN results show up: percentage of completion, RPO conversion, deposits?
    • G13. Which dated, company-reported event inside 12 months reveals the truth, and what is the pass mark?
    • G14. What could push the reveal beyond the horizon?
    • G15. If this is wrong, how wrong and how fast? What does the stock's own drawdown history say?
    • G16. Which risk is being dismissed as noise that could dominate over 3-12 months?
    • G17. What does management control (buybacks, M&A, guidance style, disclosure) that could break it?
    • G18. What is the kill rule — a number and a date?
    • G19. When has this happened before — to GE's own gas-turbine business (the 1999-2002 US gas-turbine boom and bust; the 2017-2019 GE Power collapse), to other "bottleneck supplier" stocks in capex booms — and what came next?
    • G20. Which numbers rest on one source, and which are definition traps?
    • G21. What would we expect to see if we were wrong — and has anyone looked for it?
    • G22. What in guidance or consensus has to change, and when?
    • G23. Why is the upside/downside larger than the estimate gap?
    • G24. How are SBC, deposits and cash conversion treated?
    • G25. What did you verify by hand, and what came from tools or AI?
    R

    Core ladder for the variations (R1–R14)

    Core questionOver the next 3-12 months from $962.49 (2026-09-29 close), is GE Vernova (GEV) more likely to work as a LONG or as a SHORT?

    • R1. What does today's price require (physical and financial terms)?
    • R2. What does consensus assume for FY27 and FY28, and how does that compare with management's own plan?
    • R3. What has GEV actually delivered versus its own guidance since the spin — on revenue, margin and cash?
    • R4. Where does the evidence most clearly differ from consensus: which line, which year, by how much?
    • R5. Why would the market not already know this?
    • R6. What is the strongest long argument, with its best evidence?
    • R7. What is the strongest short argument, with its best evidence?
    • R8. Which side's evidence is higher quality (primary, independent, recent), and why?
    • R9. What dated event inside 12 months reveals the answer, and what is the pass mark?
    • R10. If you are wrong, how much can you lose, judged by the stock's own history?
    • R11. What would the market pay for GEV a year from now under each estimate path?
    • R12. What historical analog fits best (gas-turbine cycles, capex-boom suppliers), and what does it say?
    • R13. What single observation would flip your view?
    • R14. How confident are you, and what drives the uncertainty most?
